ITQAN:v2p566/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p566/r13.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p566/r13.claim: قنوان is the plural of قنو.
ITQAN:v2p566/r13.anchor: قنوان جمع قنو وصنوان جمع صنو

ITQAN:v2p566/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p566/r15.speaker: ابن خالويه
ITQAN:v2p566/r15.claim: Ibn Khalawayh says only قنوان and صنوان share the same form for plural and dual, with one further non-Qur'anic form.
ITQAN:v2p566/r15.anchor: وليس في اللغة جمع ومثنى بصيغة واحدة إلا هذان ولفظ ثالث لم يقع في القرآن قاله ابن خالويه في كتاب ليس

STUDYQURAN:6:intro/r17.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:intro/r17.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:intro/r17.claim: Verses 95–99 discuss God as giver of life and death in this world and the next.
STUDYQURAN:6:intro/r17.anchor: Vv. 95–99 discuss God as the giver of both life and death, in this world and the next

IBNMUJAHID:v1p262/r9.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p262/r9.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p262/r9.claim: Mujahid notes a difference in opening or ḍamma on the thāʾ and mīm in ثمره and related forms, but this excerpt gives no reader assignments.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p262/r9.anchor: واختلفوا فى فتح الثاء والميم وضمهما من قوله ﴿ انظروا إلى ثمره ﴾ 99 و ﴿ من ثمرة ﴾ الأنعام 141

SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكأنتقولعلىقولالسائلكمصيدعل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكأنتقولعلىقولالسائلكمصيدعل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكأنتقولعلىقولالسائلكمصيدعل.claim: In answers like صيد عليه يومان, the days mean that hunting occurred over two days; the preposition is understood through concise, expanded usage.

SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكأنتقولعلىقولالسائلكمصيدعل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكأنتقولعلىقولالسائلكمصيدعل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكأنتقولعلىقولالسائلكمصيدعل.claim: كم in these questions is not itself a temporal adverb: the answer gives the time span, as with offspring born over sixty years or travel over days.
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكأنتقولعلىقولالسائلكمصيدعل.anchor: فليس كم ظرفا كما أن ما ليس بظرف

SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكأنتقولعلىقولالسائلكمصيدعل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكأنتقولعلىقولالسائلكمصيدعل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكأنتقولعلىقولالسائلكمصيدعل.claim: The question كم ضرب به can be answered with a dual or mass noun for the blows, another concise use of the same question pattern.
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكأنتقولعلىقولالسائلكمصيدعل.anchor: ضرب به ضربتان وضرب به ضرب كثير

SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكأنتقولعلىقولالسائلكمصيدعل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكأنتقولعلىقولالسائلكمصيدعل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكأنتقولعلىقولالسائلكمصيدعل.claim: Idioms such as the road treading a people omit أهل, while catching Qanawayn omits a preposition or the game associated with that place.

SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكأنتقولعلىقولالسائلكمصيدعل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكأنتقولعلىقولالسائلكمصيدعل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكأنتقولعلىقولالسائلكمصيدعل.claim: Comparisons with أن clauses refer to the person who performs the action, not the action itself, because أن is a noun with its clause as complement.
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكأنتقولعلىقولالسائلكمصيدعل.anchor: أنت أكرم على من صاحب الضرب

SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكأنتقولعلىقولالسائلكمصيدعل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكأنتقولعلىقولالسائلكمصيدعل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكأنتقولعلىقولالسائلكمصيدعل.claim: Sībawayh says al-Jaʿdī uses عذير for a sound or cry; the lines illustrate compressed expressions with a place phrase.

SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكأنتقولعلىقولالسائلكمصيدعل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكأنتقولعلىقولالسائلكمصيدعل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكأنتقولعلىقولالسائلكمصيدعل.claim: ʿĀmir ibn al-Ṭufayl's line omits bi before place names and connects the verb directly to them.

SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكأنتقولعلىقولالسائلكمصيدعل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكأنتقولعلىقولالسائلكمصيدعل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكأنتقولعلىقولالسائلكمصيدعل.claim: Sāʿidah's line means the fox moved in the road; the preposition في is omitted in the poetic wording.

SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكأنتقولعلىقولالسائلكمصيدعل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكأنتقولعلىقولالسائلكمصيدعل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكأنتقولعلىقولالسائلكمصيدعل.claim: Eating a land or town means obtaining and consuming its good things, not literally eating the place.
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكأنتقولعلىقولالسائلكمصيدعل.anchor: أكلت أرض كذا وكذا وأكلت بلدة

SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكأنتقولعلىقولالسائلكمصيدعل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكأنتقولعلىقولالسائلكمصيدعل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكأنتقولعلىقولالسائلكمصيدعل.claim: Names such as ظهر, عصر, and مغرب can mean the prayer of that time, while اجتماع القيظ means people gathered during the hot season.
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكأنتقولعلىقولالسائلكمصيدعل.anchor: هذه الظهر أو العصر أو المغرب إنما يريد

SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكأنتقولعلىقولالسائلكمصيدعل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكأنتقولعلىقولالسائلكمصيدعل.speaker: الحطيئة
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكأنتقولعلىقولالسائلكمصيدعل.claim: Al-Ḥuṭayʾah's المنايا phrase means the death of a dead man; the noun is understood as منية ميت.
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكأنتقولعلىقولالسائلكمصيدعل.anchor: وقال الحطيئة # % وشر المنايا ميت بين أهله

SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكأنتقولعلىقولالسائلكمصيدعل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكأنتقولعلىقولالسائلكمصيدعل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكأنتقولعلىقولالسائلكمصيدعل.claim: Al-Nābighah al-Jaʿdī's comparison means like the relationship or affection of Abū Marḥab, with the relational noun understood.
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكأنتقولعلىقولالسائلكمصيدعل.anchor: وقال النابغة الجعدى # % وكيف تواصل من أصبحت

SAMIN-DURR:6:99/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99/r1.claim: فأخرجنا shifts from third-person reference to the first-person plural of majesty.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99/r1.anchor: فيه التفات من غيبة إلى تكلم بنون العظمة

SAMIN-DURR:6:99/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99/r2.claim: The باء in به expresses causation.

SAMIN-DURR:6:99/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99/r3.claim: One interpretation takes نبات كل شيء to mean everything linguistically called a plant.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99/r3.anchor: قيل: المراد كل ما تسمى نباتا في اللغة

SAMIN-DURR:6:99/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99/r4.speaker: الفراء
SAMIN-DURR:6:99/r4.claim: Al-Farra interprets the phrase as the provision or food suitable to nourish each thing, restricting it to what feeds.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99/r4.anchor: وقال الفراء: " رزق كل شيء أي: ما يصلح أن يكون غذاء لكل شيء فيكون مخصوصا بالمتغذى به "

SAMIN-DURR:6:99/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99/r5.speaker: الطبري
SAMIN-DURR:6:99/r5.claim: Al-Tabari includes all growing things among animals, plants, and minerals, since all are nourished by water.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99/r5.anchor: وقال الطبري: " هو جميع ما ينمو من الحيوان والنبات والمعادن؛ لأن كل ذلك يتغذى بالماء "

SAMIN-DURR:6:99/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99/r6.claim: On the non-Farra interpretation, the annexation resembles an adjective and described noun: نبات means المنبت, not a verbal noun as in 71:17.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99/r6.anchor: إذ يصير المعنى على ذلك: فأخرجنا به كل شيء منبت فإن النبات بمعنى المنبت

SAMIN-DURR:6:99/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99/r7.claim: On al-Farra’s food/provision reading, the annexation joins distinct things: the food or provision of every thing.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99/r7.anchor: كانت الإضافة إضافة بين متباينين، إذ يصير المعنى: غذاء كل شيء أو رزقه

SAMIN-DURR:6:99/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99/r8.speaker: الفراء
SAMIN-DURR:6:99/r8.claim: Al-Farra also allows نبات to be annexed to كل شيء while intending كل شيء as نبات, like حق اليقين; al-Samin notes this additional view was omitted by the Shaykh.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99/r8.anchor: وقد يجوز في العربية أن تضيف النبات إلى كل شيء، وأنت تريد بكل شيء النبات أيضا

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#2/r1.claim: The apparent antecedent of منه is نبات; Zamakhshari gives only this option. من then marks part or point of origin.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#2/r1.anchor: أن تعود على النبات وهذا هو الظاهر ولم يذكر الزمخشري غيره

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#2/r2.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#2/r2.claim: Abu al-Baqa also allows منه to refer to ماء, with من expressing cause.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#2/r2.anchor: وأخرجنا منه أي: بسببه. ويجوز أن تكون الهاء

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#2/r3.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#2/r3.claim: If منه refers to water, Abu al-Baqa treats the second فأخرجنا clause as a semantic replacement; al-Samin says strict grammatical بدل is not evident and prefers coordination.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#2/r3.anchor: وعلى الأول يكون " فأخرجنا " بدلا من " أخرجنا " الأول

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#2/r4.claim: Al-Samin corrects the Shaykh: Abu al-Baqa’s بدل analysis depends on منه referring to water and cannot be attributed to the plant reading.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#2/r4.anchor: قلت: إنما جعله بدلا بناء على عود الضمير في " منه " على الماء

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#2/r5.speaker: أبو إسحاق
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#2/r5.claim: Abu Ishaq says خضر and أخضر both mean green, like عور and أعور.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#2/r5.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق " يقال اخضر يخضر فهو خضر وأخضر كاعور فهو عور وأعور "

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#2/r6.claim: Green lies between white and black but closer to black; thus black can denote green and vice versa, as in سواد العراق for its tree-covered greenness.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#2/r6.anchor: والخضرة أحد الألوان وهي بين البياض والسواد لكنها إلى السواد أقرب

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#2/r7.claim: مدهامتان in 55:64 means intensely black because of the gardens’ abundant moisture and greenness.

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#2/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#2/r8.claim: المخاضرة is selling green fruit before ripening; الخضيرة is a palm whose unripe dates fall while green.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#2/r8.anchor: والمخاضرة: مبايعة الخضر والثمار قبل بلوغها، والخضيرة نخلة ينتثر بسرها أخضر

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#2/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#2/r9.speaker: النبي
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#2/r9.claim: The Prophet explains خضراء الدمن as a beautiful woman from a bad upbringing; الدمن are refuse heaps where attractive plants may grow.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#2/r9.anchor: فقد فسره هو عليه السلام بقوله: " المرأة الحسناء في المنبت السوء "

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#3/r1.speaker: الجمهور وابن محيصن والأعمش
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#3/r1.claim: The majority read نخرج active in first-person plural; Ibn Muhaysin and al-Aʿmash read passive يخرج, with حب as its agent.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#3/r1.anchor: وقرأ ابن محيصن والأعمش " يخرج " بياء الغيبة مبنيا للمفعول، " حب " قائم مقام فاعله

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#3/r2.claim: On either reading, the clause is most naturally an adjective of خضرا, though it may be independent.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#3/r2.anchor: وعلى كلتا القراءتين تكون الجملة صفة ل " خضرا " وهذا هو الظاهر، وجوزوا فيها أن تكون مستأنفة

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#3/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#3/r3.claim: متراكبا can be nominative or accusative as an adjective of حب, following the two case parses.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#3/r3.anchor: ومتراكب رفعا ونصبا صفة ل " حب " بالاعتبارين

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#3/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#3/r4.claim: Best parse: من النخل is a fronted predicate, من طلعها a partitive بدل with repeated preposition, and قنوان a delayed topic; the nominal clause coordinates with the prior verbal clause.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#3/r4.anchor: أحدها: وهو أحسنها أن يكون " من النخل " خبرا مقدما، و " من طلعها " بدل بعض من كل بإعادة العامل

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#3/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#3/r5.claim: On al-Akhfash’s alternative, قنوان is raised as subject by من النخل, with من طلعها as apposition.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#3/r5.anchor: فاعلا بالجار قبله وهو من النخل

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#3/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#3/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#3/r6.claim: A تنازع parse has both prepositional phrases seeking قنوان as subject: Basrans prefer the second governor and insert a pronoun in the first, Kufans the reverse.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#3/r6.anchor: الثالث: أن تكون المسألة من باب التنازع، يعني أن كلا من الجارين يطلب قنوانا

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#3/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#3/r7.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#3/r7.claim: Abu al-Baqa’s other parse makes قنوان the subject governed by من طلعها, with a pronoun in من النخل; al-Samin assigns governance to the second phrase.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#3/r7.anchor: قال أبو البقاء: " والوجه الآخر أن يرتفع " قنوان " على أنه فاعل

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#3/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#3/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#3/r8.claim: A further parse makes قنوان a topic, من طلعها its predicate, and posits an understood شيء or ثمر with من النخل; al-Samin rejects it because the predicate cannot also be بدل.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#3/r8.anchor: وفي " من النخل " ضمير تقديره: ونبت من النخل شيء

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#3/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#3/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#3/r9.claim: If من طلعها is already the predicate, it cannot also be بدل; taking من النخل as predicate repeats the earlier parse.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#3/r9.anchor: بعد أن جعل " من طلعها " الخبر فكيف يجعل بدلا؟

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#4/r1.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#4/r1.claim: The Shaykh calls the preceding grammatical account confused.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#4/r1.anchor: قال الشيخ: " وهذا إعراب فيه تخليط "

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#4/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#4/r2.claim: Zamakhshari makes قنوان a topic with its predicate omitted and inferred from أخرجنا; the Shaykh and al-Samin find this unnecessary because the clause already informs independently.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#4/r2.anchor: هذا نص الزمخشري، وهو كما قال الشيخ لا حاجة إليه

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#4/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#4/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya links من النخل to an omitted verb and makes من طلعها قنوان a nominal clause functioning as the object of نخرج.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#4/r3.anchor: ومن النخل تقديره: " ونخرج من النخل " و " من طلعها قنوان " ابتداء خبره مقدم

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#4/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#4/r4.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#4/r4.claim: A verb taking one object cannot take a whole clause unless it licenses clausal complements and a blocker prevents governance within it; نخرج has neither condition.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#4/r4.anchor: وهذا خطأ لأن ما يتعدى إلى مفعول واحد لا تقع الجملة في موضع مفعوله

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#4/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#4/r5.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#4/r5.claim: If the verb governed a word inside the nominal clause, قنوان would have to be accusative as its object.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#4/r5.anchor: إذ لو سلط الفعل على شيء من مفردات الجملة لكان التركيب " ونخرج من النخل من طلعها قنوانا "

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#4/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#4/r6.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#4/r6.claim: With passive يخرج, the palm clause may coordinate with the passive clause; the Shaykh prefers the alternative topic-predicate parse.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#4/r6.anchor: وقال الشيخ: " ومن قرأ: " يخرج منه حب متراكب " جاز أن يكون قوله

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#4/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#4/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#4/r7.claim: قنوان is the broken plural of قنو, like صنوان from صنو; قنو is a date cluster or stalk, also called كباسة.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#4/r7.anchor: والقنو: العذق بكسر العين وهو عنقود النخلة

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#4/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#4/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#4/r8.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays uses قنو النخلة المتعثكل in a foliage simile and elsewhere uses قنوانا for red dates.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#4/r8.anchor: قال امرؤ القيس: 2015 وفرع يغشي المتن أسود فاحم

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#4/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#4/r9.speaker: أبو علي
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#4/r9.claim: Abu ʿAli says the plural’s kasra replaces rather than preserves the singular kasra of قنو, as in هجان and ظراف.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#4/r9.anchor: قال أبو علي: " الكسرة التي في قنوان ليست التي كانت في قنو لأن تلك حذفت في التكسير

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#4/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#4/r10.speaker: الواحدي
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#4/r10.claim: Al-Wahidi compares the new final ḍamma to the distinction between منصور and the vocative حار in يا حار.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#4/r10.anchor: قال الواحدي: " وهذا مما توضحه الضمة في آخر

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#4/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#4/r11.speaker: الجمهور والأعمش والحباب والأعرج
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#4/r11.claim: The majority use qaf kasra, called Hijazi; al-Aʿmash, al-Habbab from Abu ʿAmr, and al-Aʿraj use ḍamma. Al-Farra assigns it to Qays and says kasra is more common; Ibn ʿAtiyya reverses the Hijazi label.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#4/r11.anchor: فلغة الحجاز " قنوان " بكسر القاف، وهي قراءة الجمهور. وقرأ الأعمش والحباب

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#5/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#5/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#5/r1.claim: A third form, قنوان with qaf fatḥa, is Abu ʿAmr’s reading in Harun’s transmission.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#5/r1.anchor: واللغة الثالثة: قنوان بفتح القاف وهي قراءة أبي عمرو في رواية هارون عنه

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#5/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#5/r2.speaker: ابن جني
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#5/r2.claim: Ibn Jinni parses the fatḥa form as a collective noun, not a plural, since Arabic has no plural pattern فعلان with fatḥa on its first letter.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#5/r2.anchor: وخرجها ابن جني على أنها اسم جمع لقنو لا جمعا إذ ليس في صيغ الجموع ما هو على وزن فعلان بفتح الفاء

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#5/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#5/r3.speaker: الزمخشري وأبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#5/r3.claim: Zamakhshari compares it with ركب, Abu al-Baqa with الباقر; al-Durr prefers الباقر because it is uncontroversially collective while ركب is disputed by Abu al-Hasan.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#5/r3.anchor: ونظره الزمخشري بركب، وأبو البقاء بالباقر، وتنظير أبي البقاء أولى

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#5/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#5/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#5/r4.claim: The fatḥa form’s analysis is supported because the singular is attested with qaf kasra or ḍamma, never fatḥa.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#5/r4.anchor: سمع في المفرد كسر القاف وضمها فجاء الجمع عليهما

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#5/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#5/r5.speaker: تميم وربيعة
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#5/r5.claim: Two further dialectal forms use ya rather than waw: قنيان with qaf ḍamma or kasra; both are Tamim and Rabiʿa forms.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#5/r5.anchor: قنيان بضم القاف مع الياء دون الواو

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#5/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#5/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#5/r6.claim: These dialects retain waw in the singular and never use ya there, so the plural unexpectedly differs from the singular stem.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#5/r6.anchor: وأما المفرد فلا يقولونه بالياء أصلا بل بالواو سواء كسروا القاف أم ضموها

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#5/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#5/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#5/r7.claim: The view that قنو means a palm’s heart or pith is nearly mistaken: the pith is inside the palm, unlike the nearby fruit; the established meaning is a cluster.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#5/r7.anchor: فقيل: هو الجمار وهذا يكاد يكون غلطا، وكيف يوصف بكونه دانيا

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#5/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#5/r8.speaker: أبو عبيد
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#5/r8.claim: Abu ʿUbayd says the dual of قنو is قنوان with kasra on nun and the plural matches it, like صنو/صنوان, an otherwise unmatched form.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#5/r8.anchor: وإذا ثنيت قنوا قلت: قنوان بكسر النون، ثم جاء جمعه على لفظ الاثنين مثل: صنو وصنوان

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#5/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#5/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#5/r9.claim: In pause, dual and plural قنوان are homonyms; in connected speech, case marking distinguishes them.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#5/r9.anchor: إذا وقف على " قنوان " المثنى رفعا وعلى " قنوان " جمعا وقع الاشتراك اللفظي

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#5/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#5/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#5/r10.claim: Other distinctions include dual alif changing to ya in oblique cases and its nun dropping in annexation, while plural nun remains; dual nisba drops its markers but plural قنواني retains them.

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#5/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#5/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#5/r11.claim: Though قنوان and صنوان resemble sound masculine plurals, broken pattern فعلان itself conveys plurality rather than two added markers.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#5/r11.anchor: وأيضا فإن الجمع من قنوان وصنوان، إنما فهمناه من صيغة فعلان لا من الزيادتين

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#6/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#6/r1.speaker: الراغب
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#6/r1.claim: Al-Raghib compares قناة to قنو because both resemble branches; a water channel is explained by its straight extension or as a place that stores water.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#6/r1.anchor: والقناة تشبه القنو في كونهما غصنين، وأما القناة التي يجري فيها الماء

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#6/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#6/r2.speaker: الراغب
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#6/r2.claim: Al-Raghib also derives قناة from قاناه, ‘mixed it’; Imruʾ al-Qays’s مقاناة البياض بصفرة supports mixture.

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#6/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#6/r3.speaker: الراغب
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#6/r3.claim: Nasal قنا, the curvature of a nose, is named by resemblance in shape; a man is أقنى and a woman قنواء.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#6/r3.anchor: وأما " القنا " الذي هو الاحديداب في الأنف

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#6/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#6/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#6/r4.claim: طلع is the first growth to emerge from the palm within its enclosing sheaths.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#6/r4.anchor: والطلع: أول ما يخرج من النخلة في أكمامه

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#6/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#6/r5.speaker: أبو عبيد
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#6/r5.claim: Abu ʿUbayd defines الطلع as the kafara before it splits from agrīḍ, also called طلع; أطلعت النخلة describes the palm producing it while طلع الطلع describes the growth’s emergence.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#6/r5.anchor: قال أبو عبيد: " الطلع: الكفرى قبل أن تنشق عن الإغريض والإغريض يسمى طلعا

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#6/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#6/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#6/r6.claim: An unnamed poem lists palm-fruit stages: طلع, خلال, بلح, بسر, رطب, then تمر.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#6/r6.anchor: طلع وبعده خلال يظهر وبلح ثم يليه بسر ورطب تجنيه ثم تمر

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#6/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#6/r7.speaker: الجمهور
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#6/r7.claim: The majority read جنات accusative, coordinating it with نبات: the water brings forth plants generally and gardens specifically.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#6/r7.anchor: الجمهور على كسر التاء من " جنات " لأنها منصوبة نسقا على نبات

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#6/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#6/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#6/r8.claim: This is a specific-after-general construction honoring these kinds, like naming Gabriel and Michael after the angels and messengers.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#6/r8.anchor: وهو من عطف الخاص على العام تشريفا لهذين الجنسين على غيرهما

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#6/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#6/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#6/r9.claim: On this parse, the palm clause is parenthetical and formed as a topic-predicate sentence to magnify the blessing of dates, a major Arab food combining enjoyment and sustenance.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#6/r9.anchor: وأبرزت في صورة المبتدأ والخبر تعظيما للمنة به

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#6/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#6/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#6/r10.claim: جنات may instead coordinate with خضرا.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#6/r10.anchor: ويجوز أن ينتصب " جنات " نسقا على " خضرا "

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#6/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#6/r11.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#6/r11.claim: Zamakhshari prefers taking accusative جنات as اختصاص, singling out these kinds like والمقيمي الصلاة; al-Samin says his wording implies he treats nominative as famous and accusative as anomalous.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#6/r11.anchor: وجوز الزمخشري - وجعله الأحسن - أن ينتصب على الاختصاص كقوله " والمقيمي الصلاة "

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#7/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#7/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#7/r1.claim: Al-Aʿmash, Muhammad ibn Abi Layla, and Abu Bakr in a report from ʿAsim read وجنات in the nominative.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#7/r1.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش ومحمد بن أبي ليلى وأبو بكر في رواية عنه عن عاصم

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#7/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#7/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#7/r2.claim: As a nominative subject with omitted predicate, al-Zamakhshari supplies ثم, while Abu al-Baqa supplies من الكرم, matching ومن النخل.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#7/r2.anchor: أحدها: أنها مرفوعة بالابتداء، والخبر محذوف. واختلفت عبارة المعربين في تقديره

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#7/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#7/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#7/r3.claim: Al-Nahhas estimates ولهم and Ibn ʿAtiyya ولكم; the omitted-predicate construction also parallels وحور عين, whose understood predicate is لهم, and is accepted by Sibawayh, al-Kisaʾi, and al-Farraʾ.

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#7/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#7/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#7/r4.claim: A delayed omitted predicate can be أخرجناها, inferred from the earlier فأخرجنا; Ibn al-Anbari had already analyzed the phrase this way.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#7/r4.anchor: وقدره متأخرا فقال: أي وجنات من أعناب أخرجناها.

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#7/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#7/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#7/r5.claim: Al-Farazdaq's line raises الخمر although it is the object, understood as والخمر أحلها الطعنة, illustrating delayed coordination with an omitted predicate.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#7/r5.anchor: غداة أحلت لابن أصرم طعنة حصين عبيطات السدائف والخمر

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#7/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#7/r6.speaker: ابن الأنباري
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#7/r6.claim: Ibn al-Anbari also allows coordination on قنوان by proximity: eyes follow brows though they are not plucked, just as grape gardens do not come from palm flowers; the author calls this defense weak and characteristic of adjectival attraction.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#7/r6.anchor: هذا نص مذهب ابن الأنباري أيضا، فتحصل له في الآية مذهبان

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#7/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#7/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#7/r7.claim: Coordination on قنوان is also possible if من النخل does not scope over the gardens: palm clusters and separately produced grape gardens; al-Tabari gives this analysis, Ibn ʿAtiyya weakens it, and Abu al-Baqa objects that grapes do not grow from palms.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#7/r7.anchor: وقد ذكر الطبري أيضا هذا الوجه أعني عطفها على

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#7/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#7/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#7/r8.claim: من أعناب is an adjectival phrase modifying جنات; it is nominative with the nominative reading and accusative with the other reading, and depends on an omitted element.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#7/r8.anchor: صفة لجنات فتكون في محل رفع ونصب بحسب القراءتين، وتتعلق بمحذوف.

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#8/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#8/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#8/r1.claim: All readers have الزيتون and الرمان in the accusative; they may coordinate with جنات or with نبات, as al-Zamakhshari and Abu al-Baqa explain.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#8/r1.anchor: قوله: { والزيتون والرمان } لم يقرأهما أحد إلا منصوبين

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#8/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#8/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#8/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya instead coordinates these two nouns with حبا; a later conjunct may attach either to the immediately preceding item or to the first item in the series.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#8/r2.anchor: وقد تقدم لك أن في المعطوف الثالث فصاعدا احتمالين

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#8/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#8/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#8/r3.claim: زيتون follows the pattern فيعول, with ت extra and ن original, supported by زتنة for land rich in olives and by the pattern قيصوم; فعلول is absent or rare.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#8/r3.anchor: قالوا: أرض زتنة أي كثيرة الزيتون

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#8/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#8/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#8/r4.claim: زيت and زيتون are distinct roots despite oil being extracted from olives; زات الطعام means adding oil, زات الرأس means anointing it, and ازدات reflects ت changing to د after ز.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#8/r4.anchor: فإنهما مادتان متغايرتان، وإن كان الزيت معتصرا منه، ويقال: زات طعامه

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#8/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#8/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#8/r5.claim: رمان has the pattern فعال with original ن, like عناب and حماض; رمنة describes land rich in pomegranates.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#8/r5.anchor: والرمان وزنه فعال نونه أصلية فهو نظير عناب وحماض

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#9/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#9/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#9/r1.claim: مشتبها is a circumstantial accusative most naturally referring to the nearer الرمان, with an omitted matching state for الزيتون; resemblance concerns color and difference concerns taste.

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#9/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#9/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#9/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari instead applies both states to both olives and pomegranates, with omitted repeated predicates; he compares the ellipsis with 9:62 and a poetic line.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#9/r2.anchor: وإلى هذا نحا الزمخشري فإنه قال:

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#9/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#9/r3.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#9/r3.claim: The cited poem does not prove omitted predicates: بريئا can predicate of singular, dual, or plural, and can be shared by the pronoun and its conjunct; as two circumstantial states it would need dual agreement.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#9/r3.anchor: قال الشيخ: " فعلى قوله يكون تقدير البيت: كنت منه بريئا

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#9/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#9/r4.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#9/r4.claim: Abu al-Baqa says the state applies to the pomegranate and to all the fruits; that is semantically sound if ellipsis is understood, but not as literal syntactic agreement.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#9/r4.anchor: قال أبو البقاء: " حال من الرمان ومن الجميع "

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#9/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#9/r5.speaker: الجمهور
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#9/r5.claim: The majority read singular مشتبها; an anomalous reading has متشابها وغير متشابه, with the same sense, since افتعال and تفاعل often share meanings.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#9/r5.anchor: والجمهور على " مشتبها " وقرئ شاذا متشابها

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r1.claim: إلى ثمره depends on انظروا, which means to look with reflection; إلى is used because this sense includes contemplation.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r1.anchor: وهي بمعنى الرؤية، وإنما تعدت ب إلى لما تتضمنه من التفكر.

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r2.speaker: الأخوان، author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r2.claim: The Brothers' double-ḍamma reading ثمر admits four analyses: a singular noun, a plural of plurals, a plural of ثمر, or a plural of ثمرة.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r2.anchor: الباقون: بفتحتين، وقرئ شاذا بضم الأول وسكون الثاني.

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r3.claim: One analysis treats ثمر as a singular noun, like طنب or عنق.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r3.anchor: أحدها: أن تكون اسما مفردا كطنب وعنق.

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r4.claim: Another analysis makes ثمر a plural of plurals: ثمر is plural of ثمار, itself plural of ثمرة, comparable to أكم and إكام.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r4.anchor: أنه جمع الجمع فثمر جمع ثمار وثمار جمع ثمرة

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r5.claim: A third analysis treats ثمر as a plural of ثمر, by analogy with the two plural forms أسد and أسد.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r5.anchor: والثالث: أنه جمع ثمر كما قالوا: أسد وأسد.

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r6.speaker: الفارسي
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r6.claim: Al-Farisi prefers reading ثمر as the plural of ثمرة, like خشبة/خشب, أكمة/أكم, and the defective pairs لابة/لوب, ناقة/نوق, ساحة/سوح.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r6.anchor: قال الفارسي: " والأحسن أن يكون جمع ثمرة كخشبة وخشب

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r7.claim: The majority's fatḥ reading الثمر is a collective noun whose singular is ثمرة, like شجر/شجرة, بقر/بقرة, and جزر/جزرة.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r7.anchor: وأما قراءة الجماعة فالثمر اسم جنس مفرده ثمرة كشجر وشجرة

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r8.claim: The rare reading with a still second radical either eases the double-ḍamma reading or is a plural of ثمرة; with the latter analysis, ثمر parallels سمر and its broken plural is أثمار.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r8.anchor: وأما قراءة التسكين فهي تخفيف قراءة الأخوين، وقيل: بل هي جمع ثمرة

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r9.speaker: أبو عمرو
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r9.claim: Abu ʿAmr reads the Kahf occurrence with ḍamma and a still م; that is eloquent, though consistency would suggest using it here too, since recitation follows transmission.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r9.anchor: وقد قرأ أبو عمرو الذي في سورة الكهف بالضم وسكون الميم

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r10.claim: In al-Anʿām and Yāsīn, ʿĀsim, Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathir, Ibn ʿAmir, and Abu ʿAmr read fatḥ; in al-Kahf, ʿĀsim reads fatḥ, the Brothers and Nāfiʿ/Ibn Kathir/Ibn ʿAmir double ḍamma, and Abu ʿAmr ḍamma with sukūn.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r10.anchor: فعاصم يقرؤه بفتحتين كما يقرؤه في هذه السورة، وفي يس، فاستمر على عمل واحد

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r11.claim: The distinction offered for al-Kahf—ḍamma for wealth and fatḥ for edible fruit—cannot explain the readings in al-Anʿām and Yāsīn.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r11.anchor: وقد ذكروا في توجيه الضمتين في الكهف ما لا يمكن أن يأتي في السورتين

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r12.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r12.claim: As a parallel reading example, Abu ʿAmr, al-Kisaʾi, and Qunbul read خشب, while the others use ḍamma; the author calls the former reading analogous to the one just discussed.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#10/r12.anchor: والباقون بالضم، فهذه القراءة نظير تيك.

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#11/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#11/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#11/r1.claim: إذا أثمر is a time adverb for انظروا, either purely temporal or conditional with an omitted or advanced response: when it fruits, look at it.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#11/r1.anchor: وهو يحتمل أن يكون متمحضا للظرف، وأن يكون شرطا، وجوابه محذوف

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#11/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#11/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#11/r2.claim: The majority read ينعه with fatḥa on ي and sukūn on ن; Ibn Muhaysin, also reported from Qatada and al-Dahhak, uses ḍamma, while Ibrahim ibn Abi ʿAbla and al-Yamani read يانعة.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#11/r2.anchor: وهي قراءة قتادة والضحاك. وقرأ إبراهيم بن أبي عبلة واليماني: يانعة

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#11/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#11/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#11/r3.claim: الينع with fatḥa or ḍamma is the verbal noun of ripening; fatḥa is Hijazi and ḍamma is used by some Najdis, with variants ينَع and ينوع.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#11/r3.anchor: والينع بالفتح والضم مصدر: ينعت الثمرة

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#11/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#11/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#11/r4.claim: Alternatively الينع is a plural of يانع, like تاجر/تجر and صاحب/صحب; ينعت and أينعت both mean that fruit ripened, in triliteral and quadriliteral forms.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#11/r4.anchor: وقيل: الينع بالفتح جمع يانع كتاجر وتجر وصاحب وصحب

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#11/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#11/r5.speaker: الحجاج
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#11/r5.claim: Al-Hajjaj's phrase رؤوسا قد أينعت وحان قطافها describes heads as ripe and ready to be harvested.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#11/r5.anchor: وقال الحجاج: " أرى رؤوسا قد أينعت وحان قطافها "

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#11/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#11/r6.speaker: الفراء
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#11/r6.claim: Al-Farraʾ says أينعت means the fruit turned red; the hadith phrase compares a red-born child to الينعة, a red bead said to be carnelian or a kind of it.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#11/r6.anchor: قاله الفراء، ومنه الحديث في الملاعنة: " إن ولدته أحمر مثل الينعة "

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#11/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#11/r7.speaker: أبو عبيد
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#11/r7.claim: Abu ʿUbayd says ينعت تينع has fatḥa in the past and kasra in the present, citing a line about olives ripening; al-Layth reverses the vowels.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#11/r7.anchor: وقال الليث بعكس هذا: أي بكسرها في الماضي وبفتحها في المستقبل.

SAMIN-DURR:6:99#11/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#11/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#11/r8.claim: The close addresses believers because the signs show one God's power to create varied products from one soil and water; only reflective believers benefit from them.
SAMIN-DURR:6:99#11/r8.anchor: كون ما تقدم دالا على وحدانيته وإيجاده المصنوعات المختلفة

ZAJJAJ:v2p275/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p275/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p275/r1.claim: The original form of māʾ was mah; hamza replaced faint hāʾ, as shown by plural amwāh and miyāh and diminutive muwayh.
ZAJJAJ:v2p275/r1.anchor: قال أهل اللغة أصل كلمة ماء ماه إلا أن الهمزة أبدلت من الهاء لخفاء الهاء، والدليل على ذلك قولهم أمواه في جمعه، ومياه، ويصغر مويه.

ZAJJAJ:v2p275/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p275/r2.speaker: شاعر
ZAJJAJ:v2p275/r2.claim: An anonymous poet uses amwāh, supporting the plural form cited for the etymology of māʾ.
ZAJJAJ:v2p275/r2.anchor: قال الشاعر: سقى الله أمواها عرفت مكانها. . . جرابا وملكوما وبذر والغمرا

ZAJJAJ:v2p275/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p275/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p275/r3.claim: Khaḍir means akhḍar: one says akhḍara, fa-huwa akhḍar or khaḍir, analogous to aʿwara and ʿawar.
ZAJJAJ:v2p275/r3.anchor: معنى خضر كمعنى أخضر، يقال اخضر فهو أخضر وخضر، مثل أعوز فهو أعور وعور.

ZAJJAJ:v2p275/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p275/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p275/r4.claim: Qinwān is the plural of qinw, like ṣinw and ṣinwān; its dual is also qinwān with kasra on nūn.
ZAJJAJ:v2p275/r4.anchor: (قنوان) جمع قنو مثل صنو وصنوان، وإذا ثنيت القنو فهما قنوان يا هذا بكسر النون

ZAJJAJ:v2p275/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p275/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p275/r5.claim: Qinw is a date cluster; ʿidhq with kasra means a cluster, while ʿidhq with fatḥa means a palm tree.
ZAJJAJ:v2p275/r5.anchor: والقنو العذق بكسر العين وهي الكباسة، والعذق النخلة.

ZAJJAJ:v2p275/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p275/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p275/r6.claim: Dāniya means close and within reach.

ZAJJAJ:v2p275/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p275/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p275/r7.claim: Mention of nearby clusters suffices without naming distant ones, since near implies far; likewise 16:81 mentions garments protecting from heat while cold is understood.
ZAJJAJ:v2p275/r7.anchor: ولم يقل ومنها قنوان بعيدة. لأن في الكلام دليلا أن البعيدة السحيقة من النخل قد كانت غير سحيقة، واجتزئ بذكر القريبة عن ذكر البعيدة، كما قال عز وجل: (سرابيل تقيكم الحر) ولم يقل وسرابيل تقيكم البرد.

ZAJJAJ:v2p276/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p276/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p276/r1.claim: Gardens of grapes are coordinated with khaḍiran: God brought forth green vegetation and grape gardens from water.
ZAJJAJ:v2p276/r1.anchor: عطف على قوله (خضرا) أي فأخرجنا من الماء خضرا وجناب من أعناب

ZAJJAJ:v2p276/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p276/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p276/r2.claim: Janna is dense vegetation that conceals itself; the word derives from covering, and a shield is called mijan because it conceals.
ZAJJAJ:v2p276/r2.anchor: والجنة البستان، وإنما سمي البستان جنة، وكل نبت متكاثف يستر بعضه بعضا فهو جنة، وهو مشتق من جننت الشيء إذا سترته. ومن هذا قيل للترس مجن لأنه يستر.

ZAJJAJ:v2p276/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p276/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p276/r3.claim: Olive and pomegranate are alike or unlike in taste; some tastes resemble each other.
ZAJJAJ:v2p276/r3.anchor: أي في الطعم وفيه مايشبه طعم بعضه طعم بعض.

ZAJJAJ:v2p276/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p276/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p276/r4.claim: Olive and pomegranate are paired because Arabs know both trees' leaves cover their branches from end to end.
ZAJJAJ:v2p276/r4.anchor: وقرن الزيتون بالرمان لأنهما شجرتان تعرف العرب أن ورقهما يشتمل على الغصن من أوله إلى آخره.

ZAJJAJ:v2p276/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p276/r5.speaker: شاعر
ZAJJAJ:v2p276/r5.claim: An unidentified poem blesses a stranger as the fresh pomegranate and olive are blessed, illustrating their foliage.
ZAJJAJ:v2p276/r5.anchor: قال الشاعر: بورك الميت الغريب كما. . . بورك نضر الرمان والزيتون ومعناه أن البركة في ورقه واشتماله على عوده كله.

ZAJJAJ:v2p276/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p276/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p276/r6.claim: Thamara, thamar, and thimār occur; thamar is a plural of thimār, so the reading with ḍamma can be a plural of a plural or be lightened for ease.
ZAJJAJ:v2p276/r6.anchor: يقال ثمرة وثمر وثمار، وثمر جمع ثمار، فمن قرأ إلى ثمره بالضم أراد جمع الجمع، وإن شئت قلت إلى ثمره فخففت لثقل الضمة.

ZAJJAJ:v2p276/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p276/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p276/r7.claim: Yanaʿ means ripeness; trees are yanaʿa or aynʿa when fruit has matured.
ZAJJAJ:v2p276/r7.anchor: الينع النضج، يقال ينع الشجر وأينع إذا أدرك.

ZAJJAJ:v2p276/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p276/r8.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ZAJJAJ:v2p276/r8.claim: Abū ʿUbayda attributes the cited line using yanaʿa either to Yazīd ibn Muʿāwiya or al-Aḥwaṣ.
ZAJJAJ:v2p276/r8.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة البيت ليزيد بن معاوية أو للأحوص.

ZAJJAJ:v2p276/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p276/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p276/r9.claim: Creation's changes from state to state are signs that creatures cannot produce and proof God can resurrect those who denied resurrection.
ZAJJAJ:v2p276/r9.anchor: احتج الله عليهم بتصريف ما خلق ونقله من حال إلى حال، بما يعلمون أنه لا يقدر عليه المخلوقون، وأنه كذلك يبعثهم لأنهم كانوا ينكرون البعث

ZAJJAJ:v2p276/r10.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p276/r10.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p276/r10.claim: The account contains signs for believers and evidence for whoever affirms the truth.
ZAJJAJ:v2p276/r10.anchor: فقال لهم: (إن في ذلكم لآيات لقوم يؤمنون). فأعلمهم أن فيما قص دليلا لمن صدق.

ASAD-NOTES:6:99#n84/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:6:99#n84/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:6:99#n84/r1.claim: Although the following sequence uses present tense, the sentence is in past tense, obliquely pointing to life's original creation from water, as in 21:30.
ASAD-NOTES:6:99#n84/r1.anchor: In contrast with its sequence, which is governed by the present tense, the whole of the above sentence is expressed in the past tense - thus indicating, obliquely, the original, basic aspect of God's creating life "out of water"

ASAD-NOTES:6:99#n85/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:6:99#n85/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:6:99#n85/r1.claim: The plants share basic principles of life and growth but differ in physiology, appearance, and taste.
ASAD-NOTES:6:99#n85/r1.anchor: all so alike in the basic principles of their life and growth, and yet so different in physiology, appearance and taste.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p313/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p313/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p313/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses yanʿ as ripeness and full development; a poem describing a fresh, flourishing branch supports the sense.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p313/r2.anchor: قال: نضجه وبلاغه. واستشهد بقول الشاعر

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p313/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p313/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p313/r3.claim: Bint al-Shati distinguishes yanʿ as the natural peak of a plant or fruit's flourishing from naḍaj, used for skins cooked by fire in the punishment passage 4:56.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p313/r3.anchor: ولا يفوتنا معه أن الينع لأوج الأزدهار الطبيعي في النبت والثمر، على حين جاء النضج، لما تنضجه النار

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p980/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p980/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p980/r1.claim: انظروا إلى ثمره calls for reflection and contemplation, whereas كلوا من ثمره is a command to eat.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p980/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p980/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p980/r2.claim: The first verse ends by inviting contemplation of God's power; the second follows eating instructions with a warning against excess.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p980/r2.anchor: إحداهما في المطعوم والأخرى في التدبر في قدرة الله تعالى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p980/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p980/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p980/r3.claim: Mشتبه describes such strong resemblance that things become confusing or indistinguishable; متشابه can describe similarity in one respect without confusion.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p980/r3.anchor: المشتبه هو الملتبس من شدة التشابه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p980/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p980/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p980/r4.claim: Making distinct things so alike that they become confused is a stronger sign of divine power, so مشتبه suits the verse's call to contemplate that power.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p980/r4.anchor: مشتبهين أدل على القدرة أنه يجعل أمرين مختلفين ملتبسان

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p924/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p924/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p924/r1.claim: اشتباه is resemblance so intense that it causes confusion; تشابه can be limited to one aspect and need not reach confusion.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p924/r1.anchor: الاشتباه هو شدة التشابه وكثرته بحيث يؤدي ذلك إلى الاشكال

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p924/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p924/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p924/r2.claim: The verse negates both confusion and similarity; denying resemblance also rules out the stronger confusion, while the following verse uses the less intense تشابه wording.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p924/r2.anchor: نفي للاشتباه والتشابه فلو قال مشتبهاً وغير متشابه لنفى الاشتباه لكن لا ينفي التشابه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p979/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p979/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p979/r1.claim: The purpose of 6:99 is to display God's power through the growth and fruit, inviting people to look and reflect; its conclusion identifies signs for believers.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p979/r1.anchor: الغرض تبيين قدرة الله تعالى (انظُرُواْ إِلِى ثَمَرِهِ إِذَا أَثْمَرَ

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p596/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p596/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p596/r1.claim: The 6:99 wording highlights God's power through confusing resemblance, while 6:141 uses ordinary similarity in a passage about food; denying similarity also rules out confusion.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p596/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى (مشتبهاً وغير متشابه) تفيد لفت النظر إلى قدرة الله تعالى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p982/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p982/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p982/r1.claim: The author says غير متشابه fully denies resemblance, which also excludes confusion; saying غير مشتبه would leave open some resemblance.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p982/r1.anchor: قال تعالى (وغير متشابه) لينفيها من أصلها لأنه لو قال غير مشتبه يبقى التشابه موجود

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p982/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p982/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p982/r2.claim: مشتبه is the stronger term and better signals God's power, fitting 6:99's invitation to inspect and contemplate the fruit.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p982/r2.anchor: ومشتبه أدلّ على القدرة فوضعها في بيان القدرة وطلب التأمل والتدبر

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p89/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p89/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p89/.claim: The passage now turns to signs of God's mercy, providence, power, wisdom, and oneness, which also testify to the hereafter and are visible to those willing to believe.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p89/.anchor: Attention is now directed to the signs and arguments that depict God’s mercy, providence, power, wisdom and His oneness as well as testify to the hereafter.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p89/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p89/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p89/.claim: Al-samāʾ can mean either sky or clouds.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p89/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p89/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p89/.claim: The speaker first remains unspecified and is then identified as God, expressing care and providence and showing that God rules heaven, earth, air, and clouds as one realm.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p89/.anchor: the verse began with the speaker not being specified and then it was specified as God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p89/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p89/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p89/.claim: Rain falling from heaven and drawing out the earth's treasures displays harmony under one ruler; reviving dead land by rain is Qur'anic evidence that resurrection is possible.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p89/.anchor: the revival of dead land as a result of rain is presented as evidence of the hereafter.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p89/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p89/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p89/.claim: Grain illustrates a specific form of providence after the general one; it is mentioned first because it is commonly needed and can be stored, prompting reflection on a wise and powerful Creator.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p89/.anchor: First grains are mentioned since they are commonly needed and can also be stored.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p89/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p89/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p89/.claim: Verbs are omitted in both linked clauses about dates and orchards; the first omitted verb is passive and the second active.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p89/.anchor: The first is a passive verb and the second, an active one.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p89/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p89/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p89/.claim: Dates were a staple Arab fruit, and the verse traces their development from tree and buds to heavy hanging clusters so people can witness God's creativity and infer His power, wisdom, mercy, and providence.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p89/.anchor: attention is focused on their trees, on buds being created in these trees and from these buds heavy hanging bunches coming into being

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p90/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p90/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p90/.claim: People who see nature's elements sustain a date tree still foolishly imagine the world as a contest among many deities and competing intentions.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p90/.anchor: all elements of nature look after it but they still foolishly believe that this world is the battle-field of many deities and intents.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p90/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p90/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p90/.claim: Some enjoy God's provisions as if they existed only for food and comfort, never asking what responsibility they owe their provider or whether they will answer for these favors.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p90/.anchor: It is as if they enjoy privileges but have no obligation towards them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p90/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p90/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p90/.claim: Grapes, olives, and pomegranates are named because they were common in Arabia; the point is that people received fruits as well as staple food.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p90/.anchor: The purpose of their mention is not just to point to a few specific fruits for they are only mentioned because they were very common in Arabia.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p90/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p90/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p90/.claim: Fruit varieties resemble and differ from one another in appearance, size, and taste, reflecting God's providence, mercy, power, wisdom, and generosity.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p90/.anchor: each has different varieties which are similar to one another and others which are different from one another in appearance, size and taste.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p90/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p90/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p90/.claim: People could survive on bread and water, so abundant fruit that delights taste and smell manifests the Creator's generosity and is meant to awaken purification and innate gratitude, religion's foundation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p90/.anchor: Why then did the creator create for them all kinds of fruits in such abundance

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p90/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p90/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p90/.claim: The pronoun's antecedent is all the items mentioned, but its singular form directs attention to each item individually; a word meaning ripening is elided after the reference to ripening.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p90/.anchor: The pronoun occurs in the singular so that it points to each of these things separately and directs people to reflect on each of them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p90/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p90/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p90/.claim: Reflecting on every stage from inception to ripening reveals countless signs; each branch, flower, and fruit is a miracle for those demanding a sign.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p90/.anchor: If they have eyes, each branch, each flower and each fruit is no less than a miracle.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p90/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p90/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p90/.claim: The world could have survived in a plain, monotonous form, but its myriad petals and flowers were made to disclose God's power, wisdom, mercy, and providence so people could know Him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p90/.anchor: This world did not need all these marvels and majesties for its survival.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p91/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p91/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p91/.claim: The singular pronoun in “its fruit” refers collectively to everything just mentioned, while pointing separately to each item so readers reflect on each one.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p91/.anchor: points to each of these things separately and directs people to reflect on each of them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p91/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p91/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p91/.claim: The word for ripening is elided after the phrase about fruit ripening; the stated fruit supplies evidence for the suppressed wording after “its ripening.”
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p91/.anchor: what was mentioned became a proof of what was suppressed.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p91/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p91/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p91/.claim: People should observe every phase of each thing, from its inception through ripening, and they will see innumerable signs of divine power, wisdom, providence, creativity, care, benevolence, and beauty.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p91/.anchor: all the phases of each of these things that begin with their inception and end on their ripening.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p91/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p91/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p91/.claim: Nature did not need its many marvels to survive; the Creator made every petal and flower display divine power, wisdom, mercy, and providence so people could understand Him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p91/.anchor: this world did not need all these marvels and majesties for its survival.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p91/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p91/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p91/.claim: People reconstruct an entire ancient culture from a broken pottery fragment, yet fail to understand the abundant wisdom of God displayed in nature or take guidance from it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p91/.anchor: when he discovers a broken piece of pottery from the archaeological remains of the Moenjo Daro and Harappa

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p91/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p91/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p91/.claim: Recognizing an evident fact requires a sincere intent to accept it; people generally go astray through deficient intent rather than deficient knowledge.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p91/.anchor: the first thing required is that a person have the intent to accept it.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p91/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p91/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p91/.claim: The wisdom in every part of the universe shows that it was created by a powerful, wise, knowing being, rather than arising by itself or through an uncontrolled force.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p91/.anchor: The first thing that becomes evident is that this world replete with so much wisdom

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p92/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p92/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p92/.claim: The elements of nature and the seasons serve growth in specific proportions, which requires one ruling will to harmonize their diverse and conflicting effects toward a common purpose.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p92/.anchor: This is only possible if all these elements are under the command of a single intent

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p92/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p92/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p92/.claim: A universe so full of power, knowledge, and wisdom is not purposeless amusement; its moral order entails a day when God's perfect justice and absolute mercy appear.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p92/.anchor: It is not a place where there is no distinction between vice and virtue, good and evil

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p92/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p92/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p92/.claim: The benefits God placed in the universe require gratitude, worship, and obedience to Him alone, followed by accountability, reward for the grateful, and punishment for the ungrateful.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p92/.anchor: those who fulfilled their obligation towards them be rewarded and those who were ungrateful be punished.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p92/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p92/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p92/.claim: Since God provides for every human need, His grace also requires spiritual nourishment in the form of guidance, which is why prophets are needed.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p92/.anchor: The need for prophets of God arise as a result of this.

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p366/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p366/r1.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وعاصم
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p366/r1.claim: They read thamarihi with fatḥa on thāʾ and mīm. Sibawayh treats ثمر as a plural of ثمرة, supported by ثمرات and the broken plural ثمار; no distinct sense is assigned to the form.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p366/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وعاصم بالفتح في ذلك كله

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p366/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p366/r2.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p366/r2.claim: They read thumrihi with ḍamma on thāʾ and mīm. It may be a plural of ثمرة, like خشبة/خشب, or a plural of ثمار; al-Fārisī says the latter is possible by analogy though unrecorded by Sibawayh.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p366/r2.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي بالضم في ذلك

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p146/r3.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p146/r3.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p146/r3.claim: Rafʿ coordinates gardens with the preceding raised phrase qinwān dāniya.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p146/r3.anchor: فالحجة لمن رفع أنه رده على قوله ﴿ قنوان دانية وجنات ﴾

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p146/r4.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p146/r4.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p146/r4.claim: Naṣb coordinates gardens with the earlier phrase describing grain brought forth from vegetation.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p146/r4.anchor: والحجة لمن نصب أنه رده على قوله ﴿ نخرج منه حبا متراكبا ﴾ وجنات

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p146/r5.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p146/r5.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p146/r5.claim: Damma on both letters gives a collective plural from thimār or thamar, like izār and uzur.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p146/r5.anchor: فالحجة لمن ضم أنه أراد به جمع ثمار وثمر كما قالوا إزار وأزر

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p146/r6.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p146/r6.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p146/r6.claim: Fatḥa on both letters makes thamar a plural of thamara or thamar.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p146/r6.anchor: والحجة لمن فتح أنه أراد جمع

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p146/r8.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p146/r8.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p146/r8.claim: The Anʿām word denotes tree fruit, while the Cave word denotes property and furnishings, as its context says the owner had more wealth.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p146/r8.anchor: الفرق أن التي في الأنعام من أثمار الشجر والتي في الكهف من تثمير المال

IBNMUJAHID:v1p264/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p264/r1.speaker: ابن كثير، نافع، أبو عمرو، عاصم، ابن عامر
IBNMUJAHID:v1p264/r1.claim: These readers pronounce thāʾ and mīm in the cited fruit forms with fatḥa.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p264/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وعاصم وابن عامر ﴿ إلى ثمره ﴾

IBNMUJAHID:v1p264/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p264/r2.speaker: حمزة، الكسائي
IBNMUJAHID:v1p264/r2.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī pronounce thāʾ and mīm in these forms with ḍamma.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p264/r2.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائى ﴿ إلى ثمره ﴾ و ﴿ من ثمرة ﴾

QIRAAT-ER:6:99:40#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:6:99:40#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:6:99:40#1/r1.claim: The junction reads hamza al-waṣl with ḍamma rather than kasra, a canonical phonetic variation in liaison between the words.
QIRAAT-ER:6:99:40#1/r1.anchor: Hamza al-waṣl read with ḍamma instead of kasra at the junction — a canonical phonetic variation

QIRAAT-ER:6:99:43#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:6:99:43#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:6:99:43#1/r1.claim: The thumur variant has ḍamma on both syllables and makes the sense explicitly plural fruits rather than collective fruit.
QIRAAT-ER:6:99:43#1/r1.anchor: Ḍamma-ḍamma instead of fatḥa-fatḥa — thumur is the plural of thamar

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p215/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p215/r1.speaker: البراء
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p215/r1.claim: Al-Baraʾ glosses qinwan daniyah as near clusters.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p215/r1.anchor: عن أبي إسحاق عن البراء في قوله تعالى ﴿ قنوان دانية ﴾ قال قريبة

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p215/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p215/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p215/r2.claim: Qatada says qinwan are date-palm clusters and that they are near, drooping down.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p215/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ من طلعها قنوان دانية ﴾ قال قنوان عذوق النخلة يقول دانية متهدلة

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p215/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p215/r3.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p215/r3.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ وينعه ﴾ قال ونضجه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r6.speaker: الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r6.claim: Al-Zajjaj takes خضر as meaning green: the analogy is أخضر/خضر as أعور/عور.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r6.anchor: قال الزجاج الخضر بمعنى الأخضر اخضر فهو أخضر وخضر كاعور فهو أعور وعور

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r7.speaker: غيره
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r7.claim: Another view derives خضر from freshness, not color; calling the world green is a metaphor for freshness, while actual greenness denotes color.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r7.anchor: وقال غيره الخضر النضارة ولا مدخل للون فيه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r8.speaker: الليث
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r8.claim: Al-Layth says خضر means crops in the Qur'an, but in ordinary speech it can mean any green plant.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r8.anchor: قال الليث الخضر في كتاب الله الزرع وفي الكلام كل نبات من الخضرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r9.claim: Tarakub describes one thing mounted or piled upon another.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r10.claim: Ṭalʿ is the first growth emerging from a date palm within its sheaths; a palm is said to produce its ṭalʿ when it brings it out.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r10.anchor: الطلع أول ما يخرج من النخلة في أكمامه أطلعت النخلة أخرجت طلعها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r11.speaker: أبو عبيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r11.claim: Abu Ubayd says ṭalʿ is like the palm's sheath before it opens from the inner spadix, and the inner spadix itself is also called ṭalʿ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r11.anchor: قال أبو عبيد وطلعها كعراها قبل أن ينشق عن الإغريض والإغريض يسمى طلعا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r12.claim: A قنو is a palm cluster or bunch, also called الكباسة; the term can denote the cluster's stalk.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r12.anchor: القنو بكسر القاف وضمها العذق بكسر العين وهو الكباسة وهو عنقود النخلة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r13.speaker: القرطبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r13.claim: Al-Qurtubi transmits another sense for قنو: the palm heart, الجمار.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r14.claim: The few plural is أقناء and the many plural قنوان; dialects vary between قاف vowels and replacing the plural's واو with ياء, while the singular remains قنو.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r14.anchor: وجمعه في القلة أقناء وفي الكثرة قنوان بكسر القاف في لغة الحجاز وضمها في لغة قيس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r15.claim: زيتون is on the pattern فيعول like قيصوم, supported by أرض زتنة and the rarity of فعلول; its root differs from زيت.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r15.anchor: وزنه فيعول كقيصوم لقولهم أرض زتنة ولعدم فعلول أو قلته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r16.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r16.claim: رمان follows فعال like حماض and عناب, not فعلان, as shown by the expression أرض رمنة.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r16.anchor: الرمان فعال كالحماض والعناب وليس بفعلان لقولهم أرض رمنة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r17.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r17.claim: The forms ينع, الينع, and الينوع vary by dialect and mean that fruit has ripened and matured; أينه also means it ripened.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r17.anchor: يقال ينعت الثمرة إذا أدركت ونضجت وأينعت أيضا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r18.speaker: الحجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r18.claim: Al-Hajjaj's line about heads that have ripened uses أينعت metaphorically for maturity and the time to harvest.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r18.anchor: ومنه قول الحجاج: أرى رؤوسا قد أينعت وحان قطافها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r19.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r19.claim: Al-Farra says ينع and أينع can mean that fruit turned red; the liʿān hadith compares a red-born child to a red stone called الينعة, perhaps agate or a kind of it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r19.anchor: قال الفراء ينع الثمر وأينع احمر ومنه في حديث الملاعنة إن ولدته أحمر مثل الينعة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r20.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r20.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r20.claim: Some derive الينع as the plural of يانع, by analogy with تاجر/تجر and صاحب/صحب.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r20.anchor: وقيل الينع جمع يانع كتاجر وتجر وصاحب وصحب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p596/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p596/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p596/r2.claim: After recalling the favor of creating people, the passage recalls provision that sustains and serves their needs; here السماء means clouds.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p596/r2.anchor: لما ذكر إنعامه تعالى بخلقنا ذكر إنعامه علينا بما يقوم به أودنا ومصالحنا والسماء هنا السحاب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p596/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p596/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p596/r3.claim: The apparent sense is every kind of plant in Arabic: growing grains, fruits, vegetables, grasses, and trees; كل شيء means everything that grows.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p596/r3.anchor: والظاهر أن المعني بنبات كل شيء ما يسمى نباتا في اللغة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p596/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p596/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p596/r4.claim: One cause, water, yields many different outcomes, as another verse says that crops drink from one water while their produce differs.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p596/r4.anchor: وأشار إلى أن السبب واحد والمسببات كثيرة كما قال تعالى: يسقى بماء واحد ونفضل بعضها على بعض في الأكل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p596/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p596/r5.speaker: الطبري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p596/r5.claim: Al-Tabari takes plant of everything to include all growing animals, plants, minerals, and other things, since they feed and grow through rain.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p596/r5.anchor: وقال الطبري: نبات كل شيء جميع ما ينمو من الحيوان والنبات والمعادن وغير ذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p596/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p596/r6.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p596/r6.claim: Al-Farra says نبات means sustenance suitable as food for everything; on this reading كل شيء is restricted to what is nourished.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p596/r6.anchor: وقال الفراء: معناه رزق كل شيء أي ما يصلح غذاء لكل شيء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p596/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p596/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p596/r7.claim: The shift from third-person reference to first-person plural in فأخرجنا is an iltifat, using the majestic plural.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p596/r7.anchor: وفي قوله: فأخرجنا التفات من غيبة إلى تكلم بنون العظمة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p596/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p596/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p596/r8.claim: خضرا means fresh, lush, and tender, here emerging from the plant.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p596/r8.anchor: فأخرجنا منه خضرا أي من النبات غضا ناضرا طريا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p596/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p596/r9.speaker: أبو البقاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p596/r9.claim: The second فأخرجنا may be coordinated with the first, while Abu al-Baqa also allows it to be an appositional replacement for the first.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p596/r9.anchor: وفأخرجنا معطوف على فأخرجنا وأجاز أبو البقاء أن يكون بدلا من فأخرجنا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p596/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p596/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p596/r10.claim: From the greenery God brings stacked grains such as wheat, barley, and legumes, and layered seeds in fruits such as pomegranates and pine nuts.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p596/r10.anchor: أي من الخضر كالقمح والشعير وسائر القطاني ومن الثمار كالرمان والصنوبر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p596/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p596/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p596/r11.claim: نخرج may be an adjectival clause describing خضرا or an independent report.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p596/r11.anchor: ونخرج جملة في موضع الصفة لخضر أو يجوز أن يكون استئناف إخبار

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p596/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p596/r12.speaker: الأعمش وابن محيصن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p596/r12.claim: Al-Aʿmash and Ibn Muhaysin read يخرج منه حب متراكب, with حب governed in the nominative by يخرج and متراكب agreeing as its adjective.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p596/r12.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش وابن محيصن يخرج منه حب متراكب على أنه مرفوع بيخرج

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r1.speaker: ابن عباس والبراء والضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Bara, and al-Dahhak explain دانية as low and within reach, because the palm is short and its roots lie close to the ground.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r1.anchor: قنوان دانية أي قريبة من المتناول لقصرها ولصوق عروقها بالأرض قاله ابن عباس والبراء والضحاك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari praises this as meaning easy to pick and near at hand; even a seated person can reach fruit on a small palm.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r2.anchor: وحسنه الزمخشري فقال: سهلة المجتنى معرضة للقاطف كالشيء الداني القريب المتناول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r3.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r3.claim: Al-Hasan explains دانية as the palm clusters being close to one another.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن: قريب بعضها من بعض

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r4.claim: Another reported gloss says دانية means leaning or inclined.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r5.claim: Mentioning low palms but omitting tall ones may emphasize the more evident blessing, or the low palms may imply the tall ones, as a verse mentions garments protecting from heat while implying cold too.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r5.anchor: وذكر الدانية دون ذكر السحوق لأن النعمة بها أظهر أو حذف السحوق لدلالة الدانية عليها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r6.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r6.claim: The majority read قنوان with kasra on قاف.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r7.speaker: الأعمش والخفاف عن أبي عمرو والأعرج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r7.claim: Al-Aʿmash, al-Khaffaf transmitting from Abu Amr, and al-Aʿraj in one transmission read قنوان with damma on قاف; al-Sulami transmits this from Ali.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r7.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش والخفاف عن أبي عمر والأعرج في رواية بضمها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r8.speaker: الأعرج وهارون عن أبي عمرو
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r8.claim: In another transmission al-Aʿraj and Harun from Abu Amr read قنوان with fatḥa on قاف; Abu al-Fath parses it as a collective noun on فعلان.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r8.anchor: وقرأ الأعرج في رواية وهارون عن أبي عمرو قنوان بفتح القاف وخرجه أبو الفتح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r9.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r9.claim: Ibn Atiyya's book reports al-Aʿraj reading قنوان with damma as the plural of قنو with damma.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r9.anchor: وفي كتاب ابن عطية روي عن الأعرج ضم القاف على أنه جمع قنو بضم القاف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r10.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r10.claim: Al-Farra assigns this form to Qays and Hijaz dialects and says kasra is more common among Arabs.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r10.anchor: وقال الفراء: وهي لغة قيس وأهل الحجاز والكسر أشهر في العرب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r11.claim: The phrase is a subject-predicate sentence; ومن طلعها is an appositional specification of ومن النخل, yielding clusters from the palm's spathes.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r11.anchor: وهذه الجملة مبتدأ وخبر ومن طلعها بدل من ومن النخل والتقدير وقنوان دانية كائنة من طلع النخل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r12.claim: The palm is singled out from the general plant account to emphasize a great favor, since dates were among the Arabs' principal foods.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r12.anchor: وأفرد ذكر القنوان وجرد من قوله: نبات كل شيء نخرج منه خضرا لما في تجريدها من عظيم المنة والنعمة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r13.claim: Presenting the palm clusters as a nominal sentence signals that this provision is established and assured.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r13.anchor: وأبرزت في صورة المبتدأ والخبر ليدل على الثبوت والاستقرار

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r14.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r14.claim: Ibn Atiyya parses an implied نخرج من النخل and makes the following sentence its object; the author rejects this because the verb takes one object and nothing licenses a clausal object here.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r14.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: ومن النخل تقديره نخرج من النخل ومن طلعها قنوان ابتداء خبره مقدم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r15.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r15.claim: Al-Zamakhshari allows an omitted predicate, مخرجة, inferred from فأخرجنا; the author says the sentence needs no such addition.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r15.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: ويجوز أن يكون الخبر محذوفا لدلالة فأخرجنا عليه تقديره ومخرجة من طلع النخل قنوان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r16.speaker: أبو البقاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r16.claim: Abu al-Baqa offers parses making قنوان a subject or participial agent and supplying implicit pronouns; the author calls the analysis confused and unsuitable for Qur'anic parsing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r16.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: ويجوز أن يكون قنوان مبتدأ والخبر من طلعها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
