ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r17.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r17.claim: With the variant يخرج منه حب, the palm phrase may coordinate with that verb, as in parallel clauses, or stand independently as a subject-predicate sentence, the better analysis.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p597/r17.anchor: ومن قرأ يخرج منه حب متراكب جاز أن يكون قوله: من النخل من طلعها قنوان دانية معطوفا عليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r1.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r1.claim: The majority read جنات in the accusative and coordinate it with نبات: this is a distinguished specific item after the general category, with palms and vineyards singled out for their honor.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r1.anchor: قراءة الجمهور بكسر التاء عطفا على قوله نبات وهو من عطف الخاص على العام لشرفه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r2.claim: Palms and grape gardens are singled out together as especially prized, as in the verse describing a garden of palms and grapes.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r2.anchor: كما قال: أيود أحدكم أن تكون له جنة من نخيل وأعناب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r3.speaker: محمد بن أبي ليلى والأعمش وأبو بكر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r3.claim: Muhammad ibn Abi Layla, al-Aʿmash, and Abu Bakr in one transmission from Asim read جنات in the nominative.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r3.anchor: وقرأ محمد بن أبي ليلى والأعمش وأبو بكر في رواية عنه عن عاصم وجنات بالرفع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r4.speaker: أبو عبيد وأبو حاتم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r4.claim: Abu Ubayd and Abu Hatim reject the nominative reading, with Abu Hatim arguing that grape gardens cannot be from date palms; the author says the reading has valid Arabic analyses.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r4.anchor: وأنكر أبو عبيد وأبو حاتم هذه القراءة حتى قال أبو حاتم: هي محال لأن الجنات من الأعناب لا تكون من النخل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r5.speaker: النحاس وابن عطية وأبو البقاء والزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r5.claim: One grammatical analysis takes raised جنات as a subject with an omitted predicate such as لهم, لكم, من الكرم, or ثم.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r5.anchor: وجهت على أنه مبتدأ محذوف الخبر فقدره النحاس ولهم جنات وقدره ابن عطية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r6.claim: This omitted-predicate pattern resembles the nominative reading وحور عين after the verse about being served a cup, and Sibawayh, al-Kisai, and al-Farra permit it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r6.anchor: ونظيره قراءة من قرأ وحور عين بالرفع بعد قوله: يطاف عليهم بكأس من معين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r7.claim: Another parse delays the omitted predicate: gardens of grapes are brought forth, inferred from the earlier فأخرجنا, just as a predicate can be omitted after a parallel clause.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r8.speaker: الطبري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r8.claim: Al-Tabari coordinates raised جنات with قنوان; Ibn Atiyya calls that weak, and Abu al-Baqa objects that grapes do not grow from palms.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r8.anchor: ووجهها الطبري على أن وجنات عطف على قنوان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhshari offers coordination with قنوان if the phrase means palm clusters and grape gardens as two kinds of produce, without carrying over من النخل to the gardens.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r9.anchor: والثاني أن يعطف على قنوان على معنى وحاصله أو ومخرجه من النخل قنوان وجنات من أعناب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r10.claim: That coordination is possible if the palm restriction is not applied to both nouns: clusters come from palms and gardens from grapes, like paired people from different tribes.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r10.anchor: وهذا العطف هو على أن لا يلاحظ فيه قيد من النخل فكأنه قال من النخل قنوان دانية جنات من أعناب حاصلة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r11.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r11.claim: The accusative reading of الزيتون والرمان is unanimous.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r11.anchor: والزيتون والرمان مشتبها وغير متشابه قرئ بالنصب إجماعا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r12.speaker: ابن عطية والزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r12.claim: Ibn Atiyya coordinates الزيتون والرمان with حبا or نبات; al-Zamakhshari also allows coordination with نبات, but prefers accusative اختصاص because the two kinds are especially eminent.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r12.anchor: قال ابن عطية: عطفا على حبا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r13.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r13.claim: Qatadah says these plants resemble one another in their leaves but differ in their fruit.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r13.anchor: قال قتادة: يتشابه في الورق ويتباين في الثمر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r14.speaker: ابن جريج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r14.claim: Ibn Jurayj says they may look alike yet taste different, like two pomegranates with the same color but different flavors.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r14.anchor: وقال ابن جريج: متشابها في النظر وغير متشابه في الطعم مثل الرمانتين لونهما واحد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r15.speaker: الطبري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r15.claim: Al-Tabari allows similarity of fruit with different tastes, or similar taste with different appearance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r15.anchor: وقال الطبري: جائز أن يتشابه في الثمر يتباين في الطعم ويحتمل أن يريد تشابه الطعم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r16.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r16.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says some fruits resemble others and some differ in size, color, or taste; their variety shows deliberate design rather than neglect.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p598/r16.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: بعضه متشابه وبعضه غير متشابه في القدر واللون والطعم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r1.claim: A noncanonical reading has متشابها, with the same reciprocal sense as مشتبهًا; both forms express mutual resemblance, like اختصم/تخاصم.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r1.anchor: قرئ شاذا متشابها وهما بمعنى واحد كاختصم وتخاصم واشترك واستوى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r2.claim: مشتبها may be a circumstantial accusative describing the pomegranate because it is nearest, with the matching circumstance omitted after the olive.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r2.anchor: وانتصب مشتبها على أنه حال من الرمان لقربه وحذفت الحال من الأول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r3.claim: Alternatively, مشتبهًا may describe the earlier olive by precedence, with the estimate that both olive and pomegranate are similar and dissimilar.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r3.anchor: أو حال من الأول لسبقه فالتقدير والزيتون مشتبها وغير متشابه والرمان كذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r4.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects al-Zamakhsharī’s inference from the verse of poetry: بريئًا can describe singular, dual, or plural, whereas a dual circumstantial form would be required.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r4.anchor: والظاهر المعطوف عليه فيه إذ يجوز أن يكون خبرا عنهما ولا يجوز أن يكون حالا منهما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r5.speaker: الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r5.claim: Al-Zajjāj says olive and pomegranate are paired because Arabs know both trees have leaves extending along the branch from end to end; a poem illustrates the pairing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r5.anchor: وقال الزجاج: قرن الزيتون بالرمان لأنهما شجرتان تعرف العرب أن ورقهما يشتمل على الغصن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r6.claim: Look with the eyes, as إلى indicates; the sight leads to reflection and inference about God’s power in changing fruit through its stages.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r6.anchor: النظر نظر رؤية العين ولذلك عداه بإلى لكن يترتب عليه الفكر والاعتبار والاستبصار

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r7.claim: The verse singles out the beginning and ripeness, though intermediate stages invite reflection, because the endpoints are more remarkable and clearer proofs.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r7.anchor: ونبه على هاتين الحالتين وإن كان بينهما أحوال يقع بها الاعتبار والاستبصار لأنهما أغرب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r8.speaker: ابن وثاب، مجاهد، حمزة، الكسائي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r8.claim: Ibn Waththāb, Mujāhid, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī read ثمره with ḍamma on both letters; Ibn Waththāb and Mujāhid explain it as kinds of wealth yielded by the tree.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r8.anchor: وقرأ ابن وثاب ومجاهد وحمزة والكسائي إلى ثمره بضم الثاء والميم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r9.speaker: أبو علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r9.claim: Abū ʿAlī prefers ثمر as a plural of ثمرة, on the pattern of خشبة and خشب, with comparable plurals from weak nouns.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r9.anchor: قال أبو علي: والأحسن أن يكون جمع ثمرة كخشبة وخشب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r10.speaker: فرقة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r10.claim: Another group reads with ḍamma on thāʾ and a still mīm for ease, like saying كتب for الكتب.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r10.anchor: وقرأت فرقة بضم الثاء وإسكان الميم طلبا للخفة كما تقول في الكتب كتب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r11.speaker: باقي السبعة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r11.claim: The other seven canonical readers have fatḥa on both letters; Abū Ḥayyān analyzes ثمر as a collective noun like شجر.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r11.anchor: وقرأ باقي السبعة ثمره بفتح الثاء والميم وهو اسم جنس كشجرة وشجر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r12.claim: ثمر can include what grows on the tree, while calling the tree itself ثمر is figurative.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r12.anchor: والثمر حتى الشجر وما يطلع وإن سمي الشجر ثمرا فمجاز

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r13.speaker: الجمهور؛ قتادة، الضحاك، ابن محيصن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r13.claim: The majority read وينعه with fatḥa on yāʾ and still nūn; Qatāda, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, and Ibn Muḥayṣin read yāʾ with ḍamma.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r13.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور وينعه بفتح الياء وسكون النون، وقرأ قتادة والضحاك وابن محيصن بضم الياء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r14.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة، اليماني، ابن محيصن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r14.claim: Ibn Abī ʿAbla and al-Yamānī read يانعه, an active participle from ينع; al-Zamakhsharī attributes this reading to Ibn Muḥayṣin.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r14.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة واليماني ويانعه اسم فاعل من ينع ونسبها الزمخشري إلى ابن محيصن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r15.speaker: المروزي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r15.claim: Al-Marwazī says alternating winds expose fruit to sun and then shade, preventing both failure to ripen and scorching.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p599/r15.anchor: وقال المروزي: إذا أثمر عند لا ظل له دائم فلا ينضج ولا شمس دائمة فتحرق أرسل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p601/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p601/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p601/r1.claim: ذلكم points to everything just mentioned, from splitting grain and pit through all God created and bestowed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p601/r1.anchor: الإشارة بذلكم إلى جميع ما سبق ذكره من فلق الحب والنوى إلى آخر ما خلق تعالى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p601/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p601/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p601/r2.claim: The signs demonstrate God’s perfect power, workmanship, and exclusive creation; they benefit only those whom God has destined to believe.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p601/r2.anchor: والآيات العلامات الدالة على كمال قدرته وإحكام صنعته وتفرده بالخلق دون غيره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p601/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p601/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p601/r3.claim: Specifying believers signals that manifest signs do not benefit those whose destiny is unbelief.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p601/r3.anchor: وظهور الآيات لا ينفع إلا لمن قدر الله له الإيمان فأما من سبق قدر الله له بالكفر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p601/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p601/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p601/r4.claim: The sequence follows the earlier mention of splitting grain: vegetation is followed by stacked grain, then dates from their pits.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p601/r4.anchor: لما تقدم إن الله فالق الحب والنوى جاء الترتيب بعد ذلك تابعا لهذا الترتيب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p601/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p601/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p601/r5.claim: Crops precede trees because grain is nourishment, fruit a delicacy, and nourishment comes first.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p601/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p601/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p601/r6.claim: Date palms precede other fruits because they serve Arabs as a staple comparable to nourishment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p601/r6.anchor: وقدم النخل على سائر الفواكه لأنه يجري مجرى الغذاء بالنسبة إلى العرب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p601/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p601/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p601/r7.claim: Grapes are first among fruits as the noblest; all their successive states and products are useful, including sour and ripe grapes, vinegar, syrup, and raisins.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p601/r7.anchor: وقدم العنب لأنه أشرف الفواكه وهو في جميع أطواره منتفع به حنوط ثم حصرم ثم عنب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p601/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p601/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p601/r8.claim: Olive follows for its use as food and its highly beneficial oil for eating, lighting, and other uses.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p601/r8.anchor: وقدم الزيتون لأنه كثير المنفعة في الأكل وفيما يعصر منه من الدهن العظيم النفع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p601/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p601/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p601/r9.claim: Pomegranate is singled out for its mixture of rind, pith, seed, and juice: the first three are cold, dry, dense, and astringent, while its juice has opposite qualities.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p601/r9.anchor: وذكر الرمان لعجب حاله وغرابته فإنه مركب من قشر وشحم وعجم وماء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p601/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p601/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p601/r10.claim: Its juice is delicious, temperate, strengthening, and both food and medicine; combining opposed qualities in one fruit displays God’s power.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p601/r10.anchor: ألذ الأشربة وألطفها وأقربها إلى حيز الاعتدال وفيه تقوية للمزاج الضعيف غذاء من وجه ودواء من وجه

ALUSI-FULL:v7p237/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p237/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p237/r1.claim: The rain passage recalls another immense blessing that shows God’s power and the breadth of His mercy.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p237/r1.anchor: تذكير لنعمة أخرى من نعمه سبحانه الجليلة المنبئة عن كمال قدرته عز وجل وسعة رحمته

ALUSI-FULL:v7p237/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p237/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p237/r2.claim: The water is rain; “sky” may mean clouds, a direction or region of the sky with an implied noun, or the literal heaven, as al-Jubbaʾi prefers.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p237/r2.anchor: والمراد من الماء المطر ومن السماء السحاب أو الكلام على تقدير مضاف

ALUSI-FULL:v7p237/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p237/r3.speaker: الجبائي
ALUSI-FULL:v7p237/r3.claim: Al-Jubbaʾi reads the descent literally from heaven to clouds and then earth, rejecting the account that terrestrial vapors rise and condense into rain.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p237/r3.anchor: وقيل : الكلام على ظاهره والإنزال من السماء حقيقة إلى السحاب ومنه إلى الأرض واختاره الجبائي

ALUSI-FULL:v7p237/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p237/r4.speaker: الجبائي
ALUSI-FULL:v7p237/r4.claim: Al-Jubbaʾi argues that hail can occur in hot weather and rain in the coldest season without freezing, which he says undermines the vapor account.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p237/r4.anchor: واحتج على فساد قول من يقول : إن البخارات الكثيرة تجتمع في باطن الأرض ثم تصعد

ALUSI-FULL:v7p237/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p237/r5.speaker: الجبائي
ALUSI-FULL:v7p237/r5.claim: He argues that rising vapors disperse rather than form drops; abundant water forms when vapor meets a smooth ceiling, but the open air has no such surface.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p237/r5.anchor: أن البخارات إدا ارتفعت وتصاعدت تفرقت وإذا تفرقت لم يتولد منها قطرات الماء

ALUSI-FULL:v7p237/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p237/r6.speaker: الجبائي
ALUSI-FULL:v7p237/r6.claim: He further argues that if rain came from vapors rising constantly from seas, rain should continually fall above them, which it does not.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p237/r6.anchor: فإذا تصاعدت البخارات في الهواء وليس فوقها سطح أملس تتصل به وجب أن لا يحصل منها شيء

ALUSI-FULL:v7p237/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p237/r7.speaker: الجبائي
ALUSI-FULL:v7p237/r7.claim: Al-Jubbaʾi says philosophers require pre-existing matter because they regard bodies as eternal and change as merely a shift in qualities; Muslims instead hold that bodies are created and God freely creates as He wills.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p237/r7.anchor: والقوم إنما احتاجوا إلى هذا القول لأنهم اعتقدوا أن الأجسام قديمة فيمتنع دخول الزيادة والنقصان فيها

ALUSI-FULL:v7p237/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p237/r8.speaker: الجبائي
ALUSI-FULL:v7p237/r8.claim: Since the Qur’an’s apparent sense says water descends from heaven and no proof makes that impossible, al-Jubbaʾi says Muslims should affirm the apparent meaning without those speculative complications.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p237/r8.anchor: وحيث دل ظاهر القرآن على أن الماء إنما ينزل من السماء ولا دليل على امتناع هذا الظاهر

ALUSI-FULL:v7p237/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p237/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p237/r9.claim: Alusi says philosophers have answered all of al-Jubbaʾi’s objections; their account also rests on denying rupture and contact, a fiery sphere beneath the heavens, and observations of rain clouds from high mountains.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p237/r9.anchor: أنهم أجابوا عن جميع تلك الوجوه وأن الذي دعاهم إلى القول بذلك ليس مجرد ما ذكر

ALUSI-FULL:v7p237/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p237/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p237/r10.claim: Although some parts of that cosmology conflict with religious evidence and others lack scriptural confirmation, mountain observations of water descending from rain clouds support its validity in some respects, and Alusi sees no harm in it.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p237/r10.anchor: لكن مشاهدة من على الجبل ما ذكر ونحوها يستدعي صحة قولهم في الجملة ولا أرى فيه بأسا

ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r1.claim: A common view takes the statement that each raindrop comes with an angel literally.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r1.anchor: ما من قطرة تنزل الا ومعها ملك وهو عند الكثير محمول على ظاهره

ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r2.speaker: الفلاسفة
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r2.claim: Philosophers interpret the angel as the nature inherent in the body that causes the rain to descend.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r2.anchor: هذا الملك على الطبيعة الحالة في تلك الجسمية الموجبة لذلك النزول

ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r3.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r3.claim: Another view makes the angel an immaterial, self-subsisting light that directs and preserves the raindrop.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r3.anchor: نور مجرد عن المادة قائم بنفسه مدبر للقطر حافظ إياه

ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r4.speaker: افلاطون
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r4.claim: Plato posits such immaterial lights for every kind of celestial body, element, and compound; al-Qunawi's commentary on the Fatiha suggests a similar view.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r4.anchor: ويثبت افلاطون هذا النور المجرد لكل نوع من الافلاك والكواكب والبسائط العنصرية

ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r5.claim: ماء is the accusative direct object of أنزل, with the indirect object phrase من السماء preceding it.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r5.anchor: على المفعولية لانزل وتقديم المفعول به غير الصريح عليه لما مر مرارا

ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r6.claim: The فاء marks consequence, with the sequence understood according to the time appropriate to each thing.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r6.anchor: أي بسبب الماء والفاء للتعقيب وتعقيب كل شيء بحسبه

ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r7.claim: The clause is coordinated with أنزل; the shift to God's first-person plural stresses the care given to the purpose for which water was sent.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r7.anchor: والالتفات إلى التكلم إظهار لكمال العناية بشأن ما أنزل الماء لأجله

ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r8.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r8.claim: A further explanation says the earlier mention of God as creator prompts direct address, and the majestic plural underscores divine care despite the water's singularity.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r8.anchor: وهي أنه سبحانه لما ذكر فيما مضى ما ينبهك على انه الخالق اقتضى ذلك التوجه اليه حتى يخاطب

ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r9.claim: The phrase means every plant kind, whose quantity, quality, properties, and effects vary in degree, as another verse describes.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r9.anchor: أي كل صنف من أصناف النبات المختلفة في الكم والكيف والخواص والآثار

ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r10.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r10.claim: Nabat is growth that emerges from earth, whether it has a trunk like a tree or not like grass.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r10.anchor: من الناميات سواء كان له ساق كالشجر أو لم يكن له ساق كالنجم

ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r11.claim: Common usage narrows النبات to stemless plants, often those eaten by animals, while considered in its full sense it includes every growing plant, animal, or human.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r11.anchor: اختص في التعارف بما لا ساق له بل قد اختص عند العامة بما تأكله الحيوانات ومتى اعتبرت الحقائق

ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r12.speaker: بعض
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r12.claim: Some take النبات here in the broader first sense of all growth from earth.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r12.anchor: والمراد هنا عند بعض المعنى الأول

ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r13.claim: Some regard this phrase as the start of the detailed account of the general production; منه then refers to نبات.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r13.anchor: شروعا في تفصيل ما أجمل من الاخراج

ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r14.claim: خضر means green, like أعور/عور, and here denotes a tender green shoot branching from the root of a plant grown from seed.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r14.anchor: والخضر بمعنى الأخضر كأعور وعور وأكثر ما يستعمل الخضر فيما تكون خضرته خلقية

ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r15.claim: Green is a color between white and black but nearer black, so Arabic can call green black and vice versa.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r15.anchor: وأصل الخضرة لون بين البياض والسواد وهو إلى السواد أقرب ولذا يسمى الأخضر أسود

ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r16.claim: Another permitted reading returns the pronoun to water and takes من causally: the water produces the green growth.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r16.anchor: وجوز عود الضمير إلى الماء ومن سببية

ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r17.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r17.claim: On the reading where منه refers to water, he parses the clause as an appositional substitute for the first أخرجنا.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r17.anchor: أبو البقاء هذا الكلام حينئذ بدلا من ( أخرجنا ) الأول

ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r18.speaker: بعض المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r18.claim: If the pronoun refers to water, the verse highlights how sweet water, white to the eye, yields plants and fruit with diverse tastes and colors; a rain poem illustrates the image.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r18.anchor: أن في الآية على تقدير عود الضمير إلى الماء معنى بديعا

ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r19.claim: The imperfect verb can vividly present the remarkable scene; alternatively the clause is an independent sentence describing what comes from the green shoot.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r19.anchor: صفة لخضر وصيغة المضارع لاستحضار الصورة بما فيها من الغرابة

ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r20.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r20.claim: The grain is stacked one above another, as in an ear of grain.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r20.anchor: أي بعضه فوق بعض كما في السنبل

ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r21.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r21.claim: A reading has the passive third-person form يخرج منه حب متراكب.

ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r22.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r22.claim: For some, the verse now begins detailing trees after detailing stemless plants.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r22.anchor: وهذا شروع في تفصيل حال الشجر اثر بيان حال النجم عند البعض

ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r23.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r23.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r23.claim: The phrase من النخل is a fronted predicate, and من طلعها is a partitive apposition with the governing preposition repeated.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p238/r23.anchor: من طلعها بدل منه بدل بعض من كل باعادة العامل

ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r1.claim: قنوان is the subject; the phrase means that clusters come from the spathes of the palms.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r1.anchor: مبتدأ وحاصله من طلع النخيل قنوان

ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r2.claim: Alternatively the predicate is omitted and supplied by أخرجنا; on this parse the prepositional phrase attaches to an implied particular production.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r2.anchor: الخبر محذوفا فالدلالة ( أخرجنا ) عليه وهو كون خاص

ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r3.claim: With the prior reading يخرج منه, قنوان can be coordinated with حب.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r3.anchor: وعلى القراءة السابقة آنفا يكون ( قنوان ) معطوفا على حب

ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r4.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r4.claim: Another paraphrase supplies a verb: We bring out from the palms, from their spathes, clusters.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r4.anchor: المعنى واخرجنا من النخل نخلا من طلعها قنوان

ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r5.claim: قنوان is the plural of قنو, a date cluster, corresponding to a grape cluster; its dual and plural forms are distinguished by inflection.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r5.anchor: جمع قنو بنعنى العذق وهو للتمر بمنزلة العنقود للعنب

ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r6.speaker: ابن خالويه
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r6.claim: Ibn Khalawayh says قنوان, صنوان, and رئدان are among the few nouns whose dual and plural forms coincide; al-Suyuti's al-Muzhir also transmits Sibawayh's parallel forms.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r6.anchor: ولم يأت مفرد يستوي مثناه وجمعه إلا ثلاثة أسماء هذا وصنو وصنوان ورئد ورئدان بمعنى مثل قاله ابن خالويه

ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r7.claim: The قاف is read with either damma or fatha; the fatha form is a collective noun because فعْلان is not a broken-plural pattern.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r7.anchor: بضم القاف وبفتحها على أنه اسم جمع لان فعلان ليس من زنات التكسير

ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r8.speaker: الزجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r8.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains دانية as close enough to reach.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r8.anchor: قريبة من المتناول كما قال الزجاج

ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r9.claim: Only the nearby palms are mentioned because they imply the contrasting kind and signal an added blessing.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r9.anchor: واقتصر على ذكرها عن مقابلها لدلالتها عليه وزيادة النعمة فيها

ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r10.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r10.claim: A second literal interpretation is that the palms hang near the ground because their fruit is plentiful and their load heavy.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r10.anchor: دانية من الأرض بكثرة ثمرها وثقل حملها

ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r11.claim: The word may instead be figurative, describing how easily the fruit can be reached.

ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r12.claim: The gardens are coordinated with نبات كل شيء: water brings forth gardens of grapes.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r12.anchor: عطف على نبات كل شيء أي واخرجنا به جنات كائنة من أعناب

ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r14.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r14.claim: Al-Tibi considers coordination with حبا more apparent: the general plant category is then elaborated by its grains and other growth.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r14.anchor: الأظهر أن يكون عطفا على حبا

ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r15.claim: If نبات has its broad sense, gardens are already included and cannot naturally be coordinated with it; if it means stemless plants, gardens are outside it, and a new verb must be supplied for palms.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r15.anchor: وهذا مبني على أن المراد بالنبات المعنى العام وحينئذ لا يحسن عطفه عليه لأنه داخل فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r16.speaker: علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه وابن مسعود والأعمش ويحيى بن يعمر وأبو بكر عن عاصم
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r16.claim: These readers have وجنات in the nominative, with an implied لكم, ثم, or similar expression.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r16.anchor: قرأ أمير المؤمنين علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه وابن مسعود والأعمش ويحيى بن يعمر وأبو بكر عن عاصم ( وجنات ) بالرفع

ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r17.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r17.claim: Al-Zamakhshari allows coordinating the nominative gardens with قنوان.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r17.anchor: أن يكون على العطف على ( قنوان )

ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r18.speaker: التقريب
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r18.claim: Al-Taqrib objects that treating من أعناب as an adjective yields gardens from palms made from grapes, while making it a predicate leaves an indefinite subject coordinated with a singular.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r18.anchor: في التقريب : وفيه نظر لأنه ان عطف على ذلك فمن أعناب م حينئذ إا صفة ( جنات ) فيفسد المعنى

ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r19.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r19.claim: Al-Kashf says the predicate reading is unlikely to be al-Zamakhshari's intent and offers a response based on coordination with a restricted noun.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r19.anchor: وفي الكشف أن الثاني بعيد الفهم من لفظ الزمخشري وإن أمكن الجواب بأن العطف على المخصص

ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r20.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r20.claim: The apparent parse starts a new clause with an implied production phrase; the elaborate alternative is needless, while gardens are explicitly plural because their benefit usually requires a group of vines.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r20.anchor: الظاهر الاول لكنه عطف جملة على جملة ويقدر ومخرجه من الخضر أو من الكرم

ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r21.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r21.claim: Gardens are expressly mentioned as plural because people generally benefit from this kind only when several instances are gathered together.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r21.anchor: زيادة الجنات هنا كما قيل من غير اكتفاء بذكر اسم الجنس

ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r22.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r22.claim: The accusative can mark specification, highlighting these prized kinds, or coordinate them with نبات.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p239/r22.anchor: نصب على الاختصاص لعزة هذين الصنفين عندهم أو على العطف على نبات

ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r1.claim: The paired adjectives may be a circumstantial phrase for الزيتون, with the same understood for الرمان, or for الرمان with the same supplied for الزيتون.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r1.anchor: حال من الزيتون لسبقه اكتفي به عن حال ما عطف عليه والتقدير والزيتون مشتبها وغير متشابه والرمان كذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r2.claim: An omitted بعض is understood: some are alike and some unlike in appearance, size, color, taste, and other features, displaying their maker's power and wisdom.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r2.anchor: بعض أي بعض ذلك مشتبها وبعضه غير متشابه في الهيئة والمقدار واللون والطعم وغير ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r3.claim: Some allow the circumstantial phrase to apply to both nouns by supplying an interpretive adjustment.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r3.anchor: من جوز كونه حالا منهما مع التزام التأويل

ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r4.claim: Here the forms افتعل and تفاعل carry the same sense, as in استوى and تساوى.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r4.anchor: وافتعل وتفاعل هنا بمعنى كاستوى وتساوى

ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r5.claim: A reading has متشابها in place of مشتبها.

ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r6.claim: The command is to look reflectively and with insight.

ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r7.claim: Its fruit means the fruit of the olive and pomegranate trees; the verse shifts usage because those names earlier denoted the fruit itself.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r7.anchor: أي ثمر ذلك أي الزيتون والرمان والمراد شجرتهما وأريد بهما فيما سبق الثمرة ففي الكلام استخدام

ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r8.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r8.claim: Al-Farra instead takes the earlier words as referring to olive and pomegranate trees, so no shift in usage is needed.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r8.anchor: وعن الفراء أن المراد في الأول شجر الزيتون وشجر الرمان وحينئذ لا استخدام

ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r9.claim: The pronoun may be understood to include every fruit-bearing thing mentioned earlier, including palms; referring distributively to either item alone is unlikely because its antecedent would be unclear.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r9.anchor: رجوع الضمير إلى جميع ما تقدم بالتأويل المذكور ليشمل النخل وغيره مما يثمر

ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r10.claim: At first fruiting, the fruit is tiny and scarcely useful, setting up its contrast with ripeness.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r10.anchor: أي إذا أخرج ثمره كيف يخرجه ضئيلا لا يكاد ينتفع به

ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r11.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r11.claim: Hamza and al-Kisai read ثمره with a damma on the first letter, as a plural of ثمرة or of ثمار.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r11.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي ( ثمره ) بضم الثاء وهو جمع ثمرة

ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r12.claim: ينعه refers to ripening or the ripe state, when the fruit becomes large, useful, and fully pleasurable; the word originally names ripening.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r12.anchor: أي وإلى حال نضجه أو نضيجه كيف يعود ضخما ذا نفع عظيم ولذة كاملة

ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r13.claim: Alternatively, ينع is a plural of يانع, on the pattern تاجر/تجر.

ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r14.claim: The word is also read with a damma, an attested dialect, and Ibn Muhaysin reads يانعه.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r14.anchor: باضم وهي لغة فيه وقرأ ابن محيصن ( ويانعه )

ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r15.claim: Mentioning the initial fruiting stage points to its weakness and lack of use, while ripeness displays the striking change that manifests divine power.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r15.anchor: اشعارا بأن المثمر حينئذ ضعيف غير منتفع به فيقابل حال الينع ويدل كمال التفاوت

ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r16.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r16.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says ثمره is not qualified as green because coordinating ripeness with fruit singles ripeness out as superior to unripe fruit, as in the mention of Gabriel and Michael.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240/r16.anchor: وعن الزمخشري أنه قال فان قلت هلا قيل : إلى غض ثمره وينعه قلت : في هذا الاسلوب فائدة

ALUSI-FULL:v7p240#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240#2/r1.claim: The demonstrative refers to what people were commanded to inspect; its distance form carries the nuance explained elsewhere.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240#2/r1.anchor: وما في اسم الاشارة من معنى البعد لما مر غير مرة

ALUSI-FULL:v7p240#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240#2/r2.claim: The signs are great or numerous proofs of the existence and oneness of a capable, wise creator.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240#2/r2.anchor: عظيمة أو كثيرة دالة على وجود القادر الحكيم ووحدته

ALUSI-FULL:v7p240#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240#2/r3.speaker: القاضي
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240#2/r3.claim: Al-Qadi takes the people who believe as those seeking faith in God.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240#2/r3.anchor: أي يطلبون الايمان بالله تعالى كما قال القاضي

ALUSI-FULL:v7p240#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240#2/r4.claim: Alternatively, these are already believers; they alone are specified because they benefit from the signs.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240#2/r4.anchor: أو مؤمنون بالفعل وتخصيصهم بالذكر لأنهم الذين انتفعوا بذلك دون غيرهم

ALUSI-FULL:v7p240#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240#2/r5.claim: Diverse kinds arising from one source and changing through ordered stages require a knowing creator who selects what wisdom favors, unhindered by rival or opponent.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p240#2/r5.anchor: حدوث هاتيك الاجناس المختلفة والانواع المتشعبة من أصل واحد وانتقالها من حال إلى حال على نمط بديع

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r1.claim: The pronoun in by it refers to water; in from it, the referent is either water or vegetation.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r1.anchor: أي من الماء، وقيل: من النبات، {خضرا}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r2.claim: Khadr means green, like the relation between al-awar and al-aʿwar, and denotes moist green growth such as wheat and barley.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r2.anchor: {خضرا} يعني: أخضر، مثل العور والأعور، يعني: ما كان رطبا أخضر مما ينبت من القمح والشعير ونحوهما،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r3.claim: The stacked grain includes ears of wheat, barley, rice, and other grains.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r3.anchor: حبا متراكبا} أي متراكما بعضه على بعض

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r4.claim: The talʿ is the first part of the date fruit to emerge.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r4.anchor: {ومن النخل من طلعها} والطلع أول ما يخرج من ثمر النخل،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r5.claim: Qinwan is the plural of qinw, a bunch, patterned like sinw and sinwan; the pair has no parallel in ordinary speech.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r5.anchor: {قنوان} جمع قنو وهو العذق، مثل صنو وصنوان، ولا نظير لهما في الكلام،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r6.claim: Daniya means close enough to reach whether standing or sitting.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r6.anchor: {دانية} أي: قريبة المتناول ينالها القائم والقاعد،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r7.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r7.claim: Mujahid explains the bunches as hanging down.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r8.speaker: الضحاك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r8.claim: Al-Dahhak says they are short and close to the ground.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r9.claim: The verse mentions nearby bunches while omitting distant ones because the latter are readily understood; 16:81 similarly mentions protection from heat while also meaning cold.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r9.anchor: وفيه اختصار معناه: ومن النخل ما قنوانها دانية ومنها ما هي بعيدة، فاكتفى بذكر القريبة عن البعيدة لسبقه إلى الأفهام،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r10.claim: The phrase means that God also brings forth grape gardens from the water.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r10.anchor: {وجنات من أعناب} أي: وأخرجنا منه جنات،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r11.speaker: الأعمش عن عاصم وعامة القراء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r11.claim: Al-Aʿmash's transmission from ʿAsim reads gardens in the nominative, coordinating it with qinwan; the majority read otherwise.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r11.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش عن عاصم " وجنات " بالرفع نسقا على قوله " قنوان " وعامة القراء على خلافه،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r12.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r12.claim: The reference is to olive trees and pomegranate trees.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r13.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r13.claim: Qatada says their leaves resemble one another while their fruits differ.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r13.anchor: قال قتادة: معناه مشتبها ورقها مختلفا ثمرها،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r14.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r14.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r14.claim: Another view says the fruits resemble one another in appearance but differ in taste.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r14.anchor: وقيل: مشتبه في المنظر مختلف في الطعم،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r15.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r15.speaker: حمزة والكسائي والآخرون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r15.claim: Hamza and al-Kisaʾi read thamar with both vowels rounded, meaning fruits; the others use both fatḥas, a collective singular like baqara and baqar.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r15.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي بضم الثاء والميم، هذا وما بعده وفي "يس" على جمع الثمار، وقرأ الآخرون [بفتحهما] (1) على جمع الثمرة،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r16.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r16.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r16.claim: Yunʿ means its ripening, maturity, and full development.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p172/r16.anchor: {إذا أثمر وينعه} ونضجه وإدراكه، {إن في ذلكم لآيات لقوم يؤمنون}

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r1.claim: The water was sent down from clouds or from the direction of the sky.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r1.anchor: من السحاب أو من جانب السماء

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r2.claim: The shift to the first-person plural is a change in the mode of address.

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r3.claim: The pronoun refers to the water.

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r4.claim: This means the growth of every kind of plant and displays God's power in producing diverse varieties watered by one water, as in the cited description of crops watered by one water yet differing in taste.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r4.anchor: إظهار القدرة في إنبات الأنواع المختلفة المفننة المسقية بماء واحد

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r5.claim: The pronoun may refer either to the plant or to the water.

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r6.claim: Khaḍir means something green, with the alternate forms akhḍar/khudr; it is the sprout emerging from the grain and branching out.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r6.anchor: شيئا أخضر يقال أخضر وخضر كأعور وعور، وهو الخارج من الحبة المتشعب

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r7.claim: The grain stacked in layers is grain growing from the green shoot, namely an ear of grain.

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r8.claim: The syntax may mean producing palms from palms, with bunches from their spathes, or producing bunches from palm spathes; alternatively min al-nakhl predicates qinwān and min ṭalʿihā is an appositive.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r8.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون من النخل خبر قنوان ومن طلعها بدل منه

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r9.claim: Qinwān are palm clusters, the plural of qinw, like ṣinwān as the plural of ṣinw.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r9.anchor: وهو الأعذاق جمع قنو كصنوان جمع صنو

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r10.claim: Qinwān is read with ḍamma on qāf, by analogy with dhiʾb/dhuʾbān, and with fatḥa as a collective noun, since fiʿlān is not a plural pattern.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r10.anchor: وقرىء بضم القاف كذئب وذؤبان وبفتحها على أنه اسم جمع

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r11.claim: The clusters are near enough to reach, or densely clustered close together; mentioning these alone implies their opposite and adds a mark of favor.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r11.anchor: قريبة من المتناول، أو ملتفة قريب بعضها من بعض

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r12.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r12.claim: Vineyards coordinate with 'the growth of every kind'; Nāfiʿ reads them nominative as a new subject with an implied predicate, but they cannot coordinate with palm clusters because grapes do not grow from palms.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r12.anchor: ولا يجوز عطفه على { قنون } إذ العنب لا يخرج من النخل

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r13.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r13.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r13.claim: Olives and pomegranates either coordinate with the plant growth or are accusatives of specification, because these two types were prized among the audience.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r13.anchor: أيضا عطف على نبات أو نصب على الاختصاص لعزة هذين الصنفين عندهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r14.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r14.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r14.claim: The description may modify the pomegranate or all the fruits: some resemble one another and others differ in shape, size, color, and taste.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r14.anchor: حال من الرمان، أو من الجميع أي بعض ذلك متشابه وبعضه غير متشابه

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r15.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r15.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r15.claim: The fruit to observe is the fruit of each of the plants just mentioned.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r15.anchor: أي ثمر كل واحد من ذلك

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r16.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r16.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r16.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read the tāʾ and mīm with ḍamma, treating thumur as a plural of thamarah or of thimār.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r16.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي بضم التاء والميم، وهو جمع ثمرة كخشبة وخشب

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r17.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r17.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r17.claim: At first fruiting, the fruit is tiny and scarcely useful; at ripening it becomes large, useful, and delicious.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r17.anchor: إذا أخرج ثمره كيف يثمر ضئيلا لا يكاد ينتفع به

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r18.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r18.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r18.claim: Yanʿ means the fruit's ripeness or its ripe state; it is originally the verbal noun of ripening, or a plural of yāniʿ, and is also read with ḍamma or as yāniʿ.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r18.anchor: وإلى حال نضجه أو إلى نضيجة كيف يعود ضخما ذا نفع ولذة

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r19.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r19.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r19.claim: The changing, diverse genera and kinds emerging from one source show a capable, wise, knowing creator who chooses among possible states and has no rival or opponent; the verse leads into rebuke of associating partners.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:99/r19.anchor: فإن حدوث الأجناس المختلفة والأنواع المتفننة من أصل واحد ونقلها من حال إلى حال

BIQAI-FULL:v2p684/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p684/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p684/r1.claim: After describing creative differentiation and the conditions that sustain life, the discourse names water as the proximate cause of living things and develops what was summarized as producing grain and kernels.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p684/r1.anchor: أتبعه سببه القريب , وهو الماء الذي جعل منه كل شيء حي , فقال مفصلا ما أجمله في الحب والنوى

BIQAI-FULL:v2p684/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p684/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p684/r2.claim: The water descends from the real, familiar sky and comes pouring down in a strong flow.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p684/r2.anchor: { من السماء } أي الحقيقية التي تعرفونها كما دل عليه صريح العبارة وما أشبهها من ذكور الحيوان المنبه عليه بطريق الإشارة { ماء } أي منهمرا ودافقا

BIQAI-FULL:v2p684/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p684/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p684/r3.claim: The narration shifts to God's majestic first-person plural because bringing creation forth from water is too great for anyone else to reach.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p684/r3.anchor: نبه عليه بالانقال إلى التكلم في مظهر العظمة فقال : { فأخرجنا } أي على ما لنا من العظمة التي لا يدانيها أحد

BIQAI-FULL:v2p684/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p684/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p684/r4.claim: One water produces many plants with differing tastes, colors, scents, natures, and uses; the phrase also extends figuratively to offspring from male and female.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p684/r4.anchor: مختلفة طعومه وألوانه وروائحه وطبائعه ومنافعه وهو بماء واحد , فالسبب واحد والمسببات كثيرة منفتة

BIQAI-FULL:v2p684/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p684/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p684/r5.claim: The green growth is tender, fresh plant matter branching from the plant's root, itself arising from the seed.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p684/r5.anchor: خضرا } أي شيئا أخضر غضا طريا , وهو ما تشعب من أصل النبات الخارج من الحبة

BIQAI-FULL:v2p684/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p684/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p684/r6.claim: Grain grows in overlapping ears, protected from birds by husks and fine, long, rough bristles; from a single seed or scattered earth it passes through stages, proving a sovereign Creator.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p684/r6.anchor: حبا متراكبا } أي في السنبل يركب بعضه بعضا ويحرسه من أن يلتقطه الطير بعد ستره بالقشر

BIQAI-FULL:v2p684/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p684/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p684/r7.claim: Having emphasized that God alone brings forth grain, the passage turns from grain to the date palm and its kernel.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p684/r7.anchor: وبدأ بما بدأ به أولا في آية الفلق من الحب ؛ ثنى بما من النوى , فقال معبرا لذلك الأسلوب

BIQAI-FULL:v2p685/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p685/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p685/r1.claim: Putting grain before dates here and earlier indicates that grain is superior as staple food for most regions and animals; nourishment takes precedence over fruit.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p685/r1.anchor: وتقديم الحب عليه هنا وفيما قبل يدل على أن الزرع أفضل منه , فإنه قوت في أكثر البلاد

BIQAI-FULL:v2p685/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p685/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p685/r2.claim: طلع is the palm's first growth within its sheaths; قنوان is plural of قنو, a bunch or cluster, and دانية means within easy reach despite the tall trunk.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p685/r2.anchor: من طلعها } أي النخل , وهو أول ما يخرج منها في أكمامه { قنوان } جمع قنو , وهو العذق

BIQAI-FULL:v2p685/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p685/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p685/r3.claim: Grape gardens are plural for their many varieties; grapes are more excellent as fruit, useful from sour green tendrils and unripe grapes to fresh fruit, preserves, raisins, syrup, vinegar, and medicinal preparations.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p685/r3.anchor: { وجنات } أي بساتين { من أعناب } وجمعها لكثرة أنواعها , وبدأ بهاتين الشجرتين

BIQAI-FULL:v2p685/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p685/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p685/r4.claim: Dates are listed first because they are Arabs' staple and resemble humans in properties more than other plants; grapes follow as a noble fruit, though Arabs handle palms more closely.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p685/r4.anchor: وقدم النخيل لأنها قوت للعرب , وبينها وبين الإنسان مشابهة في خواص كثيرة لا توجد في النبات , ولذا جاء في الحديث

BIQAI-FULL:v2p685/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p685/r5.speaker: علي
BIQAI-FULL:v2p685/r5.claim: Ali transmits a report attributed to the Prophet calling the date palm humanity's paternal aunt, saying it was created from Adam's clay, and noting that it alone among trees is pollinated.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p685/r5.anchor: رواه أبو يعلى وأبو نعيم في الحلية وأبو الشيخ عن علي رضي الله عنه

BIQAI-FULL:v2p686/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p686/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p686/r1.claim: Olive follows because it has many uses, yielding valuable oil for food, light, and other applications.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p686/r1.anchor: { والزيتون } و قدمه لكثرة نفعه , وينفصل منه دهن عظيم النفع في الأكل والضياء

BIQAI-FULL:v2p686/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p686/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p686/r2.claim: Pomegranate is last for its beauty and great benefit: rind, pith, and seeds are cold, dry, earthy, and astringent, while its juice is opposite, agreeable, near balance, and both food and medicine.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p686/r2.anchor: { والرمان } ختم به لحسنه وعظيم نفعه , وهو مركب من أربعة أشياء : قشره وشحمه وعجمه ومائه , فالثلاثة

BIQAI-FULL:v2p686/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p686/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p686/r3.claim: Fruits and staples resemble and differ despite sharing water and soil, proving divine power and choice, supporting God's oneness and resurrection, and refuting partners who would need equal power in shared acts.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p686/r3.anchor: وكان اشتباه بعضها واختلاف بعضها - مع كونها تسقى بماء واحد وفي أرض واحدة - دالا على القدرة والاختيار

BIQAI-FULL:v2p686/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p686/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p686/r4.claim: Mشتبه describes extreme likeness: fruit from separate trees can be so similar that one cannot distinguish which tree produced it.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p686/r4.anchor: { مشتبها } أي في غاية الشبه بعضه لبعض حتى لا يكاد يتميز

BIQAI-FULL:v2p686/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p686/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p686/r5.claim: The paired wording uses ellipsis by احتباك: the first term implies absence of likeness, while the second denies actively seeking likeness, rebutting claims that natural properties act independently.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p686/r5.anchor: فالآية من الاحتباك : أثبت الاشتباه دلالة على نفي ضده , وهو عدم التشابه

BIQAI-FULL:v2p686/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p686/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p686/r6.claim: The command focuses on visible fruit as evidence for resurrection and unity; the later parallel in 6:141 addresses eating and charity while refuting Arab idol practices and self-imposed prohibitions.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p686/r6.anchor: علق الأمر بالنظر الذي هو أثبت الحواس , ودلالة على أن المراد إنما هو ظاهر ذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v2p687/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p687/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p687/r1.claim: The fruit at first appearance is weak and of little or no benefit; ينع refers to its ripening when it is ready for harvest.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p687/r1.anchor: { إذا أثمر } أي حين يبدو من كمامه ضعيفا قليل النفع أو عديمه { وينعه } أي وانظروا إلى إدراكه إذ أدرك

BIQAI-FULL:v2p687/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p687/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p687/r2.claim: Observing fruit from its first appearance to ripeness reveals intervening changes in color, size, taste, shape, and tree form; because seasons and natural elements affect them equally, only a freely acting Creator explains the changes.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p687/r2.anchor: فاستناد هذه التبدلات والتغيرات ليس إلا إلى الفاعل المختار , لأن نسبته إلى الطبائع والفصول على حد سواء

BIQAI-FULL:v2p687/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p687/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p687/r3.claim: These remarkable transformations are signs of the Maker's power and choice; believers renew their faith whenever they reflect on God's works, while signs do not benefit the doomed.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p687/r3.anchor: { لقوم يؤمنون * } أي حكم بأنهم - بحذقهم ونشاطهم وقوتهم على ما يحاولونه - يجددون الإيمان

BIQAI-FULL:v2p687/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p687/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p687/r4.claim: The account from splitting dawn onward elaborates the earlier statement that God splits grain and kernels, establishing power, oneness, and resurrection before returning to denounce idolatry.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p687/r4.anchor: وكان هذا كله في قوله { فالق الإصباح } شرحا لآية { إن الله فالق الحب والنوى }

BURSEVI:v3p56#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p56#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p56#3/r2.claim: The water sent from heaven is specifically rain.
BURSEVI:v3p56#3/r2.anchor: {الذى أنزل من السمآء مآء} خاصا هو المطر

BURSEVI:v3p56#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p56#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p56#3/r3.claim: The shift from speaking of God in the third person to 'We brought forth' uses the plural of majesty, not a plural of number.
BURSEVI:v3p56#3/r3.anchor: فالنون للعظمة لا الجمع فإن الملك العظيم

BURSEVI:v3p56#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p56#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p56#3/r4.claim: The rain produces plants such as wheat, barley, pomegranate, and apple; 'every thing' is restricted to what grows, not stones or other non-growing things.
BURSEVI:v3p56#3/r4.anchor: ينبت كنبات الحنطة والشعير والرمان والتفاح

BURSEVI:v3p56#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p56#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p56#3/r5.claim: Nabt and nabat mean growth from the earth, whether a woody tree with a trunk or a plant without one.
BURSEVI:v3p56#3/r5.anchor: والنبت والنبات ما يخرج من الأرض من الناميات سواء كان له ساق كالشجر

BURSEVI:v3p56#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p56#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p56#3/r6.claim: An objection asks whether making rain a cause means God needs instruments; Bursevī answers that rain leads to growth but does not generate it, and God can grow plants without rain.
BURSEVI:v3p56#3/r6.anchor: لأن المطر سبب يؤدي إلى النبات وليس بمولود له والله تعالى قادر على إنبات النبات بدون المطر

BURSEVI:v3p56#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p56#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p56#3/r7.claim: An agent needs a means only when the action is impossible without it; a ladder is not necessary for climbing a roof if the climber can ascend without one.
BURSEVI:v3p56#3/r7.anchor: إنما يكون الفاعل بالسبب مستعينا بذلك السبب إذا لم يمكنه فعل ذلك الشيء إلا بذلك السبب

BURSEVI:v3p57/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p57/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p57/r1.claim: The verse now unpacks the general statement about bringing forth: it first describes tender growth from plants without trunks.
BURSEVI:v3p57/r1.anchor: {فأخرجنا منه} شروع في تفصيل ما أجمل من الإخراج وقد بدأ بتفصيل حال النجم

BURSEVI:v3p57/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p57/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p57/r2.claim: Khiḍr means green: the fresh green growth that branches from the plant emerging from a seed.
BURSEVI:v3p57/r2.anchor: {خضرا} بمعنى أخضر وهو ، الشيء الأخضر الخارج من النبات ما تشعب

BURSEVI:v3p57/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p57/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p57/r3.claim: The clause describes khiḍr; grain is brought forth from that branching green growth.
BURSEVI:v3p57/r3.anchor: {نخرج منه} صفة لخضرا أي نخرج من ذلك الخضر المتشعب

BURSEVI:v3p57/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p57/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p57/r4.claim: The stacked grain refers to an ear of grain, whose kernels are arranged one above another in a particular form.
BURSEVI:v3p57/r4.anchor: {حبا متراكبا} هو السنبل المنتظم للحبوب المتراكبة بعضها فوق بعض

BURSEVI:v3p57/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p57/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p57/r5.claim: The discussion turns from herbaceous plants to trees, and the phrase is a fronted predicate.

BURSEVI:v3p57/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p57/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p57/r6.claim: Min ṭalʿihā is an apposition repeating the preposition; the palm spathe resembles two folded sandals with fruit packed between them.
BURSEVI:v3p57/r6.anchor: {من طلعها} بدل منه بإعادة العامل وهو وشيء يخرج من النخل كأنه نعلان مطبقان

BURSEVI:v3p57/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p57/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p57/r7.claim: Qinwān is the plural of qinw, a palm fruit cluster analogous to a grape cluster.
BURSEVI:v3p57/r7.anchor: {قنوان} مبتدأ ، أي : وحاصلة من طلع النخل قنوان جمع قنو وهو للثمر بمنزلة العنقود للعنب

BURSEVI:v3p57/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p57/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p57/r8.claim: The clusters are easy to pick and near the picker; the wording omits distant clusters because proximity makes the blessing greater.
BURSEVI:v3p57/r8.anchor: {دانية} سهلة المجتنى قريبة من القاطف فإنها وإن كانت صغيرة ينالها القاعد

BURSEVI:v3p57/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p57/r9.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v3p57/r9.claim: A report urges honoring palm trees, says they were made from the surplus clay of Adam, and calls the tree exceptionally honored.
BURSEVI:v3p57/r9.anchor: أكرموا عماتكم النخل فإنها خلقت من فضلة طينة آدم

BURSEVI:v3p57/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p57/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p57/r10.claim: Mary first ate fresh dates after giving birth to Jesus, which explains the recommendation to give dates to postpartum women.
BURSEVI:v3p57/r10.anchor: فظهر أن السبب في إطعام النفساء رطبا أن مريم رضي الله عنها كان أول ما أكلت

BURSEVI:v3p57/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p57/r11.speaker: بعض الأنبياء
BURSEVI:v3p57/r11.claim: A report says a prophet complained that his community's children were unattractive; God told him to have pregnant women eat quince in months three and four to beautify the child.
BURSEVI:v3p57/r11.anchor: أنه شكا بعض الأنبياء إلى الله تعالى من قبح أولاد أمته

BURSEVI:v3p57/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p57/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p57/r12.claim: Gardens of grapes are coordinated with the phrase نبات كل شيء.
BURSEVI:v3p57/r12.anchor: {من أعناب} فهو عطف على نبات كل شيء

BURSEVI:v3p57/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p57/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p57/r13.claim: The verse specifies grape gardens rather than merely naming the species because grapes are generally useful when many plants grow together.
BURSEVI:v3p57/r13.anchor: ولعل زيادة الجنات هنا من غير اكتفاء بذكر اسم الجنس كما فيما تقدم وما تأخر

BURSEVI:v3p57/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p57/r14.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p57/r14.claim: A dense growth that conceals parts of itself is called a jannah, from the root meaning concealment; aʿnāb is the plural of ʿinab, Persian angūr.
BURSEVI:v3p57/r14.anchor: وكل نبت متكاثف يستر بعضه بعضا فهو جنة من جن إذا استتر

BURSEVI:v3p57#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p57#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p57#2/r1.claim: God also brought forth olive trees and pomegranate trees.
BURSEVI:v3p57#2/r1.anchor: {والزيتون والرمان} أي : وأخرجنا أيضا شجر الزيتون وشجر الرمان

BURSEVI:v3p57#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p57#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p57#2/r2.claim: The olive and pomegranate foliage resembles one another and covers the branches from beginning to end.
BURSEVI:v3p57#2/r2.anchor: {مشتبها} أوراقهما ومشتملا على الغصن من أوله إلى آخره في كليهما

BURSEVI:v3p57#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p57#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p57#2/r3.claim: The fruits differ in taste: some are very sour, some sweet, and some both sour and sweet.

BURSEVI:v3p57#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p57#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p57#2/r4.claim: The Persian gloss likewise takes the trees' leaves as similar and their fruits as different in taste.
BURSEVI:v3p57#2/r4.anchor: در حالتي كه آن درختان بعضي ببعضي ما نند دربرك

BURSEVI:v3p57#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p57#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p57#2/r5.claim: The command is to look with reflective consideration.

BURSEVI:v3p57#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p57#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p57#2/r6.claim: Observe the fruit when it first appears, still tiny and scarcely useful, and when it ripens, becoming large, useful, and pleasant.
BURSEVI:v3p57#2/r6.anchor: كيف يخرجه ضئيلا لا يكاد ينتفع به

BURSEVI:v3p57#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p57#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p57#2/r7.claim: Yanaʿ is originally the verbal noun for a fruit coming to maturity.
BURSEVI:v3p57#2/r7.anchor: والينع في الأصل مصدر ينعت الثمرة إذا أدركت

BURSEVI:v3p57#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p57#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p57#2/r8.claim: The time clause modifies the command to look, directing attention to the fruit's first appearance and full ripeness.
BURSEVI:v3p57#2/r8.anchor: وقوله إذا أثمر ظرف لقوله انظروا أمر بالنظر في أول حال حدوث الثمرة

BURSEVI:v3p57#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p57#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p57#2/r9.claim: Fruit changes from one state to its opposite despite growing in the same soil and receiving the same water; this points to the wise, merciful, all-knowing power directing creation.
BURSEVI:v3p57#2/r9.anchor: مع كونها نابتة من أرض واحدة ومسقية بماء واحد

BURSEVI:v3p57#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p57#2/r10.speaker: القرطبي
BURSEVI:v3p57#2/r10.claim: Al-Qurṭubī says ripeness is the condition for a valid fruit sale: the fruit must be fit to eat and safe from blight.
BURSEVI:v3p57#2/r10.anchor: قال القرطبي : هذا الينع هو الذي يتوقف عليه جواز بيع الثمرة

BURSEVI:v3p57#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p57#2/r11.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v3p57#2/r11.claim: Abū Hurayra transmits the Prophet's report that morning rising of the Pleiades lifts blight from a town; the author dates this to the twelfth of May.
BURSEVI:v3p57#2/r11.anchor: روى أبو هريرة عن النبي عليه السلام أنه قال

BURSEVI:v3p57#2/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p57#2/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p57#2/r12.claim: The signs refer to the phenomena people were told to observe; they prove the existence and oneness of the almighty, wise Creator, and believers are named because they benefit from the inference.
BURSEVI:v3p57#2/r12.anchor: إشار إلى ما أمر بالنظر إليه

BURSEVI:v3p57#2/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p57#2/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p57#2/r13.claim: In the inward reading, rain from the heaven of divine care is guidance that yields kinds of gnosis and secrets suited to people's spiritual ranks; the heart is a garden growing what it is prepared for.
BURSEVI:v3p57#2/r13.anchor: إن الله تعالى ينزل من سماء العناية ماء الهداية فيخرج به أنواع المعارف والأسرار

DURR-FULL:v3p331#2/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p331#2/r13.speaker: البراء بن عازب
DURR-FULL:v3p331#2/r13.claim: Al-Bara says qinwān dāniya means near clusters.
DURR-FULL:v3p331#2/r13.anchor: عن البراء بن عازب {قنوان دانية} قال: قريبة

DURR-FULL:v3p333/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p333/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p333/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the phrase as short palm trees whose fruit clusters touch the ground.
DURR-FULL:v3p333/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس {قنوان دانية} قال: قصار النخل اللاصقة عذوقها بالأرض

DURR-FULL:v3p333/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p333/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p333/r2.claim: Another Ibn Abbas gloss calls qinwān the palm clusters and dāniya the upright ones.
DURR-FULL:v3p333/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس {قنوان} الكبائس والدانية المنصوبة

DURR-FULL:v3p333/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p333/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p333/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas also describes the clusters as drooping from the palm spathes.
DURR-FULL:v3p333/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {قنوان دانية} قال: تهدل العذوق من الطلع

DURR-FULL:v3p333/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p333/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v3p333/r4.claim: Qatada defines qinwān as palm clusters and dāniya as hanging down.
DURR-FULL:v3p333/r4.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {قنوان} قال: عذوق النخل {دانية} قال: متهدلة يعني متدلية

DURR-FULL:v3p333/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p333/r5.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v3p333/r5.claim: Qatada says the plants resemble one another in their leaves but differ in their fruits.
DURR-FULL:v3p333/r5.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {مشتبها وغير متشابه} قال: مشتبها ورقه مختلفا ثمره

DURR-FULL:v3p333/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p333/r6.speaker: محمد بن كعب
DURR-FULL:v3p333/r6.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka'b glosses the fruit as fresh dates and grapes.
DURR-FULL:v3p333/r6.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب في قوله {انظروا إلى ثمره إذا أثمر} قال: رطبه وعنبه

DURR-FULL:v3p333/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p333/r7.speaker: عاصم
DURR-FULL:v3p333/r7.claim: Asim recited thamar with fatḥa on both thāʾ and mīm, and yanʿihi with fatḥa on the yāʾ.
DURR-FULL:v3p333/r7.anchor: عن عاصم أنه قرأ (انظروا إلى ثمره) بنصب الثاء والميم (وينعه) بنصب الياء

DURR-FULL:v3p333/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p333/r8.speaker: محمد مسعر
DURR-FULL:v3p333/r8.claim: Muhammad Mas'ar says people are obligated, when fruits appear, to bring them out and look at them, citing this command.
DURR-FULL:v3p333/r8.anchor: عن محمد مسعر قال: فرضا على الناس إذا أخرجت الثمار أن يخرجوا وينظروا إليها

DURR-FULL:v3p333/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p333/r9.speaker: البراء
DURR-FULL:v3p333/r9.claim: Al-Bara glosses yanʿihi as its ripening.

DURR-FULL:v3p333/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p333/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p333/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses yanʿihi as its ripening.

DURR-FULL:v3p333/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p333/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p333/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas defines yanʿihi as ripeness and full development, and cites an unnamed poet's use of yāniʿ for a supple, fruiting branch as Arabic evidence.
DURR-FULL:v3p333/r11.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن نافع بن الأزرق قال له: أخبرني عن قوله {وينعه} قال: نضجه وبلاغه

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1358/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1358/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1358/r1.claim: He says no raindrop descends except by a measured balance.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1358/r1.anchor: عن عبد الجليل عن شهر ابن حوشب ان أبا هريرة قال : ما نزل قطر الا بميزان

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1358/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1358/r2.speaker: عكرمة
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1358/r2.claim: He says water descends from the seventh heaven and a drop falls on a cloud like a camel.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1358/r2.anchor: عن عكرمة قال : ينزل الله الماء من السماء السابعة فتقع القطرة منه علي السحابة مثل البعير

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1358/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1358/r3.speaker: خالد بن يزيد
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1358/r3.claim: At ʿAbd al-Malik's gathering, he distinguished rain from clouds fed by the sea and said thunder and lightning sweeten that water; sea-derived water produces no plants, which come from water from the sky.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1358/r3.anchor: عن خالد بن يزيد قال : كان عند عبد الملك بن مروان فذكروا الماء ، فقال خالد بن يزيد : منه من السماء

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1358/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1358/r4.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1358/r4.claim: He identifies the stacked grain as the ear of grain.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1358/r4.anchor: عن السدى : قوله : فاخرجنا منه خضرا نخرج منه حبا متراكبا قال : السنبل

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1358/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1358/r5.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1358/r5.claim: He describes the palms as growing close to the ground.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1358/r5.anchor: عن الضحاك في قوله : ومن النخل من طلعها : يعني النخل الملتزقة بالارض

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1358/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1358/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1358/r6.claim: He explains the low-hanging clusters as short palms whose bunches nearly touch the ground.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1358/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس : قوله : ومن النخل من طلعها قنوان دانية يعني بالقنوان الدانية : قصار النخل اللاصقة عذوقها بالارض

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1358/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1358/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1358/r7.claim: He glosses qinwān as palm clusters (kabāʾis).
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1358/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس : قوله : قنوان دانية قال : قنوان الكبائس

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1358/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1358/r8.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1358/r8.claim: He glosses qinwān as the clusters of dates on a palm.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1358/r8.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله : قنوان دانية قال : قنوان عذوق النخل

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1358/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1358/r9.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1358/r9.claim: He glosses qinwān as the palm's spathe.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1358/r9.anchor: عن الضحاك في قوله : قنوان دانية : يعني بالقنوان الطلع

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1359/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1359/r1.speaker: البراء بن عازب
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1359/r1.anchor: عن البراء بن عازب : قنوان دانية قال قريبة

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1359/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1359/r2.speaker: السدي عن ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1359/r2.claim: He explains dāniya as upright or set up.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1359/r2.anchor: عن السدى عن ابن عباس قوله : دانية ، والدانية المنصوبة

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1359/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1359/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1359/r3.claim: He describes the clusters as hanging down from the palm's spathe.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1359/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس : قوله : قنوان دانية قال : دانية ، تهدل العذوق من الطلع

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1359/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1359/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1359/r4.claim: He says the clusters hang down; the author clarifies that this means they are drooping.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1359/r4.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله : قنوان دانية يقول : دانية ، متهدلة

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1359/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1359/r5.speaker: author
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1359/r5.claim: The author explains Qatada's “drooping” as “hanging down.”

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1359/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1359/r6.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1359/r6.claim: The leaves are alike while the fruits differ.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1359/r6.anchor: عن قتادة : قوله : متشبها وغير متشابه ، يقال متشابها ورقة مختلفا ثمره

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1359/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1359/r7.speaker: محمد بن كعب
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1359/r7.claim: He takes the fruit when it bears to mean fresh dates and grapes.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1359/r7.anchor: عن موسى بن عبيدة عن محمد بن كعب : انظروا إلى ثمره اذا اثمر قال رطبه وعنبه

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1359/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1359/r8.speaker: البراء بن عازب
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1359/r8.claim: He glosses the fruit's ripening as its maturity when it ripens.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1359/r8.anchor: عن البراء : انظروا إلى ثمره اذا اثمر وينعه قال : نضجه حين ينضج

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1359/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1359/r9.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي والضحاك وعطاء الخرساني وقتادة وعبد الله بن أبي اسحاق البصري
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1359/r9.claim: These authorities are reported to give the same ripeness or maturity explanation.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1359/r9.anchor: وروى عن ابن عباس والسدى والضحاك وعطاء الخرساني وقتادة وعبد الله بن أبي اسحاق البصري مثل ذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p397#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p397#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p397#2/r5.claim: The restrictive form “He is the one who sent down” follows the same explanation as the corresponding wording in the preceding verse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p397#2/r5.anchor: القول في صيغة القصر من قوله : { وهو الذى أنزل } إلخ كالقول في نظيره السابق .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p397#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p397#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p397#2/r6.claim: “From the sky” marks origin: rain forms in cold upper atmospheric layers as rising earthly vapor condenses into clouds and then becomes water; “sky” means the highest rain-forming layers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p397#2/r6.anchor: لأن ماء المطر يتكون في طبقات الجو العليا الزمهريرية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p397#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p397#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p397#2/r7.claim: He links this wording to the earlier Qur'anic phrase about a downpour from the sky in al-Baqara.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p397#2/r7.anchor: وتقدم في قوله تعالى : { أو كصيب من السماء في سورة البقرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p397#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p397#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p397#2/r8.claim: The verse shifts from third-person reference to first-person plural in “We brought forth,” an instance of iltifāt.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p397#2/r8.anchor: وعدل عن ضمير الغيبة إلى ضمير التكلم في قوله : فأخرجنا } على طريقة الإلتفات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p397#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p397#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p397#2/r9.claim: The bāʾ is causal: God made water the cause of plant growth, and its attached pronoun refers to the water.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p397#2/r9.anchor: والباء للسببية جعل الله الماء سببا لخروج النبات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p397#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p397#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p397#2/r10.claim: Nabāt names what grows; originally a verbal noun of nabata, it became a common figurative name for the growing plant and now also denotes the source noun itself.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p397#2/r10.anchor: والنبات اسم لما ينبت ، وهو اسم مصدر نبت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399/r1.claim: “Each thing” means each plant species, as the annexation indicates; the clause means that water brings forth all kinds of vegetation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399/r1.anchor: و { شيء } مراد به صنف من النبات بقرينة إضافة { نبات } إليه . والمعنى : فأخرجنا بالماء ما ينبت من أصناف النبت .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399/r2.claim: The kinds include crops with soft stems, trees with thick stems such as palms and grapes, and low-growing herbage that lies against the soil.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399/r2.anchor: ومنه نجم وأب وهو ما ينبت لاصقا بالتراب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399/r3.claim: The general wording points to plants' diverse qualities, fruits, natures, properties, and tastes despite their common origin in rainwater, a sign of God's immense power.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399/r3.anchor: وهذا التعميم يشير إلى أنها مختلفة الصفات والثمرات والطبائع والخصوصيات والمذاق ، وهي كلها نابتة من ماء السماء الذي هو واحد ، وذلك آية على عظم القدرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
