IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399/r4.claim: He connects the variety despite one water source to 13:4, which says plants are watered with one water while some are favored over others in food.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399/r4.anchor: قال تعالى : { تسقى بماء واحد ونفضل بعضها على بعضض في الأكل }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399/r5.claim: The diversity invites people to consider the subtle different powers God deposited in plants that cause their varying conditions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399/r5.anchor: وهو تنبيه للناس ليعتبروا بدقائق ما أودعه الله فيها من مختلف القوى التي سببت اختلاف أحوالها .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399/r6.claim: The fāʾ in “then He brought forth by it every plant” marks consequence or elaboration.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399/r6.anchor: والفاء في قوله : { فأخرجنا به نبات كل شيء } فاء التفريع .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399#2/r1.claim: The second “then” elaborates the general bringing-forth; min may be partitive or indicate origin, its pronoun refers to vegetation, and the phrase divides the genus into kinds.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399#2/r1.anchor: وقوله : { فأخرجنا منه خضرا } تفصيل لمضمون جملة { فأخرجنا به نبات كل شيء } ، فالفاء للتفصيل ، و ( من ) ابتدائية أو تبعيضية ، والضمير المجرور بها عائد إلى النبات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399#2/r2.claim: Khudr can mean something green or, as intended here, moist nonwoody growth such as young fodder and tender shoots, since grain grows from it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399#2/r2.anchor: ويطلق الخضر اسما للنبت الرطب الذي ليس بشجر كالقصيل والقضب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399#2/r3.claim: He cites a hadith describing spring growth as sometimes killing through overeating, except for the creature that eats greenery until its flanks extend; he gives no grading.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399#2/r3.anchor: وفي الحديث : ( وإن مما ينبت الربيع لما يقتل حبطا أو يلم إلا آكلة الخضر أكلت حتى إذا امتدت خاصرتاها ) الحديث .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399#2/r4.claim: “We bring forth from it” is an adjectival clause for khudran, which has become a noun; min is connective or originative, with its pronoun returning to khudran.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399#2/r4.anchor: وجملة : { نخرج منه } صفة لقوله { خضرا } لأنه صار اسما ، و ( من ) اتصالية أو ابتدائية ، والضمير المجرور بها عائد إلى { خضرا } .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399#2/r5.claim: Ḥabb is the plant's fruit, including wheat, barley, and all cultivated grains.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399#2/r5.anchor: والحب : هو ثمر النبات ، كالبر والشعير والزراريع كلها .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399#2/r6.claim: Mutarākib means grains attached one upon another in an ear; its reciprocal pattern intensifies their piling together.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399#2/r6.anchor: والمتراكب : الملتصق بعضه على بعض في السنبلة ، مثل القمح وغيره ، والتفاعل للمبالغة في ركوب بعضه بعضا .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399#2/r7.claim: The date-palm clause is coordinated to “then We brought forth green growth,” though it may be parenthetical with an interrupting wāw; “from the palms” is the fronted predicate and “clusters” the delayed subject.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399#2/r7.anchor: وجملة : { ومن النخل من طلعها قنوان دانية } عطف على { فأخرجنا منه خضرا } . ويجوز أن تكون معترضة والواو اعتراضية ، وقوله : { من النخل } خبر مقدم و { قنوان } مبتدأ مؤخر .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399#2/r8.claim: The clause marvels at the beautiful clusters emerging from the palm spathe; its position among the other clauses also conveys their lesson and blessing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399#2/r8.anchor: والمقصود بالإخبار هنا التعجيب من خروج القنوان من الطلع وما فيه من بهجة ، وبهذا يظهر وجه تغيير أسلوب هذه الجملة عن أساليب ما قبلها وما بعدها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399#2/r9.claim: The generic definite article marks the familiar date palm, the Arabs' characteristic tree whose fruit was their staple and whose groves delighted them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399#2/r9.anchor: والتعريف في { النخل } تعريف العهد الجنسي ، وإنما جيء بالتعريف فيه للإشارة إلى أنه الجنس المألوف المعهود للعرب ، فإن النخل شجرهم وثمره قوتهم وحوائطه منبسط نفوسهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399#2/r10.claim: He allows an alternative circumstantial parse linked to the palm phrase, on the basis of lexical definiteness, by analogy with the later olive-and-pomegranate wording.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399#2/r10.anchor: ولك أن تجعله حالا من { النخل } اعتدادا بالتعريف اللفظي كقوله { والزيتون والرمان مشتبها }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399#2/r11.claim: “From its spathe” can be a partitive apposition to “the palms,” repeating the preposition used with the word it replaces.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p399#2/r11.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون { من طلعها } بدل بعض من { النخل } بإعادة حرف الجر الداخل على المبدل منه .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401/r1.claim: “Of grapes” is a genitive explanatory specification, since gardens are measured by their grapevines; this explains why the verse says gardens rather than grapes in gardens.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401/r1.anchor: وقوله : { من أعناب } تمييز مجرور ب { من } البيانية لأن الجنات للأعناب بمنزلة المقادير كما يقال جريت تمرا ، وبهذا الاعتبار عدي فعل الإخراج إلى الجنات دون الأعناب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401/r2.claim: Aʿnāb is the plural of ʿinab, itself a plural of ʿinaba; the original sense is the fruit of the grapevine.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401/r2.anchor: والأعناب جمع عنب ، وهو جمع عنبة ، وهو في الأصل ثمر شجر الكرم .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401/r3.claim: The word ʿinab also came to denote the vine by ellipsis of “tree,” an ellipsis that became so common it was forgotten.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401/r3.anchor: ويطلق على شجرة الكرم عنب على تقدير مضاف ، أي شجرة عنب ، وشاع ذلك فتنوسي المضاف .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401/r4.speaker: الراغب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401/r4.claim: Al-Rāghib says ʿinab names both the grape fruit and the vine itself.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401/r4.anchor: قال الراغب : ( العنب يقال لثمرة الكرم وللكرم نفسه ) اه .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401/r5.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr knows no Arabic use of singular ʿinaba for a vine, but says the plurals ʿinab and aʿnāb can denote vines, as in 80:27–28.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401/r5.anchor: ولا يعرف إطلاق المفرد على شجرة الكرم ، فلم أر في كلامهم إطلاق العنبة بالإفراد على شجرة الكرم ولكن يطلق بالجمع ، يقال : عنب ، مراد به الكرم ، كما في قوله تعالى : { فأنبتنا فيها حبا وعنبا }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401/r6.claim: He reads al-Rāghib's final wording as implying that singular ʿinaba can mean a vine tree.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401/r6.anchor: وظاهر كلام الراغب أنه يقال : عنبة لشجرة الكرم ، فإنه قال : ( العنب يقال لثمرة الكرم وللكرم نفسه الواحدة عنبة )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401#2/r1.claim: Olives and pomegranates are accusative, coordinated with the gardens; their definite articles are generic, as with the date palms.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401#2/r1.anchor: { والزيتون والرمان } بالنصب عطف على { جنات } والتعريف فيهما الجنس كالتعريف في قوله : { ومن النخل } .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401#2/r2.claim: The names originally designate the fruits but here denote the trees, just as with grapes.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401#2/r2.anchor: والمراد بالزيتون والرمان شجرهما . وهما في الأصل اسمان للثمرتين ثم أطلقا على شجرتيهما كما تقدم في الأعناب .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401#2/r3.claim: Though less central than palms to Arab life, the trees were scarce in Arab lands and prized for their fruit and ownership, so they are cited as signs of divine craft and grace.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401#2/r3.anchor: وهاتان الشجرتان وإن لم تكونا مثل النخل في الأهمية عند العرب إلا أنهما لعزة وجودهما في بلاد العرب ولتنافس العرب في التفكه بثمرهما والإعجاب باقتنائهما ذكرا في مقام التذكير بعجيب صنع الله تعالى ومنته .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401#2/r4.claim: Olives grew in Syria and Sinai, while pomegranates grew in al-Ṭāʾif.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401#2/r4.anchor: وكانت شجرة الزيتون موجودة بالشام وفي سينا ، وشجرة الرمان موجودة بالطائف .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401#2/r5.claim: The two expressions are coordinated circumstantial predicates, and the wāw marks division because one thing cannot be both alike and unlike; some are alike and some differ.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401#2/r5.anchor: وقوله : { مشتبها وغير متشابه } حال ومعطوف عليه ، والواو للتقسيم بقرينة أن الشيء الواحد لا يكون مشتبها وغير متشابه ، أي بعضه مشتبه وبعضه غير متشابه .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401#2/r6.claim: Both circumstantial expressions apply jointly to olives and pomegranates, and are singular because the grammatical wording is singular.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401#2/r6.anchor: وهما حالان من ( الزيتون والرمان ) معا ، وإنما أفرد ولم يجمع اعتبارا بإفراد اللفظ .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401#2/r7.claim: Tashābuh and ishtibāh are synonymous, both derived from shabah.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401#2/r7.anchor: والتشابه والاشتباه مترادفان كالتساوي والاستواء ، وهما مشتقان من الشبه .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401#2/r8.claim: The paired synonyms vary the expression to avoid repetition; the final form also makes a more fitting stopping point through its extended sound.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401#2/r8.anchor: والجمع بينهما في الآية للتفنن كراهية إعادة اللفظ ، ولأن اسم الفاعل من التشابه أسعد بالوقف لما فيه من مد الصوت بخلاف { مشتبه } . وهذا من بديع الفصاحة .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401#2/r9.claim: Similarity means matching in one feature while differing in others; plants or fruits may resemble or differ in the colors, tastes, or forms people seek according to their varying preferences.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401#2/r9.anchor: والتشابه : التماثل في حالة مع الاختلاف في غيرها من الأحوال ، أي بعض شجره يشبه بعضا وبعضه لا يشبه بعضا ، أو بعض ثمره يشبه بعضا وبعضه لا يشبه بعضا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401#2/r10.claim: Their similarity and difference point to deliberate creation and choice rather than accident.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401#2/r10.anchor: والمقصود من التقييد بهذه الحال التنبيه على أنها مخلوقة بالقصد والاختيار لا بالصدفة .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401#2/r11.claim: He relates the comparison of plant varieties to 13:4, which notes that some are favored over others in food.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p401#2/r11.anchor: وهذا كقوله تعالى : { ونفضل بعضها على بعض الأكل }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p402/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p402/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p402/r1.claim: The circumstantial phrase may instead apply to everything mentioned from the piled grain onward, since all those things are alike in some respects and unlike in others.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p402/r1.anchor: ويجوز أن تجعل هذه الحال من جميع ما تقدم من قوله : { نخرج منه حبا متراكبا } ، فإن جميع ذلك مشتبه وغير متشابه .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p402/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p402/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p402/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī attaches the circumstantial phrase only to olives and supplies an understood parallel condition for pomegranates, “likewise.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p402/r2.anchor: وجعله الزمخشري حالا من { الزيتون } لأنه المعطوف عليه وقدر ل { الرمان } حالا أخرى تدل عليها الأولى ، بتقدير : والرمان كذلك .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p402/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p402/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p402/r3.claim: He adopts this parse because he rejects one circumstantial phrase having multiple owners or a contest among them, and compares it with a singular predicate after a coordinated subject.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p402/r3.anchor: وإنما دعاه إلى ذلك أنه لا يرى تعدد صاحب الحال الواحدة ولا التنازع في الحال ونظره بإفراد الخبر بعد مبتدأ ومعطوف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p402/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p402/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p402/r4.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr quotes al-Azraq ibn Ṭarafa al-Bāhilī's line in which a singular predicate follows a subject and its conjunct, as an example relevant to the parse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p402/r4.anchor: في قول الأزرق بن طرفة الباهلي ، جوابا لبعض بني قشير وقد اختصما في بئر فقال القشيري : أنت لص ابن لص : رماني بأمر كنت منه ووالدي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p402/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p402/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p402/r5.claim: The parse causes no semantic problem: noticing signs of deliberate design in some plants guides the mind to comparable signs in others.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p402/r5.anchor: ولا ضير في هذا الإعراب من جهة المعنى لأن التنبيه إلى ما في بعض النبات من دلائل الاختيار يوجه العقول إلى ما في مماثله من أمثالها .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p402/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p402/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p402/r6.claim: The command to look explains the preceding descriptions, which aim to bring people to knowledge of God's creation and power.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p402/r6.anchor: وجملة : { انظروا إلى ثمره } بيان للجمل التي قبلها المقصود منها الوصول إلى معرفة صنع الله تعالى وقدرته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p402/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p402/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p402/r7.claim: The pronoun in “its fruit” refers to the same specific or general referent as the pronoun in “alike.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p402/r7.anchor: والضمير المضاف إليه في { ثمره } عائد إلى ما عاد إليه ضمير { مشتبها } من تخصيص أو تعميم .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p402/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p402/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p402/r8.claim: The command asks for reflective observation of the fruit's stages.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p402/r8.anchor: والمأمور به هو نظر الاستبصار والاعتبار بأطواره .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p402/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p402/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p402/r9.claim: Thamar means the produce yielded by a tree.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p402/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p402/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p402/r10.claim: Most readers pronounce thamar with fatḥ on both consonants; Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Khalaf pronounce both with ḍamm, a broken plural pattern like khashab and nuq.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p402/r10.anchor: بفتح الثاء والميم في قراءة الأكثر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p402/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p402/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p402/r11.claim: Yanaʿ is ripeness and maturity; the source gives forms yania/yainu and ayana/yunʿu.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p402/r11.anchor: والينع : الطيب والنضج . يقال : ينع بفتح النون يينع بفتح النون وكسرها ويقال : أينع يونع ينعا بفتح التحتية بعدها نون ساكنة .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p402/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p402/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p402/r12.claim: Idhā marks the time when the event begins, so this means the onset of fruiting.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p402/r12.anchor: و { إذا } ظرف لحدوث الفعل ، فهي بمعنى الوقت الذي يبتدىء فيه مضمون الجملة المضاف إليها ، أي حين ابتداء أثماره .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p402/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p402/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p402/r13.claim: “And its ripening” has no idhā because ripeness completes the plant's development and leaves no further stages to observe.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p402/r13.anchor: وقوله : { وينعه } لم يقيد بإذا أينع لأنه إذا ينع فقد تم تطوره وحان قطافه فلم تبق للنظر فيه عبرة لأنه قد انتهت أطواره .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p402/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p402/r14.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p402/r14.claim: The statement that these contain signs gives the reason for the command to observe; in here functions like the causal lām, as in a line by Bashshār.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p402/r14.anchor: وجملة : { إن في ذلكم لآيات } علة للأمر بالنظر . وموقع ( إن ) فيه موقع لام التعليل ، كقول بشار :

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r1.claim: Al-samāʾ means cloud here; anything overhead that covers you can be called sky.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r1.anchor: السماء في هذا الموضع السحاب، وكل ما أظلك فهو سماء،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r2.claim: Māʾ derives from mawha: wāw is vocalized after fatḥa to make māh, then hāʾ becomes hamza because alif and hāʾ are weak and voiceless.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r2.anchor: وماء أصله موه تحركت الواو وانفتح ما قبلها فجاء ماه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r3.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r3.claim: Some commentators take it as everything that grows; the mention of plants limits the general wording.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r3.anchor: قال بعض المفسرين أي مما ينبت، وحسن إطلاق العموم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r4.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī includes growing animals, plants, minerals, and other things, nourished and grown by rain.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r4.anchor: وقال الطبري والمراد ب كل شيء ما ينمو من جميع الحيوانات

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r5.claim: The first minhu pronoun refers to vegetation, the second to the green growth.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r5.anchor: والضمير في منه يعود على النبات، وفي الثاني يعود على الخضر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r6.claim: Khaḍiran means fresh or verdant; the Prophet's saying calls the world green and sweet. Khidr denotes freshness, akhḍar color primarily.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r6.anchor: وخضرا بمعنى أخضر، ومنه قوله عليه السلام: «الدنيا خضرة حلوة»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r7.claim: Piled grain includes ears and comparable growths such as pine cones, pomegranates, and other plants.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r7.anchor: وقوله: حبا متراكبا يعم جميع السنابل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r8.claim: ‘From palms’ expands as ‘We bring out from palms’; qinwān is a subject with predicate advanced, and the clause is object of the verb.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r8.anchor: وقوله تعالى: ومن النخل تقديره ونخرج من النخل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r9.claim: Ṭalʿ is a palm's first growth while enclosed in sheaths.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r9.anchor: «الطلع» أول ما يخرج من النخلة في أكمامه،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r10.claim: Qinwān is plural of qinw, the palm bunch; ʿarjūn is its date-bearing stalk.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r10.anchor: وقنوان جمع قنو وهو العذق بكسر العين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r11.speaker: الأعرج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r11.claim: Al-Aʿraj reads with fatḥa on qāf; Abu al-Fatḥ says it is a collective, since fiʿlān is not a plural pattern.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r11.anchor: قرأ الأعرج «قنوان» بفتح القاف، وقال أبو الفتح ينبغي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r12.speaker: المهدوي والفراء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r12.claim: Al-Mahdawī reports al-Aʿraj with ḍamma on qāf; al-Farrāʾ calls it a dialect of Qays and Hijaz, with kasra more common.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r12.anchor: قال المهدوي وروي عن الأعرج ضم القاف، وكذلك أنه جمع «قنو» بضم القاف، قال الفراء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r13.claim: The dual of qinw is qinwān, with inflected nūn.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r14.speaker: ابن عباس والبراء بن عازب والضحاك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r14.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Barāʾ b. ʿĀzib, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk say dāniya means near enough to reach; another view says clusters are near one another.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r14.anchor: ودانية معناه قريبة من المتناول، قاله ابن عباس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r15.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r15.claim: The majority read janāt accusative, coordinated with nabāt; al-Aʿmash, Ibn Abi Layla, and a transmission from Abu Bakr from ʿĀṣim read nominative with an implied ‘for you’; al-Ṭabarī coordinates it with qinwān.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p327#2/r15.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور «وجنات» بنصب جنات عطفا على قوله نبات

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p328/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p328/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p328/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls al-Ṭabarī's coordination of nominative janāt with qinwān weak.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p328/r1.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: وقوله ضعيف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p328/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p328/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p328/r2.claim: Olives and pomegranates are unanimously accusative, coordinated with ḥabbā.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p328/r2.anchor: والزيتون والرمان بالنصب إجماعا عطفا على قوله: حبا،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p328/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p328/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p328/r3.claim: Qatāda says fruits resemble in color but differ in fruit.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p328/r3.anchor: قال قتادة: معناه تتشابه في اللون وتتباين في الثمر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p328/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p328/r4.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p328/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī allows resemblance in fruit and difference in taste; Ibn ʿAṭiyya adds resemblance in taste and difference in appearance.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p328/r4.anchor: وقال الطبري: جائز أن تتشابه في الثمر وتتباين في الطعم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p328/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p328/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p328/r5.claim: Looking means seeing in a way that leads to reflection in the heart.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p328/r5.anchor: وقوله تعالى: انظروا وهو نظر بصر يترتب عليه فكرة قلب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p328/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p328/r6.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو ونافع وابن عامر وعاصم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p328/r6.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Abu ʿAmr, Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir, and ʿĀṣim read thamar with fatḥa, a plural of thamara; Yaḥyā b. Waththāb and Mujāhid read ḍamma as kinds of wealth, the reading of Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p328/r6.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو ونافع وابن عامر وعاصم «إلى ثمره» بفتح الثاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p328/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p328/r7.speaker: أبو علي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p328/r7.claim: Abu ʿAlī prefers the broken plural of thamara, like khashaba/khashab and akama/akam; the anonymous poem supplies akam. Thamar may also be a plural of plural or be read with ḍamma and still mīm for ease.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p328/r7.anchor: قال أبو علي والأحسن فيه أن يكون جمع ثمره كخشبة وخشب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p328/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p328/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p328/r8.claim: Poetic akam illustrates akama/akam; analogous weak-final pairs are lāba/lūb, nāqa/nūq, sāḥa/sūḥ. Thamar means fruit or produce; calling the tree thimār is figurative.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p328/r8.anchor: ترى الأكم فيه سجدا للحوافر نظيره في المعتل لابة ولوب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p328/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p328/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p328/r9.claim: Most read yanʿ as a verbal noun for ripening; Ibn ʿAbbās explains it as ripeness, supported by al-Ḥajjāj's ‘heads have ripened.’ Yanʿ can also mean standing tall and becoming green; al-Ṭabarī calls it plural of yāniʿ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p328/r9.anchor: وقرأ جمهور الناس و «ينعه» بفتح الياء وهو مصدر ينع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p328/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p328/r10.speaker: ابن محيصن وقتادة والضحاك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p328/r10.claim: Ibn Muḥayṣin, Qatāda, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk read with ḍamma on yāʾ; Ibn Abi ʿAbla and al-Yamānī read yāniʿahu.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p328/r10.anchor: وقرأ ابن محيصن وقتادة والضحاك «وينعه» بضم الياء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p328/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p328/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p328/r11.claim: The signs call for admonition and remembrance.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p328/r11.anchor: وقوله إن في ذلكم لآيات إيجاب تنبيه وتذكير

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93/r1.claim: The water sent down from heaven is rain, and the following phrase means that God brought things forth by the rain.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى ﴿ وهو الذي أنزل من السماء ماء ﴾ يعني المطر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93/r2.claim: One view takes the phrase as all plant produce, since everything that grows does so by water.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93/r2.anchor: أحدهما نبات كل شيء من الثمار لأن كل ما ينبت فنباته بالماء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93/r3.claim: A second view understands it as each creature's provision or food.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93/r4.claim: One view takes minhu as referring to the water, meaning that God brought the green growth forth by means of it.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93/r5.claim: A second view takes minhu as referring to the plant.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93/r5.anchor: والثاني من النبات قال الزجاج الخضر بمعنى الأخضر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93/r6.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93/r6.claim: Al-Zajjaj says khadir means green; the adjective has shortened forms paralleling aʿwar and ʿawar.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93/r6.anchor: قال الزجاج الخضر بمعنى الأخضر يقال أخضر فهو أخضر وخضر مثل أعور فهو أعور وعور

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93#2/r1.claim: In this clause, minhu refers to the green growth.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93#2/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى ﴿ نخرج منه ﴾ أي من الخضر ﴿ حبا متراكبا ﴾

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93#2/r2.claim: The stacked grain includes wheat and barley; mutarakib means piled one above another.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93#2/r2.anchor: كالسنبل والشعير والمتراكب الذي بعضه فوق بعض

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93#2/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو عن الخفاف
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93#2/r3.claim: Al-Khaffaf transmits from Abu ʿAmr qinwan with the qaf in ḍamma.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93#2/r3.anchor: وروى الخفاف عن أبي عمرو قنوان بضم القاف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93#2/r4.speaker: هارون عن أبي عمرو
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93#2/r4.claim: Harun transmits from Abu ʿAmr qinwan with the qaf in fatḥa.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93#2/r4.anchor: وروى هارون عنه بفتحها قال الفراء معناه ومن النخل ما قنوانه دانية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93#2/r5.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93#2/r5.claim: Al-Farra paraphrases the phrase as meaning that among the palms are clusters that hang near.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93#2/r5.anchor: قال الفراء معناه ومن النخل ما قنوانه دانية وأهل الحجاز يقولون قنوان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93#2/r6.speaker: أهل الحجاز، قيس، ضبة، تميم، كلب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93#2/r6.claim: The dialects vary: Hijaz says qinwan with kasra, Qays with ḍamma, Dabba and Tamim use qiniyan, and Kalb also says qiniyan.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93#2/r6.anchor: وأهل الحجاز يقولون قنوان بكسر القاف وقيس يضمونها وضبة وتميم يقولون قنيان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93#2/r7.speaker: امرؤ القيس، أبو سعيد السكري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93#2/r7.claim: The poem attributed to Imruʾ al-Qays witnesses qiniyan; al-Sukkari transmits a variant with qinwan and a kasra on the qaf, showing four language forms.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93#2/r7.anchor: وأنشدني المفضل عنهم فأثت أعاليه وآدت أصوله ومال بقنيان من البسر أحمرا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93#2/r8.claim: In the cited line, athath means increased or grew numerous, and ādat means strengthened.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93#2/r8.anchor: وأثت كثرت ومنه شعر أثيت وآدت اشتدت

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93#2/r9.speaker: ابن قتيبة، الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93#2/r9.claim: Ibn Qutayba says qinwan means palm clusters, singular qinu, and is a plural shaped like the dual; al-Zajjaj calls it a plural of qinu.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93#2/r9.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة القنوان عذوق النخل واحدها قنو جمع على لفظ تثنية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93#2/r10.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93#2/r10.claim: Al-Zajjaj distinguishes the plural qinwan from its dual, qinwan with kasra on the nun.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93#2/r10.anchor: وقال الزجاج قنوان جمع قنو وإذا ثنيته فهما قنوان بكسر النون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93#2/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93#2/r11.claim: Daniya means close enough to reach.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93#2/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93#2/r12.claim: The verse mentions nearby clusters without separately naming distant ones, relying on an implication in the wording; the phrasing is compared with 16:81.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93#2/r12.anchor: ولم يقل ومنها قنوان بعيدة لأن في الكلام دليلا أن البعيدة السحيقة قد كانت غير سحيقة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93#2/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93#2/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93#2/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas identifies the nearby clusters as short palms whose fruit bunches reach down toward the earth.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p93#2/r13.anchor: قال ابن عباس القنوان الدانية قصار النخل اللاصقة عذوقها بالأرض

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p94/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p94/r1.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p94/r1.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the grape gardens are coordinated grammatically with khadir.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p94/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج هو نسق على قوله خضرا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p94/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p94/r2.speaker: أبو زيد عن المفضل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p94/r2.claim: Abu Zayd transmits from al-Mufaddal a nominative reading, jannatun.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p94/r2.anchor: وقد روى أبو زيد عن المفضل وجنات بالرفع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p94/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p94/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p94/r3.claim: The phrase means that God also brought forth olive and pomegranate trees.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p94/r3.anchor: المعنى وأخرجنا منه شجر الزيتون والرمان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p94/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p94/r4.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p94/r4.claim: One view says the fruits resemble one another in appearance but differ in taste.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p94/r4.anchor: أحدها مشتبها في المنظر وغير متشابه في الطعم رواه أبو صالح عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p94/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p94/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p94/r5.claim: A second view says the leaves resemble each other while the fruits differ, which amounts to the first interpretation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p94/r5.anchor: والثاني مشتبها ورقه مختلفا ثمره قاله قتادة وهو في معنى الأول

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p94/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p94/r6.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p94/r6.claim: A third view says some fruits resemble one another and some differ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p94/r6.anchor: والثالث منه ما يشبه بعضه بعضا ومنه ما يخالف قال الزجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p94/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p94/r7.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p94/r7.claim: Al-Zajjaj says olive and pomegranate are paired because Arabs know that their leaves sheath each branch from end to end; a poem invokes the blessing of pomegranate and olive foliage.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p94/r7.anchor: قال الزجاج وإنما قرن الزيتون بالرمان لأنهما شجرتان تعرف العرب أن ورقهما يشتمل على الغصن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p95/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p95/r1.speaker: ابن كثير، نافع، أبو عمرو، ابن عامر، عاصم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p95/r1.claim: These readers pronounce thamar with fatḥa in this verse and in the cited phrases in 6:141 and 36:35.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p95/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وعاصم ﴿ انظروا إلى ثمره ﴾ و ﴿ كلوا من ثمره ﴾

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p95/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p95/r2.speaker: حمزة، الكسائي، خلف
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p95/r2.claim: These readers pronounce thumr with ḍamma in the three cited phrases.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p95/r2.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وخلف بالضم فيهن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p95/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p95/r3.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p95/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj lists thamarah, thamar, thimar, and thumr as forms for fruit.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p95/r3.anchor: قال الزجاج يقال ثمرة وثمر وثمار وثمر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p95/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p95/r4.speaker: أبو علي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p95/r4.claim: Abu ʿAli gives two analyses of thumr: a plural of thimar, or a plural of thamara like akama from akama and khashaba from khashaba.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p95/r4.anchor: وقال أبو علي يحتمل وجهين أحدهما هذا وهو أن يكون الثمر جمع ثمار

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p95/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p95/r5.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p95/r5.claim: Al-Farra says to look at the fruit when it first sets, and at its ripening when it reaches maturity.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p95/r5.anchor: يقول انظروا إليه أول ما يعقد وانظروا إلى ينعه وهو نضجه وبلوغه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p95/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p95/r6.speaker: أهل الحجاز، بعض أهل نجد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p95/r6.claim: The Hijaz dialect pronounces yanʿ with an open ya; some people of Najd use a ḍamma.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p95/r6.anchor: وأهل الحجاز يقولون ينع بفتح الياء وبعض أهل نجد يضمونها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p95/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p95/r7.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p95/r7.claim: Ibn Qutayba says the fruit is described as having ripened when it is fully grown and mature; the term is yanʿ or yunʿ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p95/r7.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة يقال ينعت الثمرة وأينعت إذا أدركت وهو الينع والينع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p95/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p95/r8.speaker: الحسن، مجاهد، قتادة، الأعمش، ابن محيصن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p95/r8.claim: These readers pronounce the ya of yunʿihi with ḍamma.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p95/r8.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ومجاهد وقتادة والأعمش وابن محيصن وينعه بضم الياء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p95/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p95/r9.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p95/r9.claim: Al-Zajjaj defines yunʿ as ripeness, citing a poem that says the olives around the mansion have ripened.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p95/r9.anchor: قال الزجاج الينع النضج قال الشاعر في قباب حول دسكرة حولها الزيتون قد ينعا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p95/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p95/r10.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p95/r10.claim: The changing of created things through stages, beyond human power, shows that God can likewise resurrect the dead.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p95/r10.anchor: وبين الله تعالى لهم بتصريف ما خلق ونقله من حال إلى حال لا يقدر عليه الخلق أنه كذلك يبعثهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p96/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p96/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p96/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says believers affirm that the One who produced this vegetation can bring the dead to life.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p96/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس يصدقون أن لذي أخرج هذا النبات قادر على أن يحيي الموتى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p96/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p96/r2.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p96/r2.claim: Muqatil says the phrase means those who believe in divine oneness.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p306/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p306/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p306/r2.claim: God sends measured, blessed water as provision for people, relief for creatures, and mercy for His creation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p306/r2.anchor: أي بقدر مباركا، رزقا للعباد وغياثا (2) للخلائق، رحمة من الله لخلقه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p306/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p306/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p306/r3.claim: The water brings forth every kind of plant; Ibn Kathir relates this to the statement that every living thing was made from water.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p306/r3.anchor: كما قال {وجعلنا من الماء كل شيء حي} [الأنبياء: 30]

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p306/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p306/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p306/r4.claim: The green growth means green crops and trees; grain and fruit develop within them afterward.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p306/r4.anchor: أي: زرعا وشجرا أخضر، ثم بعد ذلك يخلق فيه الحب والثمر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p306/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p306/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p306/r5.claim: Mutarākib means grains stacked one upon another, as in ears of grain.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p306/r5.anchor: أي: يركب بعضه بعضا، كالسنابل ونحوها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p306/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p306/r6.speaker: علي بن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p306/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas explains the nearby clusters as short date palms whose bunches hang close to the ground; Ibn Jarir transmits the report.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p306/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {قنوان دانية} يعني بالقنوان الدانية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p306/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p306/r7.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p306/r7.claim: Ibn Jarir says qinwān is the plural of qinw; Hijaz and Qays use qinwān, while Tamim says qinyān, just as sinw has plural sinwān. Imruʾ al-Qays’s verse witnesses qinwān.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p306/r7.anchor: قال ابن جرير: وأهل الحجاز يقولون: قنوان، وقيس يقولون: قنوان، وقال امرؤ القيس:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p306#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p306#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p306#2/r1.claim: In the phrase about vineyards, Ibn Kathir supplies the omitted verb: We bring forth vineyards from it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p306#2/r1.anchor: وقوله: {وجنات من أعناب} أي: ونخرج منه جنات من أعناب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p306#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p306#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p306#2/r2.claim: Date palms and grapes are especially esteemed among the people of the Hijaz and may be the finest fruits in the world; God also names these blessings in 16:67 and 36:34, before wine was prohibited.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p306#2/r2.anchor: وهذان النوعان هما أشرف عند أهل الحجاز، وربما كانا (6) خيار الثمار في الدنيا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p306#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p306#2/r3.speaker: قتادة وغيره
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p306#2/r3.claim: Qatada and others say the plants resemble one another in their leaves and general appearance but differ in fruit shape, taste, and nature.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p306#2/r3.anchor: قال قتادة وغيره: يتشابه في الورق، قريب الشكل بعضه من بعض، ويتخالف في الثمار شكلا وطعما وطبعا.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p306#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p306#2/r4.speaker: البراء بن عازب وابن عباس والضحاك وعطاء الخراساني والسدي وقتادة وغيرهم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p306#2/r4.claim: Al-Baraʾ ibn ʿAzib, Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Dahhak, ʿAta al-Khurasani, al-Suddi, Qatada, and others gloss yanʿ as ripeness.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p306#2/r4.anchor: قاله البراء بن عازب، وابن عباس، والضحاك، وعطاء الخراساني، والسدي، وقتادة، وغيرهم.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p306#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p306#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p306#2/r5.claim: People should reflect on the Creator’s power as plants emerge from nothingness, wood becomes grapes or dates, and creation takes varied colors, shapes, tastes, and scents.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p306#2/r5.anchor: فكروا في قدرة خالقه من العدم إلى الوجود، بعد أن كان حطبا صار عنبا ورطبا وغير ذلك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p306#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p306#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p306#2/r6.claim: These fruits are signs of the Creator’s perfect power, wisdom, and mercy for people who believe in Him and follow His messengers.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p306#2/r6.anchor: أي: دلالات على كمال قدرة خالق هذه الأشياء وحكمته ورحمته

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p306#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p306#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p306#2/r7.claim: The mention of grapes and dates recalls God’s favor of these fruits in 16:67 and the gardens of palms and grapes in 36:34.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p306#2/r7.anchor: كما امتن تعالى بهما على عباده، في قوله

JISHUMI:v3p2337/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2337/r5.speaker: شعبة عن عاصم
JISHUMI:v3p2337/r5.claim: Shuʿba from ʿĀṣim reads jannāt with ḍamma on tāʾ; the source also names ʿAlī, Ibn Masʿūd, al-Sulamī, al-Aʿmash, and Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar with this reading.
JISHUMI:v3p2337/r5.anchor: قرأ شعبة عن عاصم: جنات بضم التاء، وهو قراءة علي بن أبي طالب

JISHUMI:v3p2337/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2337/r6.speaker: باقي القراء
JISHUMI:v3p2337/r6.claim: The other readers put kasra on tāʾ, construing the phrase as 'and We brought forth gardens.'
JISHUMI:v3p2337/r6.anchor: وقرأ الباقون جنات بكسر التاء على معنى: فأخرجنا جنات

JISHUMI:v3p2337/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2337/r7.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
JISHUMI:v3p2337/r7.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read thumur with ḍamma on both letters, as a plural of thimār.
JISHUMI:v3p2337/r7.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي: ثمره بضم الثاء والميم على أنه جمع: ثمار

JISHUMI:v3p2337/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2337/r8.speaker: أبو عمرو
JISHUMI:v3p2337/r8.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads thumur with ḍamma on thāʾ and a still mīm, a lightened form.
JISHUMI:v3p2337/r8.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو: ثمر بضم الثاء وسكون الميم تخفيفا

JISHUMI:v3p2337/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2337/r9.speaker: باقي القراء
JISHUMI:v3p2337/r9.claim: The other readers use fatḥa on both letters, taking thamar as the plural of thamara.
JISHUMI:v3p2337/r9.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بفتحهما على أنها جمع ثمرة

JISHUMI:v3p2337/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2337/r10.speaker: عامة القراء
JISHUMI:v3p2337/r10.claim: The common reading has kasra on qāf in qinwān; al-Aʿraj reads it with ḍamma, and both are dialect forms.
JISHUMI:v3p2337/r10.anchor: وقراءة العامة: قنوان بكسر القاف، وعن الأعرج بضم القاف، وهما لغتان

JISHUMI:v3p2337/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2337/r11.speaker: عامة القراء
JISHUMI:v3p2337/r11.claim: The common reading takes yanʿ as a verbal noun; some read yāniʿahu with an alif as a noun.
JISHUMI:v3p2337/r11.anchor: وعامة القراء قرؤوا: وينعه على المصدر، وعن بعضهم (ويانعه) بالألف على الاسم

JISHUMI:v3p2337/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2337/r12.speaker: أبو السمال وقتادة
JISHUMI:v3p2337/r12.claim: Abū al-Sammāl and Qatāda read wayunʿihi with ḍamma on yāʾ; the text gives yāniʿ and ayānaʿ as related forms.
JISHUMI:v3p2337/r12.anchor: وقرأ أبو [السمال] وقتادة: وينعه بضم الياء

JISHUMI:v3p2337/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2337/r13.speaker: أبو عبيدة
JISHUMI:v3p2337/r13.claim: Abū ʿUbayda says yanaʿ is a plural of yāniʿ, like tājir and tajr.
JISHUMI:v3p2337/r13.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: ينع: جمع يانع، كتاجر وتجر

JISHUMI:v3p2337/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2337/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2337/r14.claim: Khaḍir means green foliage; the form khaḍira can mean akhḍar, while Arab usage also calls anything soft or fresh khaḍir.
JISHUMI:v3p2337/r14.anchor: الخضر: الورق الأخضر، وفعل بمعنى أفعل، خضر بمعنى أخضر

JISHUMI:v3p2337/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2337/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2337/r15.claim: The expression al-dunyā ḥulwa khaḍira in a hadith means the world is sweet, tender, and fresh.
JISHUMI:v3p2337/r15.anchor: ومنه الحديث: الدنيا حلوة خضرة يعني غضة ناعمة طرية

JISHUMI:v3p2337/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2337/r16.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2337/r16.claim: Taking something khaḍiran naḍiran means taking it without payment or taking it while fresh and tender.
JISHUMI:v3p2337/r16.anchor: ويقال: أخذ الشيء خضرا نضرا: إذا أخذه بغير ثمن

JISHUMI:v3p2337/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2337/r17.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2337/r17.claim: The phrase 'his blood went khaḍiran muḍiran' means his blood was wasted.
JISHUMI:v3p2337/r17.anchor: وذهب دمه خضرا مضرا أي: هدرا باطلا

JISHUMI:v3p2337/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2337/r18.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2337/r18.claim: A 'green' battalion means blackened by iron armor; Arabs use green and black for one another and call Iraq black from its greenery.
JISHUMI:v3p2337/r18.anchor: وكتيبة خضراء: إذا كانت عليها سواد الحديد. والعرب تسمى الأسود أخضر والأخضر أسود

JISHUMI:v3p2337/r19.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2337/r19.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2337/r19.claim: In the line 'I am al-akhdar,' the word means pure complexion, since Arab complexions are brown.
JISHUMI:v3p2337/r19.anchor: ومنه قوله: وأنا الأخضر من يعرفني يعني: خالص اللون؛ لأن ألوان العرب السمرة

JISHUMI:v3p2337/r20.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2337/r20.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2337/r20.claim: The hadith warning against khadrāʾ al-diman likens a beautiful woman from bad stock to a lush plant growing in dung.
JISHUMI:v3p2337/r20.anchor: وقوله: إياكم وخضراء الدمن، يعني شجرة ناعمة في دمنة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p49#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p49#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p49#2/r1.claim: Water produces every kind of growing thing: the cause is one, while the resulting species are varied.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p49#2/r1.anchor: نبت كل صنف من أصناف النامي ، يعني أن السبب واحد وهو الماء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p49#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p49#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p49#2/r2.claim: Khaḍir is a tender green shoot branching from the plant base grown from the seed; the word has singular and collective forms.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p49#2/r2.anchor: شيئا غضا أخضر . يقال خضر وخضر ، كأعور وعور ، وهو ما تشعب من أصل النبات الخارج من الحبة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p49#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p49#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p49#2/r3.claim: The clustered grain produced from the green shoot is the ear of grain.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p49#2/r3.anchor: من الخضر { حبا متراكبا } وهو السنبل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p49#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p49#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p49#2/r4.claim: Qinwān can be a subject with min al-nakhl its predicate and min ṭalʿihā an apposition; alternatively, an omitted predicate is supplied from the earlier verb.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p49#2/r4.anchor: و { قنوان } رفع الابتداء . و { من * النخل } خبره

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p49#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p49#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p49#2/r5.claim: With the reading yakhruju, qinwān coordinates with ḥabb rather than serving as a new subject.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p49#2/r5.anchor: ومن قرأ يخرج منه حب متراكب ، كان

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p49#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p49#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p49#2/r6.claim: Qinwān is the plural of qinw, like ṣinw and ṣinwān; its qāf is read with ḍamma or fatḥa, the latter as a collective noun.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p49#2/r6.anchor: والقنوان : جمع قنو ، ونظيره : صنو وصنوان

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p49#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p49#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p49#2/r7.claim: Nearby clusters are easy to pick; even a short palm bears fruit without waiting to grow tall.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p49#2/r7.anchor: سهلة المجتنى معرضة للقاطف ، كالشيء الداني القريب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p49#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p49#2/r8.speaker: الحسن
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p49#2/r8.claim: Al-Hasan says the date clusters are close to one another.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p49#2/r8.anchor: وقال الحسن : دانية قريب بعضها من بعض

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p49#2/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p49#2/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p49#2/r9.claim: Near clusters are mentioned while distant ones are omitted because the blessing is clearer in the near ones, which imply the distant ones; the author compares the mention of protection from heat.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p49#2/r9.anchor: ذكر القريبة وترك ذكر البعيدة : لأن النعمة فيها أظهر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p49#2/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p49#2/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p49#2/r10.claim: Gardens of grapes can be an additional item alongside palms or coordinated with qinwān as another product.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p49#2/r10.anchor: فيه وجهان ، أحدهما : أن يراد : وثم جنات من أعناب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p49#2/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p49#2/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p49#2/r11.claim: The accusative can coordinate these products with plants of every kind; the author prefers parsing them as a specification because these fruits deserve special mention.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p49#2/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p49#2/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p49#2/r12.claim: Ishtabaha and tashābaha often share a meaning; the variant describes olives and pomegranates as alike and unlike.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p49#2/r12.anchor: يقال اشتبه الشيئان وتشابها ، كقولك استويا وتساويا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p49#2/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p49#2/r13.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p49#2/r13.claim: A variant reads mutashābihan wa-ghayra mutashābih, with both fruits understood as alike and unlike.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p148/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p148/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p148/r8.claim: One interpretation says the water brings forth provision for every kind of animal.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p148/r8.anchor: أحدهما : معناه رزق كل شيء من الحيوان .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p148/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p148/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p148/r9.claim: A second interpretation says it brings forth every kind of fruit.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p148/r9.anchor: والثاني : نبات كل شيء من الثمار .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p148/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p148/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p148/r10.claim: Khadiran means fresh green crops, in contrast with their state when sown.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p148/r10.anchor: يعني زرعا رطبا بخلاف صفته عند بذره .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p148/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p148/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p148/r11.claim: The stacked grain is grain layered or packed together in the ear.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p148/r11.anchor: يعني السنبل الذي قد تراكب حبه .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p148/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p148/r12.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p148/r12.claim: Al-Dahhak interprets qinwan as the palm's spathe or flowering stalk.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p148/r12.anchor: الطلع , قاله الضحاك . والثاني : أنه الجمار .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p148/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p148/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p148/r13.claim: A second interpretation takes qinwan as the palm heart, or jummar.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p148/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p148/r14.speaker: امرؤ القيس
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p148/r14.claim: Qinwan means date clusters; Imru al-Qays's verse is cited as evidence for the word's use.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p148/r14.anchor: والثالث : هي الأعذاق , قال امرؤ القيس

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p149/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p149/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p149/r1.claim: The clusters are near enough to a picker because the palms are short and fruit is easy to reach.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p149/r1.anchor: دانية من المجتني لقصر نخلها وقرب تناولها , قاله ابن عباس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p149/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p149/r2.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p149/r2.claim: Hasan says the clusters are near one another because they grow close together.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p149/r2.anchor: داينة بعضها من بعض لتقاربها , قاله الحسن .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p149/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p149/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p149/r3.claim: The phrase means gardens or orchards of grapevines.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p149/r3.anchor: { وجنات من أعناب } يعني بساتين من أعناب .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p149/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p149/r4.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p149/r4.claim: Qatada says the leaves are similar while the fruits differ.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p149/r4.anchor: مشتبها ورقه مختلفا ثمره , قال قتادة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p149/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p149/r5.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p149/r5.claim: Al-Kalbi says the fruits have similar colors but different tastes.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p149/r5.anchor: مشتبها لونه مختلفا طعمه , قاله الكلبي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p149/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p149/r6.speaker: حمزة، الكسائي
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p149/r6.claim: Hamza and al-Kisa'i read thamarihi with damma, while the other readers read it with fatha.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p149/r6.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي بالضم , وقرأ الباقون بالفتح ,

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p149/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p149/r7.speaker: علي بن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p149/r7.claim: One explanation says the damma form is the plural of thimar, while the fatha form is the plural of thamarah.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p149/r7.anchor: أن الثمر بالضم جمع ثمار , وبالفتح جمع ثمرة , قاله علي بن عيسى .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p149/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p149/r8.speaker: مجاهد، أبو جعفر الطبري
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p149/r8.claim: Another distinction makes thamar with damma mean wealth and the fatha form mean dates or palm fruit.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p149/r8.anchor: أن الثمر بالضم : المال , وبالفتح : ثمر النخل , قاله مجاهد , وأبو جعفر الطبري .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p149/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p149/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p149/r9.claim: Yun'ihi means the fruit's ripening and coming to full maturity.

MUQATIL:6:95-99/r17.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r17.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r17.claim: The water sent down from heaven is rain.
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r17.anchor: { وهو الذي أنزل من السمآء مآء } ، يعني المطر،

MUQATIL:6:95-99/r18.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r18.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r18.claim: Rain brings out fruits, grains, and the varieties of vegetation.
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r18.anchor: { فأخرجنا به } ، يعني بالمطر، { نبات كل شيء } ، يعني الثمار والحبوب وألوان النبات،

MUQATIL:6:95-99/r19.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r19.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r19.claim: The “green” is the first growth of a plant.
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r19.anchor: { فأخرجنا منه خضرا } ، يعني أول النبات،

MUQATIL:6:95-99/r20.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r20.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r20.claim: Muqātil takes “from it” as from the water, and the piled grain as an ear whose kernels are stacked upon one another.
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r20.anchor: { نخرج منه } ، يعني من الماء، { حبا متراكبا } ، يعني السنبل قد ركب بعضه بعضا،

MUQATIL:6:95-99/r21.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r21.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r21.claim: The palm's ṭalʿ refers to its fruit.
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r21.anchor: { ومن النخل من طلعها } ، يعني من ثمرها، { قنوان } ، يعني قصار النخل،

MUQATIL:6:95-99/r22.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r22.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r22.claim: Qinwān are short palms; dāniya means close to the ground and hand-picked.
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r22.anchor: { دانية } ، يعني ملتصقة بالأرض تجنى باليد،

MUQATIL:6:95-99/r23.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r23.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r23.anchor: { وجنات } ، يعني البساتين، ثم نعت البساتين، فقال:

MUQATIL:6:95-99/r24.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r24.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r24.claim: The plants resemble each other in the appearance of their leaves, while differing in color and taste.
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r24.anchor: { من } نخيل و { أعناب والزيتون والرمان مشتبها } ، ورقها في المنظر يشبه ورق الزيتون وورق الرمان،

MUQATIL:6:95-99/r25.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r25.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r25.claim: The fruits differ in color and taste.
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r25.anchor: { وغير متشابه } في اللون مختلف في الطعم،

MUQATIL:6:95-99/r26.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r26.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r26.claim: People should observe fruit when it first appears, still fresh and at its earliest, tiny stage.
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r26.anchor: { انظروا إلى ثمره إذا أثمر } حين يبدو غضا أوله صيصا،

MUQATIL:6:95-99/r27.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r27.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r27.claim: Observing the fruit's ripening reveals a sign in God's works and marvels for believers in His oneness.
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r27.anchor: { وينعه إن في ذلكم } ، يعني إن في هذا الذى ذكر من صنعه وعجائبه لعبرة، { لآيات لقوم يؤمنون } [آية: 99]، يعني يصدقون بالتوحيد.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r1.claim: The water sent down from the sky is rain from clouds.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r1.anchor: ﴿ وهو الذي أنزل من السماء ماء ﴾ من السحاب مطرا

NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r2.claim: The water brings forth every kind of growing thing: one cause produces many different kinds of result.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r2.anchor: نبت كل صنف من أصناف النامى أى السبب وهو الماء واحد والمسببات صنوف مختلفة

NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r3.claim: Khadr is fresh green growth branching from the plant's base, and may be said as akhḍar or khaḍir.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r3.anchor: أى شيئا غضا أخضر يقال أخضر وخضر وهو ما تشعب من أصل النبات الخارج من الحبة

NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r4.claim: The clustered grain is the ear in which the grains are stacked together.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r4.anchor: ﴿ نخرج منه ﴾ من الخضر ﴿ حبا متراكبا ﴾ وهو السنبل

NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r5.claim: Qinwān is the plural of qinw, meaning a date cluster, like ṣinw and ṣinwān.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r5.anchor: ﴿ ومن النخل من طلعها قنوان ﴾ وهو جمع قنو وهو العذق

NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r6.claim: The clusters are low and easy to pick because their weight bends them down or their stalks are short.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r6.anchor: من المجتنى لا نحنائها يثقل حملها أو لقصر ساقها

NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r7.claim: The wording omits the contrasting tall clusters, as 16:81 mentions clothing that protects from heat while omitting cold.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r7.anchor: وفيه اكتفاء أى وغير دانية لطولها كقوله سرابيل تقيكم الحر

NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r8.claim: With jannāt in the accusative, it is coordinated with نبات كل شيء: God also brings forth vineyards by the water.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r8.anchor: ﴿ وجنات ﴾ بالنصب عطفا على نبات كل شيء أى وأخرجنا به جنات

NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r9.speaker: الأعمش
NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r9.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads jannāt in the nominative, implying: and there are also gardens of grapes.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r9.anchor: وجنات بالرفع الأعشى أى وثم جنات من أعناب أى مع النخل

NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r10.claim: The wording includes olives and pomegranates along with the date palms.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r10.anchor: أى مع النخل وكذا ﴿ والزيتون والرمان

NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r11.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r11.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r11.claim: Iftʿāl and tafaʿul forms often share a meaning, as in the verbs for resembling; olives and pomegranates are each alike in some respects and unlike in others.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r11.anchor: والافتعال والتفاعل يشتركان كثيرا أو تقديره والزيتون متشابها وغير متشابه والرمان كذلك

NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r12.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r12.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r12.claim: The fruits resemble or differ from one another in size, color, and taste.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r12.anchor: يعنى بعضه متشابه وبعضه غير متشابه فى القدر واللون والطعم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r13.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r13.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r13.claim: At first the fruit emerges weak and unusable; at ripeness it becomes useful, showing God's power and care in moving it between states.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r13.anchor: ﴿ انظروا إلى ثمره إذا أثمر ﴾ إذا أخرج ثمره كيف يخرجه ضعيفا لا ينتفع به

NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r14.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r14.speaker: حمزة وعلى
NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r14.claim: Hamza and al-Kisāʾī read thumurihi, the plural of thamar, which is itself a plural form.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p337#2/r14.anchor: ثمرة وكذا ما بعده حمزة وعلى جمع ثمار فهو جمع الجمع يقال ثمرة وثمر وثمار وثمر

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r1.claim: The water sent down from heaven is rain.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r2.claim: Nabat kull shayʾ means every kind of plant; another explanation is provision for every animal.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r2.anchor: أي كل صنف من النبات. وقيل: رزق كل حيوان

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r3.speaker: الأخفش
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r3.claim: Al-Akhfash glosses khadiran as green, citing an Arabic expression about seeing a striped garment as rain-colored.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r3.anchor: قال الأخفش: أي أخضر كما تقول العرب: أرينها نمرة

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r4.claim: Al-khaḍr is fresh green vegetable growth.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the green growth as wheat, barley, silt, corn, rice, and other grains.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: يريد القمح والشعير والسلت والذرة

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r6.claim: The stacked grain is piled one part upon another, as in an ear of grain.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r6.anchor: أي يركب بعضه على بعض كالسنبلة

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r7.claim: Qinwān dāniya is parsed as subject and predicate; al-Farra allows a non-Qur'anic accusative qinwānan coordinated with what precedes.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r7.anchor: ابتداء وخبر. وأجاز الفراء في غير القرآن «قنوانا دانية»

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r8.speaker: سيبويه والفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r8.claim: Sibawayh notes qinwān; al-Farra assigns it to Qays and the Hijaz, while Tamim says qiniyān, though their singular is qinw/qan.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r8.anchor: قال سيبويه: ومن العرب من يقول: قنوان. قال الفراء: هذه لغة قيس

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r9.claim: Ṭalʿ is the palm spathe before it splits to reveal the bloom; the bloom is also called ṭalʿ, as is what appears on a palm cluster.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r9.anchor: والطلع الكفرى قبل أن ينشق عن الإغريض. والإغريض يسمى طلعا أيضا

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r10.claim: Qinwān is plural of qinw, and its dual is qinwān like sinw/sinwān; qinw means a date cluster.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r10.anchor: والقنوان: جمع قنو، وتثنيته قنوان كصنو وصنوان

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r11.speaker: الجوهري وغيره
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r11.claim: Al-Jawhari and others note that the dual is sinwān and the plural sinwān, with differing case vowels.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r11.anchor: قال الجوهري وغيره: الاثنان صنوان والجمع صنوان برفع النون

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r12.claim: Qinwān and aqnāʾ are plurals of qinw; a cited line describes palms as having long aqnāʾ, a small-count plural.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r12.anchor: والقنو: العذق والجمع القنوان والأقناء قال: طويلة الأقناء والأثاكل

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r13.speaker: ابن هرمز
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r13.claim: Ibn Harmuz read qinwān with fatḥa on qāf, also reported with ḍamma; fatḥa is a collective noun, while ḍamma makes it a plural of qinw.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r13.anchor: قال المهدوي: قرأ ابن هرمز «قنوان» بفتح القاف، وروي عنه ضمها

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r14.speaker: سيبويه
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r14.claim: With fatḥa qinwān is a collective noun, not a broken plural, like rakb, al-bāqir, and al-jāmil; with ḍamma it is plural of qinw.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r14.anchor: فعلى الفتح هو اسم للجمع غير مكسر، بمنزلة ركب عند سيبويه

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r15.claim: Qinw means a date cluster; ʿidhq with kasra means the cluster, while ʿadhq with fatḥa means the palm tree.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r15.anchor: وهو العذق بكسر العين وهي الكباسة، وهي عنقود النخلة

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r16.speaker: ابن عباس والبراء بن عازب
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r16.claim: Dāniya means near, reachable by someone standing or sitting.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r16.anchor: { دانية } قريبة، ينالها القائم والقاعد. عن ابن عباس والبراء

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r17.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r17.claim: Al-Zajjaj understands an omitted contrast: some clusters are near and some far, as in 16:81.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r17.anchor: قال الزجاج: منها دانية ومنها بعيدة فحذف ومثله سرابيل تقيكم الحر

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r18.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r18.claim: Near clusters are singled out because the verse emphasizes power and beneficence, and a benefit within easy reach is greater.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r18.anchor: وخص الدانية بالذكر، لأن من الغرض في الآية ذكر القدرة والامتنان بالنعمة

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r19.speaker: محمد بن عبد الرحمن بن أبي ليلى والأعمش
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r19.claim: Ibn Abi Layla and al-A'mash, in the sound reading of Asim, read jannāt in the nominative; Abu Ubayd and Abu Hatim reject it, with Abu Hatim objecting that gardens cannot be of palms.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r19.anchor: وقرأ محمد بن عبد الرحمن بن أبي ليلى والأعمش، وهو الصحيح من قراءة عاصم «وجنات» بالرفع

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r20.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r20.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r20.claim: Al-Nahhas accepts the nominative as a subject with an omitted predicate, “and they have gardens,” a construction allowed by Sibawayh, al-Kisa'i, and al-Farra.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99/r20.anchor: قال النحاس: والقراءة جائزة، وليس التأويل على هذا

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r1.claim: Olives and pomegranates are accusative, with consensus on that reading.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r1.anchor: فأما الزيتون والرمان فليس فيه إلا النصب للإجماع على ذلك.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r2.speaker: قتادة وغيره
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r2.claim: Qatada and others explain similarity as resemblance of olive and pomegranate leaves, but difference as their distinct tastes.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r2.anchor: أي متشابها في الأوراق أي ورق الزيتون يشبه ورق الرمان في اشتماله على جميع الغصن

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r3.speaker: ابن جريج
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r3.claim: Ibn Jurayj says fruits resemble in appearance but differ in taste, like two pomegranates of one color but different flavors.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن جريج: «متشابها» في النظر «وغير متشابه» في الطعم

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r4.claim: Olive and pomegranate are named because locally familiar and prominent, like the camel used as a familiar example in 88:17.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r4.anchor: وخص الرمان والزيتون بالذكر لقربهما منهم ومكانهما عندهم

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r5.claim: Looking at the fruit means reflective observation, not mere eyesight without thought.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r5.anchor: أي نظر الاعتبار لا نظر الإبصار المجرد عن التفكر

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r6.claim: Thamar means the produce of a tree.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r7.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r7.claim: Hamza and al-Kisa'i read thamarahu with ḍamma on thāʾ and mīm; other readers use fatḥa as a plural of thamarah.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي «ثمره» بضم الثاء والميم

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r8.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r8.claim: Mujahid says thamar denotes kinds of wealth, whereas tamr is dates; the sense is wealth yielding produce.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r8.anchor: قال مجاهد: الثمر أصناف المال، والتمر ثمر النخل

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r9.speaker: الأعمش
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r9.claim: Al-A'mash is reported to read thamar with ḍamma on thāʾ and a still mīm, dropping the vowel for ease.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r9.anchor: وروي عن الأعمش «ثمره» بضم الثاء وسكون الميم

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r10.claim: Thamar may be a plural of thamarah, a plural of a plural, or a direct plural of thamarah, like khashab from khashaba.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r10.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون ثمر جمع ثمرة مثل بدنة وبدن

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r11.speaker: محمد بن السميقع
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r11.claim: Muhammad ibn al-Sumayqa read the word as wayāniʿuhu.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r12.speaker: ابن محيصن وابن أبي إسحاق
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r12.claim: Ibn Muhaysin and Ibn Abi Ishaq read wayunʿuhu with ḍamma on yāʾ.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r12.anchor: وابن محيصن وابن أبي إسحاق «وينعه» بضم الياء

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r13.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r13.claim: Al-Farra says the ḍamma reading is a Najdi dialect; yanaʿ and ayanaʿa describe ripening, and mawniʿ describes ripe dates.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r13.anchor: قال الفراء: هي لغة بعض أهل نجد يقال: ينع الثمر يينع

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r14.claim: Yanaʿ and ayanaʿa mean ripening and reaching maturity; al-Hajjaj's phrase about heads ripening and harvest time illustrates the usage.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r14.anchor: ينع وأينع إذا نضج وأدرك. وقال الحجاج في خطبته

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r15.speaker: ابن الأنباري
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r15.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says al-yanaʿ is a plural of yāniʿ, like rakib/rakb and tājir/tijr, meaning mature and fully developed.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r15.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري: الينع جمع يانع، كراكب وركب، وتاجر وتجر

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r16.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r16.claim: Al-Farra says ayanaʿa is more common and means turning red; al-yinʿa in a report about a disputed newborn is a red bead, perhaps agate.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r16.anchor: وقال الفراء: أينع أكثر من ينع، ومعناه أحمر

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r17.claim: Another parsing supplies “we brought them out,” like saying “I honored Abdullah and his brother.”
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#2/r17.anchor: وقيل: التقدير «وجنات من أعناب» أخرجناها كقولك:

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#3/r1.claim: Reflecting on changing fruit shows that changing things require a changer; its stages prove God's oneness, power, and knowledge, and support resurrection after plants dry.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#3/r1.anchor: فدلت الآية لمن تدبر ونظر ببصره وقلبه، نظر من تفكر، أن المتغيرات لا بد لها من مغير

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#3/r2.claim: A palm develops from spathe to exposed bloom (also called ḍaḥk), then balah, sayāb, and jadāl before hardening, followed by busr and reddening zahw.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#3/r2.anchor: فتراه أولا طلعا ثم إغريضا إذا انشق عنه الطلع

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#3/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#3/r3.claim: Later stages include mawkit with ripening spots, mudhniba/tadhannub, thaʿda, mujazzaʿa at half ripe, ḥalqāna at two-thirds, munasbita when fully ripe, then dates.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#3/r3.anchor: فإن كان ذلك من قبل الذنب فهي مذنبة، وهو التذنوب، فإذا لانت فهي ثعدة

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#3/r4.speaker: الجوهري
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#3/r4.claim: Al-Jawhari lists several forms of yanaʿa and glosses them as ripening.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#3/r4.anchor: قال الجوهري: ينع الثمر يينع ويينع ينعا وينعا وينوعا، أي نضج

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#3/r5.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#3/r5.claim: Malik defines sale-relevant ripeness as natural sweetness without corruption or artificial treatment; Basran naqsh punctures fruit to hasten ripening and does not qualify.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#3/r5.anchor: قال مالك: الإيناع الطيب بغير فساد ولا نقش

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#3/r6.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#3/r6.claim: Malik says puncturing fruit is not the ripeness intended in the verse or condition the Prophet attached to sale; qualifying ripeness occurs naturally.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#3/r6.anchor: فليس ذلك الينع المراد في القرآن، ولا هو الذي ربط به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم البيع،

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#3/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#3/r7.claim: In cold fig-growing regions, an oil-coated stick inserted into the fig opening is a necessary local ripening method; once ripe the fruit may be sold.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#3/r7.anchor: وفي بعض بلاد التين، وهي البلاد الباردة، لا ينضج حتى يدخل في فمه عود قد دهن زيتا،

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#3/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#3/r8.claim: The natural ripeness that permits date sales, improves eating, and averts crop damage conventionally arrives when the Pleiades rise, by God's established order.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#3/r8.anchor: وهذا الينع الذي يقف عليه جواز بيع التمر وبه يطيب أكلها ويأمن من العاهة، هو عند طلوع الثريا

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#4/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#4/r1.claim: Thurayya is the Pleiades, and its morning rising is placed twelve nights into Ayyar, the month of May.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#4/r1.anchor: والثريا النجم، لا خلاف في ذلك. وطلوعها صباحا لاثنتي عشرة ليلة

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#4/r2.speaker: خارجة بن زيد بن ثابت
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#4/r2.claim: Kharija reports that Zayd ibn Thabit would not sell his land's fruit until the Pleiades rose and the yellow and red colors became clear.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#4/r2.anchor: وأخبرني خارجة بن زيد بن ثابت أن زيد بن ثابت لم يكن يبيع ثمار أرضه حتى تطلع الثريا

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#4/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#4/r3.claim: Some who exempt crop disasters from the buyer's liability relied on these reports and on prohibitions against selling fruit before ripeness or before the blight passed.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#4/r3.anchor: وقد استدل من أسقط الجوائح في الثمار بهذه الآثار، وما كان مثلها من نهيه عليه السلام عن بيع الثمرة حتى يبدو صلاحها

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#4/r4.speaker: عثمان بن سراقة
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#4/r4.claim: When Uthman ibn Suraqa asked Ibn Umar when the relevant time was, Ibn Umar answered that it was the rising of the Pleiades.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#4/r4.anchor: قال عثمان بن سراقة: فسألت ابن عمر متى هذا؟ فقال: طلوع الثريا.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#4/r5.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#4/r5.claim: Al-Shafii says the Prophetic order to remit crop disasters was not established for him; the buyer bears loss after a valid sale and possession, and if remission were adopted it should cover small and large losses. Al-Thawri and Kufans agree.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#4/r5.anchor: قال الشافعي: لم يثبت عندي أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أمر بوضع الجوائح،

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#4/r6.speaker: مالك وأكثر أهل المدينة
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#4/r6.claim: Malik and most Medinese remit crop disasters based on Jabir's report that the Prophet ordered remission; Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz judged by it, as did Ahmad and the hadith scholars.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#4/r6.anchor: وذهب مالك وأكثر أهل المدينة إلى وضعها لحديث جابر: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أمر بوضع الجوائح.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#4/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#4/r7.speaker: أهل الظاهر
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#4/r7.claim: The Zahiris apply the general wording of the report to remit disasters from the buyer in both small and large amounts.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#4/r7.anchor: وأهل الظاهر وضعوها عن المبتاع في القليل والكثير على عموم الحديث

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#4/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#4/r8.speaker: مالك وأصحابه
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#4/r8.claim: Malik and his school require a disaster to destroy at least a third of the crop; smaller loss is disregarded as incidental because every crop has minor inaccessible or spoiled portions.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#4/r8.anchor: إلا أن مالكا وأصحابه اعتبروا أن تبلغ الجائحة ثلث الثمرة فصاعدا، وما كان دون الثلث

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#4/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#4/r9.speaker: أصبغ وأشهب
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#4/r9.claim: Asbagh and Ashhab assess the crop's value rather than its quantity, remitting payment when the value lost reaches a third.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#4/r9.anchor: وكان أصبغ وأشهب لا ينظران إلى الثمرة ولكن إلى القيمة، فإذا كانت القيمة الثلث فصاعدا

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#4/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#4/r10.speaker: ابن القاسم
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#4/r10.claim: Ibn al-Qasim defines a crop disaster as damage that cannot be prevented, so theft is excluded; the books differ, with one treating theft as a disaster, a report also attributed to him that his companions and others opposed.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#4/r10.anchor: والجائحة ما لا يمكن دفعه عند ابن القاسم. وعليه فلا تكون السرقة جائحة، وكذا في كتاب محمد.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#4/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#4/r11.speaker: مطرف وابن الماجشون
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#4/r11.claim: Mutarrif and Ibn al-Majishun count heavenly rot, hail, drought, heat, or nonhuman breaking of trees as disasters; Ibn al-Qasim's report specifically counts drought.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#4/r11.anchor: وقال مطرف وابن الماجشون: ما أصاب الثمرة من السماء من عفن أو برد، أو عطش أو حر أو كسر الشجر

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#4/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#4/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#4/r12.claim: The sound position is that vegetables, like fruit, are subject to crop-disaster remission.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#4/r12.anchor: والصحيح في البقول أنها فيها جائحة كالثمرة

QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:99#5/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
