ELMALILI:6:98-99#3/r13.anchor: Arada ne büyük bir fark vardır, ve bu farkta ne mühim bir feyz-i terbiye

ELMALILI:6:98-99#3/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:98-99#3/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:98-99#3/r14.claim: The water's descent and greenery's emergence are past tense, while producing stacked grains is present or future and portrays their potential; buds and clusters are coordinated similarly.
ELMALILI:6:98-99#3/r14.anchor: Suyun inzâli, nebâtın, çimin ihrâcı فَأَخْرَجْنَا / أَنزَلَ diye mâzî sîgasıyla ifade edilmiş olduğu hâlde, habb-i müterâkibi ihraç نُّخْرِجُ diye istikbal sîgasıyla

ELMALILI:6:98-99#3/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:98-99#3/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:98-99#3/r15.claim: The tense and growth imagery also hints that Islam at the verse's Meccan revelation was like grass or a bud, while the Quran was heavenly mercy and believers' future would resemble mature gardens and fruit.
ELMALILI:6:98-99#3/r15.anchor: dîn-i İslâm’ın henüz o çim, o tomurcuk misâlinde olduğuna, Kur’ân’ın semâdan inen bir rahmet bulunduğuna ve mü’minlerin istikbâli o cennetler ve kemâle ermiş meyveler gibi olacağına bir işaret dahi edilmiştir.

ELMALILI:6:98-99#4/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:98-99#4/r1.speaker: Fahreddin Râzî
ELMALILI:6:98-99#4/r1.claim: Razi explains the order: staple grain precedes tree fruits because food comes before delicacies; date palms then precede other fruits because dates are Arab staple food and philosophers see many animal-like qualities in the palm.
ELMALILI:6:98-99#4/r1.anchor: Fahreddin Râzî der ki: “Burada evvelâ hubûbat, sonra nahl, ineb, zeytin, rummân dört nevi ağaç zikredilmiş ve zer‘, eşcâra takdim olunmuştur.

ELMALILI:6:98-99#4/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:98-99#4/r2.speaker: Aleyhissalâtü vesselâm
ELMALILI:6:98-99#4/r2.claim: The Prophet is reported to call the palm the maternal aunt of the community and say it was created from what remained of Adam's clay.
ELMALILI:6:98-99#4/r2.anchor: Aleyhissalâtü vesselâm da demiştir ki ‘Ammeniz, yani halanız nahleye ikram ediniz. Çünkü o Âdem’in tînetinin bakiyesinden halk edildi’

ELMALILI:6:98-99#4/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:98-99#4/r3.speaker: Fahreddin Râzî
ELMALILI:6:98-99#4/r3.claim: Razi calls grapes the noblest fruit and describes their usefulness from the first shoots and leaves through unripe and ripe fruit, including storage on the vine.
ELMALILI:6:98-99#4/r3.anchor: Zira üzüm envâ‘-i fevâkihin en şereflisidir.

ELMALILI:6:98-99#4/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:98-99#4/r4.speaker: Fahreddin Râzî
ELMALILI:6:98-99#4/r4.claim: Razi lists four products obtained from grapes: raisins, grape molasses, vinegar, and wine, and says their benefits would fill volumes.
ELMALILI:6:98-99#4/r4.anchor: Sonra üzümden tenavül olunacak dört nevi şey yapılır: Kuru üzüm, pekmez, sirke, şarap.

ELMALILI:6:98-99#4/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:98-99#4/r5.speaker: Fahreddin Râzî
ELMALILI:6:98-99#4/r5.claim: Although wine is forbidden by Islamic law, Razi cites the Quran's judgment that its sin outweighs its benefit.

ELMALILI:6:98-99#4/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:98-99#4/r6.speaker: Fahreddin Râzî
ELMALILI:6:98-99#4/r6.claim: Razi says grape seeds are especially valuable and that physicians prepare remedies from them for weak, damp stomachs; contemporary doctors agree when seeds are chewed and crushed.
ELMALILI:6:98-99#4/r6.anchor: tertibler[^16] yaparlar ki zayıf ve râtib mideler için pek büyük menfaatleri olur.

ELMALILI:6:98-99#4/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:98-99#4/r7.speaker: Fahreddin Râzî
ELMALILI:6:98-99#4/r7.claim: Razi concludes that grapes deserve the title “sultan of fruits.”
ELMALILI:6:98-99#4/r7.anchor: Hâsılı üzüm “sultânü’lfevâkih” ıtlâkına şâyân bir meyvedir.

ELMALILI:6:98-99#4/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:98-99#4/r8.speaker: Fahreddin Râzî
ELMALILI:6:98-99#4/r8.claim: Razi notes that olives are eaten and their oil has extensive benefits and uses in food and other matters.
ELMALILI:6:98-99#4/r8.anchor: dânesi tenâvül olunur, yağının da yemek vesâir husûsâtta ne kadar menfa‘ati azîm ve isti‘mâli kesîr olduğu mâlumdur.

ELMALILI:6:98-99#4/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:98-99#4/r9.speaker: Fahreddin Râzî
ELMALILI:6:98-99#4/r9.claim: Razi describes pomegranate as rind, membranes, seeds, and juice: its first three parts are powerfully cold, dry, dense, and astringent, while its tasty, delicate juice is nearer to balance, suits balanced constitutions, strengthens weak ones, and acts as both food and medicine.
ELMALILI:6:98-99#4/r9.anchor: ilk üçü yani kışrı, şahmı, çekirdeği bârid, yâbis, kesif, kābızdır.

ELMALILI:6:98-99#4/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:98-99#4/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:98-99#4/r10.claim: Elmalılı takes pomegranate's contrasting dense parts and delicate juice as a clear example of the verse's rule that likeness and difference coexist.
ELMALILI:6:98-99#4/r10.anchor: Yani bunda مُشْتَبِهًۭا وَغَيْرَ مُتَشَٰبِهٍ mazmûnundaki tevâfuk ve tegāyür kanununun bâriz bir misâli vardır.

ELMALILI:6:98-99#5/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:98-99#5/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:98-99#5/r1.claim: At every thing’s origin and each moment of its development, signs of God’s lordship and proofs of power and unity are evident to scholars, the learned, and all who can believe.
ELMALILI:6:98-99#5/r1.anchor: Hâsılı her şeyin gerek mebde’inde ve gerek seyr-i tekâmülünün her lahzasında hem ehl-i ilme hem ehl-i fıkh u hikmete

MAJAZ:v1p201/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p201/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p201/r4.claim: Qinw is a date cluster; qinwān serves as both dual and plural, with the dual’s nūn fixed and the plural’s nūn inflected, like ṣinw/ṣinwān.
MAJAZ:v1p201/r4.anchor: القنو هو العذق، والاثنان: قنوان، النون مكسورة، والجميع قنوان على تقدير لفظ الاثنين

MAJAZ:v1p202/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p202/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p202/r1.claim: Yanʿ is the ripening or maturity of fruit; its singular is yāniʿ and plural yanaʿ, like tājir/tujjār and ṣāḥib/ṣaḥb.
MAJAZ:v1p202/r1.anchor: وينعه إن في ذلكم» (99) ، ينعه: مصدر من ينع إذا أينع أي: من مدركه، واحده يانع والجميع ينع

MAJAZ:v1p202/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p202/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p202/r2.claim: Both yanʿat and ay̆naʿat are Arabic forms for fruit ripening, and the verse contains both; the poem’s yanʿa witnesses the usage.
MAJAZ:v1p202/r2.anchor: ويقال: قد ينعت الثمرة وأينعت لغتان، فالآية فيها اللغتان جميعا، قال: فى قباب حول دسكرة ... حولها الزيتون قد ينعا

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:99/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:99/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:99/r1.claim: The extraordinary variety of plants nourished by the same rain comes from divine power, not unconscious nature or blind chance; each manifestation is a sign for believers.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:99/r1.anchor: Aynı yağmurla sulandığı halde sayılamayacak kadar çok çeşitli cinslerde bitkiler veren yeryüzündeki tabiat hârikalarından bir demet sunulmakta

BURHAN:v2p458/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p458/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p458/r1.claim: Zarkashī sides with the majority: a بدل should add clarification absent from its base, often by mentioning a specific after a general.
BURHAN:v2p458/r1.anchor: والصحيح ما صار عليه الجمهور لان باب البدل ان يكون في الثاني بيان ليس في الآول بأن يذكر الخاص بعد العام مبينا وموضحا

BURHAN:v2p458/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p458/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p458/r2.claim: Partitive بدل normally requires a pronoun referring back to the whole; the Qur'anic example from حج البيت omits it because another verse makes the referent clear.
BURHAN:v2p458/r2.anchor: وقد يحذف لدليل كقوله ﴿ ولله على الناس حج البيت من استطاع ﴾ منهم وهو مراد بدليل ظهوره في الآية الأخرى

BURHAN:v2p458/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p458/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p458/r3.claim: بدل can transfer the predicate from its base to a related element, as in the people being described through most of them and Zayd through his garment.
BURHAN:v2p458/r3.anchor: وقد يأتي البدل لنقل الحكم عن مبدله نحو جاء القوم أكثرهم واعجبني زيد ثوبه

BURHAN:v2p458/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p458/r4.speaker: ابن عصفور
BURHAN:v2p458/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAṣfūr rejects غلمانه as a valid example of this construction.
BURHAN:v2p458/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عصفور ولا يصح غلمانه

BURHAN:v2p458/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p458/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p458/r6.claim: بدل is like repeating its governor and can represent two clauses; repeated prepositions demonstrate this, unlike an adjective construction.
BURHAN:v2p458/r6.anchor: والبدل في تقدير تكرير العامل وليس كالصفة ولكنه في تقدير جملتين بدليل تكرير حرف الجر

BURHAN:v2p458/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p458/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p458/r7.claim: In 6:99, طلعها is a بدل اشتمال of النخل, with من repeated as its governor.

NAHHAS:v2p85/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p85/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p85/r5.claim: The older form of māʾ is māh; its weak final hāʾ and alif gave way to hamza, a stronger letter.
NAHHAS:v2p85/r5.anchor: والأصل في ماء ماه والهاء خفية والألف كذلك فأبدل من الهاء همزة لأن الهمزة جلدة

NAHHAS:v2p85/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p85/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p85/r6.claim: Nabāt kulli shayʾ means the growth of everything that grows.

NAHHAS:v2p85/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p85/r7.speaker: الأخفش
NAHHAS:v2p85/r7.claim: Al-Akhfash glosses khaḍiran as akhḍar, green, citing the Arab expression “show me a speckled one and I will show it rainy.”
NAHHAS:v2p85/r7.anchor: قال الأخفش أي أخضر كما يقول العرب أرنيها نمرة أركها مطرة

NAHHAS:v2p85/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p85/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p85/r8.claim: Qinwān is nominative as a subject; al-Farrāʾ allows non-Qurʾanic qinwānan coordinated with the preceding object.
NAHHAS:v2p85/r8.anchor: ( ومن النخل من طلعها قنوان دانية ) رفع بالابتداء وأجاز الفراء في غير القرآن قنوانا دانية

NAHHAS:v2p85/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p85/r9.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v2p85/r9.claim: Al-Farrāʾ records dialects: Qays and the Ḥijāz say qinwān, Tamīm says qinyān, while the singular is qinw.
NAHHAS:v2p85/r9.anchor: قال الفراء هذه لغة قيس وأهل الحجاز يقولون قنوان وتميم تقول قنيان ثم يجتمعون في الواحد فيقولون قنو

NAHHAS:v2p85/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p85/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p85/r10.claim: The common reading has accusative janāt coordinated as an object; Ibn Abī Laylā and al-Aʿmash, also the sound reading of ʿĀṣim, have nominative. Abū ʿUbayd and Abū Ḥātim reject it, but al-Naḥḥās accepts it as a new subject with omitted “for them,” supported by major grammarians and parallel readings; the cited verse illustrates such coordination.
NAHHAS:v2p85/r10.anchor: قراءة العامة بالنصب عطفا أي فأخرجنا جنات وقرأ محمد بن عبد الرحمن بن أبي ليلى والأعمش

NAHHAS:v2p85/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p85/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p85/r11.claim: The nominative reading is not coordinated with the palms; it is an independent subject with an omitted predicate, “and for them are gardens.” Sībawayh, al-Kisāʾī, and al-Farrāʾ permit this, as in ḥūr ʿīn; poetry also illustrates the construction.
NAHHAS:v2p85/r11.anchor: رفع بالابتداء والخبر محذوف أي ولهم جنات كما قرأ جماعة من القراء ( وحور عين ) وأجاز مثل هذا

NAHHAS:v2p85/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p85/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p85/r12.claim: Al-zaytūn and al-rummān can only be accusative, by consensus.
NAHHAS:v2p85/r12.anchor: فأما ( والزيتون والرمان ) فليس فيه إلا النصب للإجماع على ذلك

NAHHAS:v2p85/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p85/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p85/r13.claim: Abū ʿAmr and Medinan readers read thamar as the plural of thamara; Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī read thumur, a plural of thimār. It may also mean fruitful property.
NAHHAS:v2p85/r13.anchor: قراءة أبي عمرو وأهل المدينة جمع ثمرة وقراءة يحيى بن وثاب وحمزة والكسائي ( إلى ثمره )

NAHHAS:v2p85/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p85/r14.speaker: الأعمش
NAHHAS:v2p85/r14.claim: Al-Aʿmash is also reported to read thamar with ḍamma on thāʾ and a still mīm; the heavy ḍamma may be dropped, or the form may be a plural like badana/badan.
NAHHAS:v2p85/r14.anchor: وروي عن الأعمش ( إلى ثمره ) بضم الثاء وإسكان الميم حذفت الضمة لثقلها

NAHHAS:v2p85/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p85/r15.speaker: ابن محمد بن السميفع اليماني
NAHHAS:v2p85/r15.claim: Ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Sumayfa al-Yamānī reads yāniʿihi, “and its ripening/maturity.”
NAHHAS:v2p85/r15.anchor: وقرأ ابن محمد بن السميفع اليماني ( ويانعه ) أي ومدركه

NAHHAS:v2p85/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p85/r16.speaker: ابن محيصن وابن أبي إسحاق
NAHHAS:v2p85/r16.claim: Ibn Muḥayṣin and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read yunʿihi with ḍamma on yāʾ; al-Farrāʾ calls this a dialect of some Najd tribes.
NAHHAS:v2p85/r16.anchor: وقرأ ابن محيصن وابن أبي إسحاق ( وينعه ) بضم الياء قال الفراء الضم لغة بعض أهل نجد

ITQAN:v2p348/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p348/r4.speaker: unknown
ITQAN:v2p348/r4.claim: The response glosses the fruit’s ripening and yielding as maturity and full development, and cites a poetic comparison with fresh vegetation.
ITQAN:v2p348/r4.anchor: قال أخبرني عن قوله ﴿ إذا أثمر وينعه ﴾ قال نضجه وبلاغه

ITQAN:v3p218#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p218#2/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p218#2/r5.claim: Other imperative functions include bringing something into being, recalling blessing, challenging a false claim, consultation, reflection, and amazement; al-Sakkaki treats the last as performative used for report.
ITQAN:v3p218#2/r5.anchor: والتكوين وهو أعم من التسخير نحو ﴿ كن فيكون ﴾

ITQAN:v3p272/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p272/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p272/r6.claim: The account of abundant provision, crops, and fruits ends “for people who believe,” since recognizing these blessings should lead to faith and gratitude.
ITQAN:v3p272/r6.anchor: ولما ذكر ما أنعم به على عباده من سعة الأرزاق والأقوات والثمار وأنواع ذلك ناسب ختمه بالإيمان

ITQAN:v2p310/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p310/r15.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p310/r15.claim: Qinwān dāniya means short palm clusters whose roots cling close to the earth.
ITQAN:v2p310/r15.anchor: 1611 ﴿ قنوان دانية ﴾ قصار النخل اللاصقة عروقها بالأرض

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p546/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p546/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p546/r5.claim: Aqna is unique in form and root in the Qur'an; the related w-root appears in qinwan in 6:99.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p546/r5.anchor: وحيدة في القرآن، صيغة ومادة. ومن الواوى جاءت {قِنْوَانٌ} في آية الأنعام 99

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p546/r8.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p546/r8.speaker: أبو موسى والزمخشري
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p546/r8.claim: For the hadith forbidding slaughter of qini sheep, Abu Musa says they are kept for milk and offspring; al-Zamakhshari defines qinya as livestock kept as property.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p546/r8.anchor: هي التي تُقتنى للدَّارَّ والولد، واحدتها قنوة، بالضم والكسر، وقنية بالياء
